道承于下君君臣臣而世道隆矣吁叙先後之
倫而與可悖秩上下之分而禮可廣春秋非聖
人莫能脩豈游夏所能贊歟惟此義不明後世
===
有使男事女夫屈於婦以貽牝鳴麀聚之禍者
班位莫定上下陵替至猶上梗弁髦之視者天
經隳矣地維裂矣人紀壞矣悲夫
晉侯使韓穿來言汶陽之田歸之于齊〔成〕
〔公八年〕公會晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯鄭伯曹伯
莒子杞伯同盟于蒲〔成公九年〕叔孫如晉〔昭〕
〔公八年〕公會劉子晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯鄭伯
曹伯莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾子于
平丘〔昭公十三年〕
punctuated:
一，視大君有開，然實天王之貳、天下之本也。爵方宗少海之流，四表仰前星之照。其君道之常尊，與三公宰臣之任，有進退之節，有均勞之義，豈同哉？昔帝堯授命，必先元后；皐陶賡歌，必先元首。周未嘗混稱也。經於王世子，必書及以會，蓋殊詞以正大分焉。此義行，則乾道運于上，坤道承于下，君君臣臣，而世道隆矣。吁！叙先後之倫，而與可悖？秩上下之分，而禮可廣？春秋非聖人莫能脩，豈游夏所能贊歟？惟此義不明，後世有使男事女、夫屈於婦，以貽牝鳴麀聚之禍者；班位莫定，上下陵替，至猶上梗弁髦之視者。天經隳矣，地維裂矣，人紀壞矣。悲夫！
晉侯使韓穿來言汶陽之田歸之于齊〔成〕〔公八年〕。公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、杞伯，同盟于蒲〔成公九年〕。叔孫如晉〔昭〕〔公八年〕。公會劉子、晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子于平丘〔昭公十三年〕。
translation_en:
…united. He was regarded as a great ruler opening a new order [?], yet he was in fact the deputy of the Son of Heaven and the foundation of all under Heaven. The ranks turn toward the streams of the Lesser Sea [?], and the four distant quarters look up to the radiance of the Foremost Star—images of the royal heir. His enduring eminence as a ruler—how could it be the same as the responsibilities of the Three Dukes and chief ministers, who are subject to rules governing advancement and withdrawal and to the duty of sharing the burden of service? In antiquity, when Emperor Yao issued his charge, he necessarily put the sovereign first; when Gao Yao continued the song, he necessarily put the head of state first. Zhou never referred to these indiscriminately [?]. When the Classic speaks of the royal heir apparent, it invariably writes “and” in recording the meeting, using distinct wording to rectify the great distinctions of status. When this principle prevails, the Way of Heaven moves above and the Way of Earth obediently supports it below; rulers act as rulers and ministers as ministers, and the order of the world flourishes.

Ah! Once the proper sequence of relationships has been set forth, can it be contravened [?]? Once the distinctions between higher and lower have been ordered, can ritual propriety be stretched [?]? None but a sage could compile the Spring and Autumn Annals: could even Ziyou and Zixia have assisted in it? Yet because this principle was not understood, later ages saw men made to serve women and husbands subjected to wives, bringing the calamities of hens crowing and deer mating indiscriminately. Ranks and positions were unsettled; those below encroached upon those above, and those above lost their authority. Matters reached the point of treating superiors as obstructions or as discarded ceremonial caps and forelocks [?]. Heaven’s enduring norms were overthrown, Earth’s supporting bonds were torn apart, and human relationships were ruined. How lamentable!

The Marquis of Jin sent Han Chuan to come and say that the lands of Wenyang should be returned to Qi. 〔Eighth year of Duke Cheng.〕 The duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, and the Earl of Qi; together they entered into a covenant at Pu. 〔Ninth year of Duke Cheng.〕 Shusun went to Jin. 〔Eighth year of Duke Zhao.〕 The duke met the Viscount of Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Lesser Zhu at Pingqiu. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhao.〕

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
陳情
同考試官教諭李　批〔旨遠詞文必非稚筆可到〕
考試官主事袁　批〔文有軌度錄此爲浮夸者式〕
考試官主事蕭　批〔融會傳意文采爛然〕
春秋旣譏失信咎貳者徒要以盟復譏崇侈啓
貳者徒示以威此汶陽之田厖祁之宮皆叛之
招也而蒲之盟平丘之會適增其叛耳晉至景
昭何以伯諸侯哉且汶陽固魯之故田也晉初
下令而反之韓穿來言俾魯成以獻焉噫誠者
=
動物之基信者感人之本無輗無軏易食易生
明訓何如也予奪之易發命不衷授受之私食
言罔顧無感于諸侯之解體也柰何黷信以要
蒲之盟邪申蠡牢之約尋馬陵之歃不知固結
之本徒事詛盟之末何益哉夫信在言前不言
而自喻誠在令外不令而自行景之所爲若是
世業何由振哉經於韓穿歸田之後特書同盟
于蒲蓋深罪之若厖祁非晉之故宮也昭方創
制而落之叔弓徃使偕諸侯以賀焉噫儉維德
punctuated:
陳情

同考試官教諭李　批〔旨遠詞文，必非稚筆可到。〕
考試官主事袁　批〔文有軌度，錄此爲浮夸者式。〕
考試官主事蕭　批〔融會傳意，文采爛然。〕

春秋旣譏失信，咎貳者徒要以盟，復譏崇侈，啓貳者徒示以威。此汶陽之田、厖祁之宮，皆叛之招也，而蒲之盟、平丘之會，適增其叛耳。晉至景、昭，何以伯諸侯哉？且汶陽固魯之故田也，晉初下令而反之，韓穿來言，俾魯成以獻焉。噫！誠者動物之基，信者感人之本。無輗無軏，易食易生，明訓何如也？予奪之易，發命不衷；授受之私，食言罔顧。無感于諸侯之解體也，柰何黷信以要蒲之盟邪？申蠡牢之約，尋馬陵之歃，不知固結之本，徒事詛盟之末，何益哉？夫信在言前，不言而自喻；誠在令外，不令而自行。景之所爲若是，世業何由振哉？經於韓穿歸田之後，特書同盟于蒲，蓋深罪之。若厖祁非晉之故宮也，昭方創制而落之，叔弓徃使，偕諸侯以賀焉。噫！儉維德
translation_en:
Chen Qing

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning is far-reaching and the language elegant: surely beyond the capacity of an immature writer.〕
Examiner Yuan, Secretary, comments: 〔The composition observes proper standards. It is included as a model for those given to extravagant rhetoric.〕
Examiner Xiao, Secretary, comments: 〔It integrates and conveys the meaning of the commentaries, with splendid literary expression.〕

The Spring and Autumn Annals censures breaches of trust: those who blamed others for wavering allegiance merely sought to bind them by covenants. It also censures the promotion of extravagance: those who provoked wavering allegiance merely sought to overawe others with force. The lands of Wenyang and the palace at Pangqi both invited rebellion; the covenant at Pu and the assembly at Pingqiu only increased it. When Jin came to the reigns of Dukes Jing and Zhao, how could it exercise hegemony over the feudal lords?

Now Wenyang was indeed land formerly belonging to Lu. Jin initially ordered its return, but Han Chuan then came with instructions that Duke Cheng of Lu should surrender it [to Qi]. Alas! Sincerity is the foundation for moving other beings, and trustworthiness the basis for influencing people. A cart without its yoke-pin or a carriage without its cross-pin; changing food and changing life [?]—how clear are these teachings! So readily giving and taking away, issuing commands without fairness; privately arranging transfers, breaking one's word without a thought: did they not perceive that the feudal lords were falling away? Why, then, profane good faith by exacting the covenant at Pu? Reaffirming the agreement at Lilao [?] and renewing the blood-oath at Maling, they did not understand the foundation of lasting unity, but attended only to the superficial business of imprecations and covenants. What benefit could this bring?

Trustworthiness precedes words: without speaking, one is understood. Sincerity extends beyond commands: without issuing orders, one's purposes are carried out. With Duke Jing acting in this way, how could the achievement inherited from his predecessors be revived? After recording Han Chuan's return of the lands, the Classic expressly records that they entered into a joint covenant at Pu, thereby condemning him severely.

As for Pangqi, it was not an old palace of Jin. Duke Zhao had newly built it and was inaugurating it; Shu Gong went as an envoy to offer congratulations together with the feudal lords. Alas! Frugality is virtue's …

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
之共後維惡之大清廟茅屋峻宇雕墻明徵何
如也仁賢政事弗慮弗諶宮室臺榭是崇是飾
無怪乎諸侯之貳心也柰何不威以徵平丘之
會邪既治辛未之兵復建壬申之旆無忠信誠
慤之心肆恫疑恐喝之術何爲哉夫德日新萬
邦惟懷志自滿九族乃離昭之所爲若是世業
其浸微矣經於叔弓如晉之下直書會于平丘
蓋深惡之屬比而觀則知服人之道貴信不貴
盟以德不以威可以爲求鑒矣大抵天下莫大
===
於理莫強於信義而盟誓不足恃詐力非所先
也子曰大道之行三代之英丘未之逮焉其所
感也深矣春秋時猶有如齊桓者衣裳不歃血
兵車無大戰一匡之業其在玆乎晉亦有之五
會之信推誠而鄭不復叛三駕之兵善陣而楚
不能爭悼其有君子之資歟然由管仲知鑒佐
之也故曰得人者興能自得師者王君人者宜
鑒于斯
禮記
punctuated:
之共，後維惡之大。清廟茅屋，峻宇雕墻，明徵何如也？仁賢政事弗慮弗諶，宮室臺榭是崇是飾，無怪乎諸侯之貳心也。柰何不威以徵平丘之會邪？既治辛未之兵，復建壬申之旆，無忠信誠慤之心，肆恫疑恐喝之術，何爲哉？夫德日新，萬邦惟懷；志自滿，九族乃離。昭之所爲若是，世業其浸微矣。經於叔弓如晉之下，直書會于平丘，蓋深惡之。屬比而觀，則知服人之道，貴信不貴盟，以德不以威，可以爲求鑒矣。大抵天下莫大於理，莫強於信義，而盟誓不足恃，詐力非所先也。子曰：「大道之行，三代之英，丘未之逮焉。」其所感也深矣！春秋時，猶有如齊桓者，衣裳不歃血，兵車無大戰，一匡之業，其在玆乎？晉亦有之，五會之信，推誠而鄭不復叛；三駕之兵，善陣而楚不能爭。悼其有君子之資歟？然由管仲、知鑒佐之也。故曰：「得人者興，能自得師者王。」君人者宜鑒于斯。

禮記
translation_en:
…the foundation of virtue, while extravagance [?; the transcription reads 後] is the greatest of evils. The pure ancestral temple with its thatched roof, and lofty buildings with carved walls—how clear are the lessons they furnish! He neither considered nor trusted the humane and worthy or their conduct of government, but exalted and embellished palaces, terraces, and pavilions. No wonder the feudal lords became divided in their allegiance. Why, then, did he resort to intimidation [?] to summon them to the meeting at Pingqiu? Having arrayed his troops on the xinwei day, he again raised his banners on the renshen day. Without a heart of loyalty, trustworthiness, sincerity, and honesty, he freely employed techniques of intimidation, unsettling suspicions, and threats. What purpose could this serve? When virtue is renewed daily, the myriad states cherish their ruler; when his ambitions are self-satisfied, even the nine degrees of kinship become estranged. With Duke Zhao acting thus, his inherited dominion was bound gradually to decline. After recording Shugong’s journey to Jin, the Classic directly records the meeting at Pingqiu, expressing profound condemnation. Reading these entries together, we learn that the way to secure people’s submission values trustworthiness over covenants and employs virtue rather than intimidation. Here one may seek a lesson.

In general, nothing under Heaven is greater than principle, and nothing stronger than trustworthiness and righteousness. Oaths and covenants cannot be relied upon, nor should deceit and force take precedence. The Master said: “The practice of the Great Way and the outstanding men of the Three Dynasties—I, Qiu, did not live to see them.” How profound was the feeling behind his words! Even in the Spring and Autumn period, there were still men like Duke Huan of Qi: at meetings in ceremonial robes, no blood covenant was sworn; in expeditions with war chariots, no great battle was fought. Was this not the basis of his achievement in setting the realm right? Jin, too, had such a ruler. Through the trust established at five meetings, he extended his sincerity, and Zheng no longer rebelled; through the forces of three campaigns, he deployed his troops so well that Chu could not contend with him. Did Duke Dao not possess the qualities of a gentleman? Yet these achievements depended on the assistance of Guan Zhong and Zhi Jian [?], respectively. Thus it is said: “Those who obtain worthy men flourish; those who can obtain teachers for themselves become kings.” Those who rule others should take their lesson from this.

Book of Rites

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
毋不敬儼若思安定辭安民哉
許制
同考試官訓導梁　批〔上述禮經安民之道以□□□〕
考試官主事袁　批〔以敬字立說□□□□〕
考試官主事蕭　批〔意足辭暢非苟作者〕
記禮者詳君子脩己以敬而嘆其效之大也甚
矣敬者脩身之要也而其效足以安民然則敬
者君子之所以成己成物者乎此在禮經之言
也想其意謂敬德之聚也政之本也君子務焉
===
主一無適而禁止乎非僻之干莊敬日強而絕
去夫慢易之失閑邪以存誠也克己以復禮也
而身心一於敬矣容色不端非敬也君子則儼
威儼恪顒然丰範之端凝若有所思而不敢肆
者貌之肅者心之敬也言辭不審非敬也必安
舒詳緩秩乎德音之簡易若有所防而不敢出
者言之定者心之敬也若是則脩身之要盡而
出政之本立矣吾見篤恭不顯自足以神觀感
之機瞻其顏色而民弗敢爭也恭己無爲自有
punctuated:
毋不敬，儼若思，安定辭，安民哉！
許制
同考試官訓導梁，批〔上述禮經安民之道以□□□〕
考試官主事袁，批〔以敬字立說□□□□〕
考試官主事蕭，批〔意足辭暢，非苟作者。〕
記禮者詳君子脩己以敬，而嘆其效之大也。甚矣，敬者脩身之要也，而其效足以安民！然則敬者，君子之所以成己成物者乎？此在禮經之言也，想其意謂：敬，德之聚也，政之本也，君子務焉。主一無適，而禁止乎非僻之干；莊敬日強，而絕去夫慢易之失。閑邪以存誠也，克己以復禮也，而身心一於敬矣。容色不端，非敬也。君子則儼威儼恪，顒然丰範之端凝，若有所思而不敢肆者，貌之肅者，心之敬也。言辭不審，非敬也。必安舒詳緩，秩乎德音之簡易，若有所防而不敢出者，言之定者，心之敬也。若是，則脩身之要盡，而出政之本立矣。吾見篤恭不顯，自足以神觀感之機，瞻其顏色而民弗敢爭也；恭己無爲，自有
translation_en:
“Be reverent in all things; maintain a grave bearing, as though in thought; speak calmly and deliberately. How this brings peace to the people!”
Xu Zhi
Associate Examiner Liang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The foregoing sets out the way of bringing peace to the people in the ritual classic, by means of … [?]〕
Examiner Yuan, Secretary, comments: 〔Develops the argument around the word ‘reverence’ … [?]〕
Examiner Xiao, Secretary, comments: 〔The ideas are fully expressed and the language flows freely; this is no carelessly composed work.〕
The recorder of the rites elaborates upon the gentleman’s cultivation of himself through reverence and marvels at the greatness of its effects. How profound this is! Reverence is the essential means of cultivating oneself, and its effects suffice to bring peace to the people. Is reverence, then, the means by which the gentleman perfects himself and other beings? Such is the statement in the ritual classic. We may suppose its meaning to be this: reverence is where virtue gathers and the foundation of government; the gentleman devotes himself to it.
He concentrates on the one without turning elsewhere, preventing the intrusion of what is wrong and perverse. Through solemn reverence he grows stronger each day, wholly eliminating the faults of arrogance and carelessness. He guards against evil to preserve sincerity and overcomes the self to return to ritual propriety. Thus body and mind are united in reverence. An improper bearing or expression is not reverence. The gentleman therefore maintains solemn dignity and scrupulous respect, his imposing deportment upright and composed, as though occupied in thought and not daring to indulge himself. The gravity of his appearance is the reverence of his heart. Incautious speech is not reverence. His speech must be calm, unhurried, considered, and measured; his virtuous words must be orderly, simple, and straightforward, as though he were guarding against something and dared not let it escape his lips. The steadiness of his speech is the reverence of his heart.
In this way, the essentials of self-cultivation are fully realized, and the foundation for conducting government is established. I see that his profound reverence, without outward display, is itself sufficient to give wondrous efficacy to the process by which people observe him and are moved: gazing upon his countenance, the people dare not contend. Maintaining a reverent bearing and governing without action, he naturally has …

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
以妙儀刑之化望其容貌而民弗敢慢也上者
下之倡也建其有極則所以神道設教者不出
乎反身自治之中四海其升猷矣君者民之表
也慎厥身脩則所以奠麗陳教者不出乎脩己
以敬之內兆民其敏德矣故曰安民哉者信乎
無一人之不得其所而上下一於恭敬矣脩身
之效大矣哉記禮者首以爲言其示人主敬之
意切矣嗟乎古昔帝王之所以彌綸參贊孰有
不本於敬者哉如堯之欽舜之恭禹之祗德湯
===
之懋昭文之敬止武之敬勝皆是物也故曰經
禮三百曲禮三千一言以蔽之曰毋不敬
人生而靜天之性也感於物而動性之欲
也
同考試官訓導梁　批　〔此題非深於性與天道者　不能言是作其庶乎〕
高拱
考試官主事袁　批　〔有原委有開闔而辭亦精瑩　可與言性情之妙矣〕
punctuated:
以妙儀刑之化，望其容貌而民弗敢慢也。上者，下之倡也；建其有極，則所以神道設教者，不出乎反身自治之中，四海其升猷矣。君者，民之表也；慎厥身脩，則所以奠麗陳教者，不出乎脩己以敬之內，兆民其敏德矣。故曰「安民哉」者，信乎無一人之不得其所，而上下一於恭敬矣。脩身之效大矣哉！記禮者首以爲言，其示人主敬之意切矣。嗟乎！古昔帝王之所以彌綸參贊，孰有不本於敬者哉？如堯之欽、舜之恭、禹之祗德、湯之懋昭、文之敬止、武之敬勝，皆是物也。故曰：「經禮三百，曲禮三千，一言以蔽之，曰毋不敬。」

人生而靜，天之性也；感於物而動，性之欲也。

同考試官訓導梁，批：〔此題非深於性與天道者不能言，是作其庶乎！〕

高拱

考試官主事袁，批：〔有原委，有開闔，而辭亦精瑩，可與言性情之妙矣。〕
translation_en:
… thereby bringing about the subtle transforming influence of an exemplary model: beholding his countenance, the people dare not be disrespectful. Those above lead those below. When the ruler establishes the highest standard, his means of instituting instruction through the numinous Way lie entirely within turning back upon himself and governing himself; all within the Four Seas will advance along the Way. The ruler is the people's model. When he attends carefully to cultivating himself, his means of settling the people and setting forth instruction lie entirely within cultivating himself through reverence; the myriad people will apply themselves diligently to virtue. Thus the words “bring peace to the people” mean that truly not a single person fails to find their proper place, while those above and below are united in respectful reverence. Great indeed are the effects of self-cultivation! The recorder of the rites placed this teaching first: how earnest was his intention to show people that they should make reverence their guiding principle!

Ah! Among the emperors and kings of antiquity, whose work of ordering all things and assisting the transforming processes of Heaven and Earth was not rooted in reverence? Yao's respectful attentiveness, Shun's deference, Yu's reverent virtue, Tang's diligent manifestation of virtue, King Wen's abiding in reverence, and King Wu's overcoming through reverence—all are this same thing. Thus it is said: “The three hundred principal rites and the three thousand detailed observances can be summed up in a single phrase: Be reverent in everything.”

“Human beings are still at birth: this is the nature bestowed by Heaven. When affected by things, they become active: these are the desires of that nature.”

Associate Examiner Liang, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Only someone with a profound understanding of human nature and the Way of Heaven can discuss this topic. This composition comes close to that standard!〕

Gao Gong

Examiner Yuan, Secretary, comments: 〔It traces origins and developments, and knows when to expand and when to draw together; its language, too, is refined and lucid. With this writer one may discuss the subtleties of human nature and the emotions.〕

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官主事蕭　批〔文有機軸蓋嘗用心於性學者〕
論人心之寂感而有性情之分焉夫心統性情者也未發者爲性而已發者爲情先王之所以
制作禮樂者蓋原於此矣且夫合虛與氣有性之名合性與知覺有心之名而心也者則統乎
性情者也是故有靜之時焉有動之時焉自其
靜者觀之人之生也寂然不動無感無形而湛
一之常存退藏於密何思何慮而真純之內蘊
非惟人心之知覺不可得見而道心亦不可得
===
而窺矣若是者何以爲天之性耶蓋有是形即
有是性而性者天之所命也吾知真精凝於妙
合而純粹至善者實帝降之衷太極具於化醇
而有物有則者一民稟之懿敦化爲川流之本
也黃中極通理之妙也性之體本若是其靜耳
故曰人生而靜者天之性也自其動者觀之物
之感也由中應外而五性出焉于以達思通之
用事至物來而七情生焉于以神妙應之機非
惟道心之知覺於是乎生而人心亦胥此焉出
punctuated:
考試官主事蕭，批〔文有機軸，蓋嘗用心於性學者。〕

論人心之寂感，而有性情之分焉。夫心統性情者也，未發者爲性，而已發者爲情。先王之所以制作禮樂者，蓋原於此矣。且夫合虛與氣，有性之名；合性與知覺，有心之名。而心也者，則統乎性情者也。是故有靜之時焉，有動之時焉。自其靜者觀之，人之生也，寂然不動，無感無形，而湛一之常存；退藏於密，何思何慮，而真純之內蘊。非惟人心之知覺不可得見，而道心亦不可得而窺矣。若是者，何以爲天之性耶？蓋有是形，即有是性，而性者天之所命也。吾知真精凝於妙合，而純粹至善者，實帝降之衷；太極具於化醇，而有物有則者，一民稟之懿。敦化爲川流之本也，黃中極通理之妙也，性之體本若是其靜耳。故曰：「人生而靜者，天之性也。」自其動者觀之，物之感也，由中應外，而五性出焉，于以達思通之用；事至物來，而七情生焉，于以神妙應之機。非惟道心之知覺於是乎生，而人心亦胥此焉出
translation_en:
Examiner Xiao, Secretary, comments: 〔The composition has an organizing conception; its author has evidently devoted thought to the study of human nature.〕

In discussing the stillness and responsiveness of the human mind, we distinguish between nature and feelings. The mind encompasses both nature and feelings: what has not yet been aroused is nature, while what has already been aroused is feeling. This, indeed, is the basis upon which the former kings instituted rites and music. The conjunction of the void and vital energy is called nature; the conjunction of nature and awareness is called mind. The mind thus encompasses nature and feelings. Accordingly, it has times of stillness and times of activity.

Viewed in its stillness, the mind at a person’s birth is quiescent and unmoving, without stimulus or manifest form, while its clear unity constantly abides. It withdraws into hidden depths, without thought or deliberation, while its genuineness and purity remain stored within. Not only is the awareness of the human mind imperceptible; even the moral mind cannot be glimpsed. Why is this called the nature bestowed by Heaven? Wherever there is this bodily form, there is this nature, and nature is what Heaven ordains. I know that true essence congeals in a wondrous union, and that what is pure and supremely good is truly the inner norm bestowed by the Lord on High. The Supreme Ultimate is fully present in the rich interaction of transformative forces, and the fact that things exist with their inherent principles is the excellence uniformly endowed upon the people. The profundity of transformation is the source of its flowing forth like rivers; the yellow center brings to perfection the subtlety of comprehending principle. The substance of nature is originally just this still. Thus it is said: “That human beings are still at birth is their Heaven-bestowed nature.”

Viewed in its activity, when external things exert their influence, the mind responds from within to what is outside, and the five aspects of nature emerge, thereby realizing the function of thought that penetrates and comprehends. As affairs arise and things approach, the seven feelings are generated, thereby giving wondrous efficacy to the workings of subtle response. Not only does the awareness of the moral mind arise here; the human mind likewise emerges from this …

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
矣若是者何以為性之欲邪蓋有是性即有是
情而情者性之所發也吾知形生神發而耆欲
之將至一出乎良能知誘物化而情偽之相感
漸流于人欲攻取釁其端也好惡決其幾也性
之欲不能以不動耳故曰感於物而動者性之
欲也是則心一也動靜分而性情著先王之所
以制作禮樂者亦惟節民之情以復其性焉耳
樂記君子其有以達性情之妙而窺禮樂之本
乎大抵人有性情而情之所感每失之動故惟
===
聖人為能主靜以制乎動先儒所謂情順萬事
而無情者非主靜何以能之學者未至乎是其
亦於靜存動察之功加之意焉爾
第貳場
論
古之學者為己
同考試官教諭林　批　諸作多剽竊陳言冗雜可
陳炟
厭此論意議亦層疊而獨能約束筆勢千鈞末盜呂中
punctuated:
矣。若是者，何以為性之欲邪？蓋有是性，即有是情，而情者，性之所發也。吾知形生神發，而耆欲之將至，一出乎良能；知誘物化，而情偽之相感，漸流于人欲。攻取釁其端也，好惡決其幾也，性之欲不能以不動耳。故曰：「感於物而動者，性之欲也。」是則心一也，動靜分而性情著。先王之所以制作禮樂者，亦惟節民之情以復其性焉耳。樂記君子，其有以達性情之妙而窺禮樂之本乎？大抵人有性情，而情之所感，每失之動，故惟聖人為能主靜以制乎動。先儒所謂「情順萬事而無情」者，非主靜何以能之？學者未至乎是，其亦於靜存動察之功加之意焉爾。

第貳場

論

古之學者為己

同考試官教諭林，批：「諸作多剽竊陳言，冗雜可

陳炟

厭。此論意議亦層疊，而獨能約束，筆勢千鈞。末盜呂中
translation_en:
… Why should such manifestations be called the desires of human nature? Wherever there is this nature, there are these feelings; feelings are what issue from nature. I understand that, as the bodily form comes into being and the spirit develops, the appetites and desires about to arise all proceed from innate capacity. When awareness is enticed and transformed by external things, however, genuine and artificial feelings affect one another and gradually flow into selfish human desires. Aggressive acquisition opens the breach, and likes and dislikes determine the incipient tendency: the desires of human nature cannot but become active. Thus it is said: “Being stimulated by things and becoming active is the desire of human nature.”

The mind, then, is one; as activity and stillness become differentiated, nature and feelings become manifest. The former kings instituted rites and music solely to regulate the people’s feelings and thereby restore their nature. Did not the gentleman who composed the Record of Music grasp the subtle workings of nature and feelings and discern the foundation of rites and music? Generally speaking, people possess nature and feelings, but when their feelings are stimulated, they repeatedly go astray through activity. Only the sage can therefore make stillness his governing principle and thereby control activity. An earlier Confucian spoke of “feelings responding appropriately to the myriad affairs, yet remaining without feelings.” Without making stillness the governing principle, how could one achieve this? Those who study but have not yet attained this state should devote their attention to preserving the mind in stillness and examining it in activity.

Second Session

Discourse

“Those Who Studied in Antiquity Did So for Their Own Sake”

Chen Da 陳炟

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: “Most of the compositions plagiarize stock expressions and are tediously diffuse and miscellaneous. This discourse, too, piles up its ideas and arguments, yet it alone succeeds in keeping them under control; its writing has the force of a thousand jun. At the end, [the transcription is unclear: ‘盜呂中’] [?] …”

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
庸下學之功尤見親切非素養深厚詎不及此
同考試官教諭鄧　批　微詞奥義中斐然成章中
州俊才如吾子者豈可多得
同考試官學正梁　批　心外無道道外無學學之
不明由其心之蔽也此作只予古人立心專一處言而
末學紕雜之弊自在言外且文辭端雅未嘗用一隱僻
語有氣可以占吾子之心之學矣
考試官主事袁　批　剗點浮辭三覆不厭
考試官主事蕭　批　析理精明曲中程度可與共
學矣
===
古人之實學始諸其立心而已矣何也學以致
道者也而學之成與不成則惟其立心何如耳
心乎爲己則所學者實實則一一則道斯致而
已成矣取諸至近而萬物備歛之至密而功化
全而古人之學可識也否則二交而異異紛而
支支流而僞僞極而亡兹固所謂令之爲人者
而可與語古人之學也哉故求盡古人之道者
自其學始求盡古人之學者自其心始古之學
punctuated:
庸下學之功，尤見親切，非素養深厚，詎不及此？
同考試官教諭鄧批：微詞奥義中，斐然成章。中州俊才如吾子者，豈可多得？
同考試官學正梁批：心外無道，道外無學。學之不明，由其心之蔽也。此作只予古人立心專一處言，而末學紕雜之弊自在言外。且文辭端雅，未嘗用一隱僻語，有氣，可以占吾子之心之學矣。
考試官主事袁批：剗點浮辭，三覆不厭。
考試官主事蕭批：析理精明，曲中程度，可與共學矣。
古人之實學，始諸其立心而已矣。何也？學以致道者也，而學之成與不成，則惟其立心何如耳。心乎爲己，則所學者實；實則一，一則道斯致，而已成矣。取諸至近而萬物備，歛之至密而功化全，而古人之學可識也。否則二，交而異，異紛而支，支流而僞，僞極而亡。兹固所謂令之爲人者，而可與語古人之學也哉？故求盡古人之道者，自其學始；求盡古人之學者，自其心始。古之學
translation_en:
…the work of learning at the elementary level in the Doctrine of the Mean [?] is especially pertinent. Without deep and sustained cultivation, how could one fail to attain this [?]?
Associate Examiner Deng, Instructor, comments: Amid subtle expressions and profound meanings, the writing takes elegant form. How often can one find a gifted man of the Central Plain such as you?
Associate Examiner Liang, School Instructor, comments: Outside the mind there is no Way; outside the Way there is no learning. Failure to understand learning arises from the mind’s obscuration. This essay speaks only of the ancients’ singleness of purpose in setting their minds [?], while the faults and confusion of latter-day learning are implicit throughout. Moreover, its language is dignified and elegant, never employing a single obscure expression. It has vitality: from it one can discern the learning of your mind.
Examiner Yuan, Secretary, comments: It pares away and marks out empty phrasing [?]; one can read it three times without tiring.
Examiner Xiao, Secretary, comments: Its analysis of principle is precise and clear, conforming to the proper standards at every turn. You are someone with whom one can pursue learning.
The substantial learning of the ancients began simply with how they set their minds. Why? Learning is the means of attaining the Way, and whether learning succeeds depends solely on how one sets one’s mind. If the mind is directed toward learning for oneself, what one learns is substantial. Being substantial, it is unified; being unified, the Way is thereby attained, and one’s own cultivation is accomplished. Draw upon what is nearest, and the myriad things are all present; gather it into the utmost inward concentration, and its transformative efficacy is complete. Thus the learning of the ancients can be understood. Otherwise, the mind becomes divided; competing concerns produce divergence, divergence becomes entangled and branches out, these branches spread into falsity, and falsity at its extreme brings ruin. This is surely what is called learning for others nowadays [?]. Can one speak of the ancients’ learning with such a person? Thus, those who seek fully to realize the Way of the ancients begin with their learning; those who seek fully to realize the learning of the ancients begin with their minds. Those of antiquity who studied…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
者爲已吾夫子有是言也夫學奚有初乎自古
人始也古人奚爲而有學也所以學爲聖人也
夫其學爲聖人也聖人之道各具於夫人之身
而奚以外求爲哉自夫人之不知此也喪其眞
於情欲之感奪其志於攻取之端梏其量於見
聞之小變其守於顯微之間馳其情於是非毁
譽之途而道日遠矣夫是之謂之失已失已者
古人之學乎古人之學有三而功化不與焉得
擇而決得誠而固得天而定夫唯其擇之決也
===
則内外有辨理欲有分而在人者弗足以惑誠
之固也則忠信以居果確以執而在人者弗足
以誣天之定也則安土敦仁窮理致命而在人
者弗足以動弗惑也斯在已者一弗誣也斯在
已者信弗動也斯在已者安由是藴之爲德行
發之爲事業上而天地中而民物遠而古今舉
弗能外吾學而吾學〔畢矣〕〔玆學〕也吾夫子言之
未詳也中庸一書首之以性命道教之原終之
以聖神功化之極實之以舜之知文之純武下
punctuated: 者爲已，吾夫子有是言也。夫學奚有初乎？自古人始也。古人奚爲而有學也？所以學爲聖人也。夫其學爲聖人也，聖人之道各具於夫人之身，而奚以外求爲哉？自夫人之不知此也，喪其眞於情欲之感，奪其志於攻取之端，梏其量於見聞之小，變其守於顯微之間，馳其情於是非毁譽之途，而道日遠矣。夫是之謂之失已。失已者，古人之學乎？古人之學有三，而功化不與焉：得擇而決，得誠而固，得天而定。夫唯其擇之決也，則内外有辨，理欲有分，而在人者弗足以惑；誠之固也，則忠信以居，果確以執，而在人者弗足以誣；天之定也，則安土敦仁，窮理致命，而在人者弗足以動。弗惑也，斯在已者一；弗誣也，斯在已者信；弗動也，斯在已者安。由是藴之爲德行，發之爲事業，上而天地，中而民物，遠而古今，舉弗能外吾學，而吾學〔畢矣〕。〔玆學〕也，吾夫子言之未詳也。《中庸》一書，首之以性命道教之原，終之以聖神功化之極，實之以舜之知、文之純、武下
translation_en:
…those who learned did so for themselves: our Master spoke these words. Where did learning originate? It began with the ancients. Why did the ancients engage in learning? To learn to become sages. In learning to become sages, the Way of the sages is already present within each person. Why, then, seek it outside oneself? Because people do not understand this, they lose their genuineness under the influence of passions and desires; their resolve is diverted by pursuits of acquisition; their capacity is confined by the narrowness of what they have seen and heard; their steadfastness changes according to whether they are observed or unseen; and their feelings race along the paths of approval and disapproval, disparagement and praise. Thus they grow daily more distant from the Way. This is what is called losing oneself. Can losing oneself be the learning of the ancients?

The learning of the ancients has three essentials, not counting its achievements and transforming effects: attaining discrimination and thereby becoming decisive; attaining sincerity and thereby becoming firm; attaining accord with Heaven and thereby becoming settled. Through decisiveness in discrimination, one distinguishes the internal from the external and separates principle from desire, so that what lies with others cannot confuse one. Through firmness in sincerity, one abides in loyalty and trustworthiness and holds fast with resolution, so that what lies with others cannot deceive one. Through settled accord with Heaven, one rests content where one dwells and cultivates benevolence, fathoms principle and fulfills one’s allotted destiny, so that what lies with others cannot unsettle one. Undeluded, what lies within oneself becomes unified; undeceived, what lies within oneself becomes true; unshaken, what lies within oneself becomes secure. Stored within, this becomes virtuous conduct; expressed outwardly, it becomes practical achievement. Above, Heaven and Earth; in our midst, people and things; across the distance of time, antiquity and the present—nothing can fall outside my learning, and my learning is then 〔complete〕.

As for 〔this learning〕, our Master did not discuss it in detail. The Doctrine of the Mean begins with the origins of human nature, Heaven’s mandate, the Way, and instruction, and ends with the utmost achievements and transforming effects of sagely and spiritual attainment. It gives these substance through Shun’s wisdom, King Wen’s purity, King Wu’s [?]…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
周公之制作其言學問之極功固已盡矣及廿□
末也卒歸之尚絅之一言究其說惟曰闇然惟
曰淡而不厭簡而文温而理惟曰無惡于志惟
曰不言而信不動而敬殆亦始諸立心而已爾
嗚呼茲固吾之所謂實學者也茲固吾夫子之
所謂爲己者也蓋嘗執是而求之聖門諸子有
專於爲己者顔氏子之庶幾是也有專於爲人
者子張氏之賤儒是也若子夏之入見夫子之
道而悅出見世俗之紛華而悅其猶在爲人爲
===
己之間乎是則爲人之病雖賢者不免他奚足
云宜夫子之有是言也千載而下吾于董生差
有取焉其言曰正其誼不謀其利明其道不計
其功豈亦有得于爲己之學者邪謹論
同前
張浹
同考試官教諭馬　批　立意高邁脩辭雋永且議
論識見卓犖有度珍評珍評
同考試官教諭張　批　力辨陳詞一自肺腑流出
punctuated:
周公之制作，其言學問之極功，固已盡矣。及廿□末也，卒歸之尚絅之一言。究其說，惟曰闇然，惟曰淡而不厭、簡而文、温而理，惟曰無惡于志，惟曰不言而信、不動而敬，殆亦始諸立心而已爾。嗚呼！茲固吾之所謂實學者也，茲固吾夫子之所謂爲己者也。蓋嘗執是而求之聖門諸子，有專於爲己者，顔氏子之庶幾是也；有專於爲人者，子張氏之賤儒是也。若子夏之入見夫子之道而悅，出見世俗之紛華而悅，其猶在爲人爲己之間乎？是則爲人之病，雖賢者不免，他奚足云！宜夫子之有是言也。千載而下，吾于董生差有取焉。其言曰：「正其誼不謀其利，明其道不計其功。」豈亦有得于爲己之學者邪？謹論。
同前。
張浹。
同考試官教諭馬，批：「立意高邁，脩辭雋永，且議論識見卓犖有度。珍評！珍評！」
同考試官教諭張，批：「力辨陳詞，一自肺腑流出，
translation_en:
…and the institutions established by the Duke of Zhou: its account of the ultimate achievements of learning is already exhaustive. Yet when it reaches its conclusion [? text corrupt: 廿□], it finally returns to the single phrase, “wearing a plain outer garment over brocade.” Examining its explanation, we find only “remaining inconspicuous”; only “bland yet never tiresome, simple yet patterned, gentle yet principled”; only “nothing objectionable in one’s intentions”; only “trusted without speaking, revered without moving.” This, too, surely begins simply with setting one’s heart aright. Alas! This is precisely what I call substantive learning, precisely what our Master called learning for oneself. Applying this principle, I have sought examples among the disciples of the Sage. There was one devoted to learning for himself: Master Yan, who came close to the Way. There was one devoted to learning for others’ approval: Zizhang, associated with the “petty scholar.” As for Zixia, who delighted in the Master’s Way when he entered his presence, yet delighted in the world’s glitter and bustle when he went out—was he not still poised between learning for others’ approval and learning for himself? Thus even the worthy cannot escape the failing of learning for others’ approval; what need is there to speak of anyone else? It was fitting that the Master should have made this statement. A thousand years later, I find something to approve in Master Dong. He said: “Set right what is morally fitting without seeking profit; illuminate the Way without calculating achievement.” Might he, too, have attained some understanding of learning for oneself? Respectfully submitted as a discourse.
Same as above.
Zhang Jia.
Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: “The conception is lofty and far-reaching, the phrasing rich in lasting meaning. Moreover, the argument and insight are outstanding and measured. A precious appraisal! A precious appraisal! [?]”
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The vigorous argument and its expression flow entirely from the depths of the heart…”

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
簡古中淵渊曲折有一瀉千里之勢傷今懷古其志偉
然物表奇才奇才
考試官主事袁　批　鍛鍊精奇步驟閒雅起伏頓
挫蛟騰虎踞感慨中臨痱含蓄如聞韶鈞一倡三嘆他
日翔翔橫鶩凌轢踔踊文不在玆乎錄之以俟知音君
子首焉
考試官主事蕭　批　立論奇特無一俗句知非尋
常舉業士也
天下之道散於博而統於約後世之學遺於內
===
而詳乎外而聖人始有取於古矣天下之道固
亦天下之人學之也而聖人者豈固嘉彼以病
此樂前以虞後而取古以廢今哉惟夫後世之
學槩之於其變也雜之於其動也紛更之於其
多端也心痼於有我志眩於沉思道狃於多岐
學病於罔覺紛紛蠱惑卒無所定而天下之道
始不可以其身有矣夫已者寄道之具也學者
葦道之府也失之寄以求其具壞之府以求其
葦略之已以求其成昧之學以求其道奉之見
punctuated:
簡古中淵渊曲折，有一瀉千里之勢。傷今懷古，其志偉然物表。奇才！奇才！
考試官主事袁，批：鍛鍊精奇，步驟閒雅，起伏頓挫，蛟騰虎踞。感慨中臨痱，含蓄如聞韶鈞，一倡三嘆。他日翔翔橫鶩，凌轢踔踊，文不在玆乎？錄之以俟知音君子首焉。
考試官主事蕭，批：立論奇特，無一俗句，知非尋常舉業士也。
天下之道，散於博而統於約。後世之學，遺於內而詳乎外，而聖人始有取於古矣。天下之道，固亦天下之人學之也。而聖人者，豈固嘉彼以病此，樂前以虞後，而取古以廢今哉？惟夫後世之學，槩之於其變也，雜之於其動也，紛更之於其多端也。心痼於有我，志眩於沉思，道狃於多岐，學病於罔覺，紛紛蠱惑，卒無所定，而天下之道始不可以其身有矣。夫已者，寄道之具也；學者，葦道之府也。失之寄以求其具，壞之府以求其葦，略之已以求其成，昧之學以求其道，奉之見
translation_en:
…Within its spare, antique style are depth [?] and intricate turns, with the momentum of a torrent pouring a thousand li. Lamenting the present and cherishing antiquity, his aspirations rise grandly above worldly things. An extraordinary talent! An extraordinary talent!
Examiner Yuan, a Bureau Secretary, comments: The writing is exquisitely and remarkably wrought; its progression is composed and elegant. Its rises, falls, pauses, and turns resemble a soaring dragon and a crouching tiger. Amid its impassioned reflections, [the wording is unclear: 臨痱][?]; its restrained resonance is like hearing the Shao and Jun music, one voice singing and three responding. In days to come, he will soar and range freely, surpassing others and leaping high. Does not literary accomplishment reside here? I record this to await discerning gentlemen who will accord it first place.
Examiner Xiao, a Bureau Secretary, comments: The argument is extraordinary, without a single commonplace phrase. One can tell that this is no ordinary student of examination writing.
The Way of all under Heaven is dispersed in breadth but united in essentials. The learning of later ages neglects what is within and elaborates what is without; thus the Sage came to favor antiquity. The Way of all under Heaven is, of course, also what the people of all under Heaven study. Yet would the Sage really praise the one to disparage the other, delight in earlier times to express misgivings about later ones, and favor antiquity to discard the present? It is simply that the learning of later ages becomes indiscriminate amid its changes [?], mixed amid its activities, and confusedly altered amid its many pursuits. The mind is inveterately attached to self; the will is bewildered by deep reflection; the Way becomes accustomed to divergent paths; and learning suffers from a lack of awakening. Amid a welter of delusion, nothing is finally settled, and people can no longer embody the Way of all under Heaven in themselves. The self [?] is the instrument in which the Way lodges; learning is the repository that preserves [?] the Way. Losing what lodges there while seeking its instrument, destroying the repository while seeking what it preserves [?], neglecting the self [?] while seeking its perfection, obscuring learning while seeking its Way, upholding one's views [?]…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
也是豈聖人所望於天下而學之貴哉春秋之
世斯風熾矣聖遠言湮道出多門讒人鼓煩學
士失真雖以由求子張之徒卒以㶊於利祿之
從而弗知警則其甚可以卜矣孔子曰古之學
者爲己嗚呼其有感於今哉且今猶古也人物
之孳生恒相同也性道之流出恒相類也時教
之植立恒相關也正學之遊息恒相一也而古
之學者卒若此今之學者卒若彼予於是嘗有
以求其故矣夫兩儀奠位元化攸生五性感動
===
咸居其所道斯出矣賦性有高下資禀有强弱
才思有昏明多者衰之寡者益之奠麗和則以
引以翼教斯立矣玉不琢不成器焉不調不爲
良人不學不知道高山景行先民時若遜志時
敏乾乾不息學斯建矣是故敦典庸禮以若其
性匡直輔翼以誘其質候明揵識以並其生離
經辨志以考其成鞭朴夏楚以董其威博依雜
詠以精其藝退息居業以勑其幾性若則理斯
復矣質誘則才斯達矣生並則仁斯久矣成考
punctuated:
也。是豈聖人所望於天下而學之貴哉？春秋之世，斯風熾矣。聖遠言湮，道出多門，讒人鼓煩，學士失真。雖以由、求、子張之徒，卒以㶊於利祿之從而弗知警，則其甚可以卜矣。孔子曰：「古之學者爲己。」嗚呼，其有感於今哉！且今猶古也，人物之孳生恒相同也，性道之流出恒相類也，時教之植立恒相關也，正學之遊息恒相一也。而古之學者卒若此，今之學者卒若彼，予於是嘗有以求其故矣。
夫兩儀奠位，元化攸生，五性感動，咸居其所，道斯出矣。賦性有高下，資禀有强弱，才思有昏明，多者衰之，寡者益之，奠麗和則，以引以翼，教斯立矣。玉不琢，不成器；焉不調，不爲良；人不學，不知道。高山景行，先民時若，遜志時敏，乾乾不息，學斯建矣。
是故敦典庸禮，以若其性；匡直輔翼，以誘其質；候明揵識，以並其生；離經辨志，以考其成；鞭朴夏楚，以董其威；博依雜詠，以精其藝；退息居業，以勑其幾。性若則理斯復矣，質誘則才斯達矣，生並則仁斯久矣，成考……
translation_en:
…Is this what the sage hoped for from all under Heaven, and what makes learning precious? In the Spring and Autumn period, this tendency flourished. The sages were distant and their words obscured; the Way issued from many schools, slanderers stirred up confusion, and scholars lost what was genuine. Even men such as You, Qiu, and Zizhang ultimately became absorbed [?] in pursuing profit and official emoluments, without recognizing the need for caution. From this one can judge how extreme the situation had become. Confucius said, “The learners of antiquity studied for their own sake.” Alas, surely he spoke out of concern for his own times! Yet the present is like antiquity: the propagation of people and other beings is always the same; the unfolding of human nature and the Way is always similar; the establishment of instruction suited to the times is always interconnected; and the pursuit of proper learning, in both activity and repose, is always one. Yet the learners of antiquity ultimately were like this, while those of today are like that. I have therefore sought the reason.
When the Two Powers, Heaven and Earth, took their places, primordial transformation arose. The five aspects of human nature were stirred into activity, each occupying its proper place: thus the Way emerged. Endowed natures differ in elevation, innate capacities in strength, and intellectual abilities in clarity. Reducing what is excessive and augmenting what is deficient, establishing adherence to harmonious norms [?], guiding and supporting—thus instruction was established. Jade that is not carved does not become a vessel; [a horse?] that is not trained does not become a fine one; a person who does not learn does not know the Way. Looking up to lofty mountains and following the great road, taking the ancients as models, being humble in purpose and constantly diligent, striving unceasingly—thus learning was established.
Therefore, they upheld the enduring norms and employed ritual to accord with people's nature; corrected and supported them to guide their native qualities; fostered clarity and strengthened understanding [?] to nurture their life together; examined their parsing of the classics and discernment of aspirations to assess their attainment; used whips, rods, and switches of catalpa and thorn to enforce discipline; employed broad recitation and varied chanting to refine their accomplishments; and, in retirement and repose, dwelt upon their studies to attend carefully to the first stirrings of thought. When their nature was accorded with, principle was restored; when their native qualities were guided, their abilities developed fully; when their life was nurtured together, benevolence endured; when their attainment was assessed…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
則賢斯兢矣威董則殆斯決矣藝精則末其兼
矣幾勑則本斯固矣理復而不危才達而不限
仁久而不息賢兢而不棄殆決而不疑末兼而
不偏本固而不搖是故賦形有定從違有常貞
固有求操執有經尋向有門外不詳而內不略
人不虞而已是爲此其所以爲古之學而非瑣
瑣者之可倫也及其流風既遠愈久愈失真傳
不見僞學迭興執守之心喪馳騖之念長窮經
之意衰浮利之志動貪者慕柔願辨者競遊說
===
愚者苦昏惑智者逞譎詐強勇者樂饕餮夫然
後真性失於昏惑之岐道義喪於異端之圖知
能鑿於鴻鵠之務道心危於困蒙之遠天理賊
於視儍之錯中心搖搖靡知所趨意緒紛紜往
來無所然後迪教履道之能精義入神之極盡
性希天之妙窮理知化之學始不足爲君人者
望矣嗚呼人一也而有古今之異學一也而有
人已之異道一也而有從違之異此其所以一
古一今一彼一此一得一失而聖人之拳拳於
punctuated: 則賢斯兢矣，威董則殆斯決矣，藝精則末其兼矣，幾勑則本斯固矣。理復而不危，才達而不限，仁久而不息，賢兢而不棄，殆決而不疑，末兼而不偏，本固而不搖。是故賦形有定，從違有常，貞固有求，操執有經，尋向有門，外不詳而內不略，人不虞而已是爲。此其所以爲古之學，而非瑣瑣者之可倫也。及其流風既遠，愈久愈失，真傳不見，僞學迭興，執守之心喪，馳騖之念長，窮經之意衰，浮利之志動。貪者慕柔願，辨者競遊說，愚者苦昏惑，智者逞譎詐，強勇者樂饕餮。夫然後真性失於昏惑之岐，道義喪於異端之圖，知能鑿於鴻鵠之務，道心危於困蒙之遠，天理賊於視儍之錯。中心搖搖，靡知所趨；意緒紛紜，往來無所。然後迪教履道之能，精義入神之極，盡性希天之妙，窮理知化之學，始不足爲君人者望矣。嗚呼！人一也，而有古今之異；學一也，而有人已之異；道一也，而有從違之異。此其所以一古一今，一彼一此，一得一失，而聖人之拳拳於
translation_en:
…then the worthy strive earnestly. When disciplinary authority is exercised, danger is dispelled; when the arts are mastered, their subsidiary aspects are comprehensively embraced [?]; when incipient impulses are kept in check, the foundation is secured. Principle is restored without peril; talent develops without restriction; benevolence endures without interruption; the worthy strive without abandoning their efforts; danger is dispelled without uncertainty; subsidiary aspects are comprehensively embraced without partiality; and the foundation is secured without wavering. Thus, the endowment of bodily form has its fixed constitution; following or departing from the Way has its constant consequences; steadfastness has an object to pursue; maintaining one's commitments has guiding standards; and seeking a direction has a gateway. One does not elaborate on externals while neglecting what is within; one does not concern oneself with others, but attends to oneself [?]. This is what constitutes the learning of antiquity, which petty scholars cannot equal.

But once its lingering influence had grown remote, the longer the interval, the greater the loss. The true transmission disappeared, and spurious learning arose in succession. The resolve to hold firmly to one's principles was lost, while thoughts of restless pursuit increased. The desire to fathom the Classics declined, while ambitions for fleeting profit stirred. The greedy admired pliant docility [?]; the eloquent competed in itinerant persuasion; the foolish suffered from confusion and delusion; the clever gave free rein to deceit; and the strong and bold delighted in voracious indulgence. Only then was one's true nature lost along the branching paths of confusion, and the Way and righteousness forfeited in schemes of heterodox teaching. Knowledge and ability were distorted by preoccupation with swans and wild geese; the mind of the Way was imperiled by estrangement amid ignorance and perplexity [?]; and Heaven's principle was injured by errors of foolish perception [?]. Inwardly unsettled, people did not know where to turn; their thoughts were tangled, coming and going without a resting place.

Then the capacity to follow instruction and practice the Way, the highest attainment of refining one's understanding of righteousness and entering the realm of the spiritual, the subtle achievement of fully realizing one's nature and aspiring to Heaven, and the learning that fathoms principle and understands transformation ceased to be things that rulers could hope for.

Alas! Human beings are alike, yet there is a difference between antiquity and the present. Learning is one, yet there is a difference between learning for others and learning for oneself. The Way is one, yet there is a difference between following it and departing from it. This is why there is antiquity on one side and the present on the other, that on one side and this on the other, attainment on one side and loss on the other, and why the sage was so earnestly concerned with…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
是矣雖然孔子之斯意也亦屢見矣直道之行
不已於嘆或是之亡三致之辭豈天之降才果
爾殊而人之爲學果今古之不同歟嗟夫亦其
時焉耳矣夫唐虞之民也完其極也流而爲野
夏之民也質其極也流而爲史周之民也文其
極也流而爲史江河日轉愈趨愈下孔子之所
以致謹於此其爲世慮也至矣夫觀變以易化
者聖也矯時以從俗者明也孔子備明聖之德
而不得用於時徒使其說著於言語文字之間
===
甚哉春秋之世亦可卜矣
表
擬宋司馬光進三事五規表〔嘉祐六年〕
劉棨
同考試官教諭林　批〔得四六體〕
同考試官教諭鄧　批〔老臣謀國用意忠厚此作得之〕
同考試官學正梁　批〔典雅渾厚〕
考試官主事袁　批〔叙事有體〕
考試官主事蕭　批〔不尚辭華且有諷諫之〕
punctuated:
是矣。雖然，孔子之斯意也，亦屢見矣。「直道之行」，不已於嘆；「或是之亡」，三致之辭。豈天之降才果爾殊，而人之爲學果今古之不同歟？嗟夫！亦其時焉耳矣。夫唐虞之民也完，其極也流而爲野；夏之民也質，其極也流而爲史；周之民也文，其極也流而爲史。江河日轉，愈趨愈下。孔子之所以致謹於此，其爲世慮也至矣。夫觀變以易化者，聖也；矯時以從俗者，明也。孔子備明聖之德，而不得用於時，徒使其說著於言語文字之間。甚哉！春秋之世，亦可卜矣。

表
擬宋司馬光進三事五規表〔嘉祐六年〕
劉棨
同考試官教諭林批〔得四六體〕。
同考試官教諭鄧批〔老臣謀國，用意忠厚，此作得之〕。
同考試官學正梁批〔典雅渾厚〕。
考試官主事袁批〔叙事有體〕。
考試官主事蕭批〔不尚辭華，且有諷諫之〕。
translation_en:
…this is what concerned the sage so deeply. Nevertheless, this intention of Confucius appears repeatedly. Concerning “the practice of the straight Way,” he did not cease to sigh; concerning “the disappearance of such things,” he expressed himself repeatedly [?]. Could Heaven’s endowment of talent really differ so greatly, and could people’s pursuit of learning really differ between antiquity and the present? Alas! It is simply a matter of their times. The people under Tang and Yu were whole in their nature; carried to an extreme, this degenerated into rusticity. The people of Xia were plain; carried to an extreme, this degenerated into excessive refinement [?]. The people of Zhou were cultivated; carried to an extreme, this degenerated into excessive refinement. Like rivers flowing onward each day, the farther they run, the lower they descend. Confucius’s particular care in this matter shows the utmost concern for the world. To observe changes and thereby transform people is sagacity; to correct the times while accommodating prevailing customs is discernment. Confucius possessed both discernment and sagacity, yet could not put them into practice in his time, leaving his teachings merely recorded in speech and writing. How lamentable! From this one can also judge the state of the Spring and Autumn age.

Memorial
A Memorial Presenting Three Matters and Five Admonitions, Written in the Person of Sima Guang of the Song Dynasty 〔Sixth year of Jiayou [1061]〕
By Liu Qi

Associate Examiner Lin, an Instructor, comments: 〔It achieves the form of four-and-six parallel prose.〕
Associate Examiner Deng, an Instructor, comments: 〔An elder minister’s planning for the state is loyal and generous in intention; this composition captures that quality.〕
Associate Examiner Liang, a Director of Studies, comments: 〔Classically elegant, full, and substantial.〕
Examiner Yuan, a Secretary, comments: 〔The presentation of affairs observes the proper form.〕
Examiner Xiao, a Secretary, comments: 〔It does not prize ornate diction, and furthermore possesses the … of indirect remonstrance [?].〕

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
嘉祐六年某月日臣光言昨蒙
聖恩以臣知諫院謹以所草三事五規
上進者
謀猷入告九重垂兼聽之明
儆戒相成一得效颺言之職事存敷奏義
切箴規臣光誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊念忠
臣愛君在納誨以輔德聖王從諫恒虛已
以受人合宮來庶績之謨衢室播省成之
訓詩夸補衮書叙從繩徇木鐸於道人徵
===
丹書於尚父〔□〕疇洛風遠獻納司存慨治安
數千言設施〔□〕究暨太平十二策論列徒
勤仰惟側席之虛懷祇若和羹之休命忠
非逆耳道豈格心理亂興衰粗陳梗槩是
非名實詳析幾微庶愚衷上達於
宸旒望下體不遺乎葑菲茲蓋伏遇
〇〇〇〇
體元斂福
則大凝圖
punctuated:
嘉祐六年某月日，臣光言：昨蒙聖恩，以臣知諫院，謹以所草三事五規上進者。
謀猷入告，九重垂兼聽之明；儆戒相成，一得效颺言之職。事存敷奏，義切箴規。臣光誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊念忠臣愛君，在納誨以輔德；聖王從諫，恒虛已以受人。合宮來庶績之謨，衢室播省成之訓。詩夸補衮，書叙從繩。徇木鐸於道人，徵丹書於尚父。〔□〕疇洛風遠，獻納司存。慨治安數千言，設施〔□〕究；暨太平十二策，論列徒勤。仰惟側席之虛懷，祇若和羹之休命。忠非逆耳，道豈格心？理亂興衰，粗陳梗槩；是非名實，詳析幾微。庶愚衷上達於宸旒，望下體不遺乎葑菲。茲蓋伏遇〇〇〇〇，體元斂福，則大凝圖。
translation_en:
On a certain day of a certain month in the sixth year of Jiayou, your servant Guang states: Recently, through your sagely grace, I was appointed to administer the Remonstrance Bureau. I respectfully submit the Three Matters and Five Admonitions that I have drafted.
Plans and counsels are presented to the throne, and Your Majesty manifests the wisdom of hearing all sides. Warnings and admonitions assist in bringing things to completion; with whatever insight I possess, I discharge my duty to speak openly. My purpose lies in presenting counsel; my intent is earnestly to admonish. Your servant Guang, in fear and trembling, bows his head to the ground again and again.
I humbly reflect that a loyal minister’s love for his ruler consists in offering admonition to assist his virtue; a sage king, in following remonstrance, always humbles himself to receive the words of others. To the Hegong palace came counsels for every undertaking; from the Qushi hall went forth instructions to examine accomplishments. The Book of Odes praises the mending of the royal robe; the Book of Documents recounts following the marking line. A wooden bell was sounded along the roads to solicit counsel, and the Cinnabar Writing was sought from Shangfu. [Illegible annotation.] The traditions of the categories and the Luo River are remote [?], yet the office charged with presenting counsel remains.
Alas, the several thousand words on good government and security were not fully put into effect [?]; and the twelve policy proposals for great peace likewise amounted only to diligent exposition. Looking up to Your Majesty’s open-minded readiness to receive counsel, I reverently follow your gracious command to help season the broth of government. Is loyalty not sometimes displeasing to the ear? How could the Way fail to reach the sovereign’s heart? On order and disorder, rise and decline, I have roughly set out the essentials; on right and wrong, names and realities, I have closely distinguished the subtlest points. May my humble sincerity reach the imperial throne; may you not discard the roots of turnips and radishes merely because they lie below—that is, may you accept what is useful even in lowly counsel.
This is because I have humbly encountered [four circle placeholders in the text]—one who embodies the primal principle and gathers blessings, who takes greatness as his model and consolidates the imperial design …

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
渾溥汜以無私
道含弘而不殺式奏舞干之績載歌茅拔之
篇俊乂明揚工師競勸如臣迂謬亦辱甄
收叢脞逃譏宗儲過裘采納頃者條陳日
食□傳脩容超躐班階叨塵諫諍循牆是
懼綿臁奚能念涓流靡益於江河而大厦
或資於榱桷首開三事繼進五規曰君德
曰馭臣曰揀軍皇王之道備矣如惜時如
遠謀如保業古今之鑒昭然深致意於謹
===
微欲求端於務實綱宏目細綴緝無遺事
核詞繁贊襄不暇自謂勉傾夫葵藿敢云
切中乎膏肓倘
垂一夜之觀或備萬幾之助臣光潛脩涑水
何意登庸試判幷州豈圖知遇有懷必吐
背負
明時無言不酬冀收實效蓋平生學力盡在
此書而天與朴忠竊嘗自許遂忘固陋少
答
punctuated: 渾溥汜以無私，道含弘而不殺。式奏舞干之績，載歌茅拔之篇。俊乂明揚，工師競勸。如臣迂謬，亦辱甄收。叢脞逃譏，宗儲過裘采納。頃者條陳日食□傳脩容，超躐班階，叨塵諫諍。循牆是懼，綿臁奚能？念涓流靡益於江河，而大厦或資於榱桷。首開三事，繼進五規：曰君德，曰馭臣，曰揀軍，皇王之道備矣；如惜時，如遠謀，如保業，古今之鑒昭然。深致意於謹微，欲求端於務實。綱宏目細，綴緝無遺；事核詞繁，贊襄不暇。自謂勉傾夫葵藿，敢云切中乎膏肓？倘垂一夜之觀，或備萬幾之助。臣光潛脩涑水，何意登庸？試判幷州，豈圖知遇？有懷必吐，背負明時；無言不酬，冀收實效。蓋平生學力盡在此書，而天與朴忠，竊嘗自許，遂忘固陋，少答
translation_en:
…vastly encompassing all without partiality, Your Way embraces all generously and diminishes none. Thus are achieved the pacifying results of the shield dance, and again is sung the poem of pulling up the thatch grass. The talented and worthy are publicly commended and promoted; officials of every rank vie in diligent service. Even one as misguided and inept as your servant has been honored with selection and appointment. I have escaped censure for preoccupation with petty matters; the passage concerning the imperial heir and the acceptance of advice is obscure [?]. Recently I submitted proposals concerning a solar eclipse and the reform of personal conduct [□; intervening wording doubtful]. Promoted beyond the normal steps of rank, I presumptuously occupied a remonstrance post. Fearfully I kept close to the wall: what could one so feeble accomplish [?]? I reflected that a trickle adds little to rivers, yet a great hall may depend upon its rafters.

I first set forth three matters, then presented five admonitions. Concerning the ruler’s virtue, the management of ministers, and the selection of troops, the Way of the august sovereigns and kings is fully provided. In such matters as valuing time, planning far ahead, and preserving the imperial enterprise, the lessons of past and present stand clear. I devoted particular attention to vigilance over small beginnings, seeking a starting point in practical substance. Broad in outline and detailed in particulars, the work was compiled without omission. Its matters were examined closely and its language was copious; I spared no effort in assisting the government. I would say only that I strove to pour out my loyalty, like mallows turning toward the sun. How could I dare claim to have struck at the deepest seat of the malady? If You should condescend to read it for a single night, it might offer some assistance amid the myriad affairs of state.

Your servant Guang cultivated himself in retirement at Sushui: how could I have expected advancement to office? When provisionally serving as assistant administrator of Bingzhou, how could I have anticipated recognition and favor? Whatever I held in my heart I had to express—‘turning my back upon and failing this enlightened age’ [?]. Every word sought to repay Your favor, in the hope of achieving practical results. The learning and effort of my entire life are contained in this book. I have privately ventured to credit myself with a plain loyalty bestowed by Heaven; thus, forgetting my ignorance and limited understanding, I seek in some small measure to repay…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
恩私伏望
懋止輦之芳規時時省覽
宏轉圜之雅量一一施行
離照緝熙忠邪不惑
乾剛獨斷威福必行仁明武以文脩庶富教
之克盡本支百世益培豐芑之遺
歷數萬年永繫苞桑之固臣無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屛營之至謹以三事五規隨表封進以
聞
===
第叄場
策
第一問
陳乙
同考試官教諭林 批 古之帝王及我
聖祖神宗維持世道以成太平無疆之休惟有此學此道我
皇上會其全闡其妙亦惟在此子能歷歷言之不媿中州之士矣
同考試官教諭鄭 批 愉楊
punctuated:
恩私。伏望懋止輦之芳規，時時省覽；宏轉圜之雅量，一一施行。離照緝熙，忠邪不惑；乾剛獨斷，威福必行。仁明武以文脩，庶富教之克盡。本支百世，益培豐芑之遺；歷數萬年，永繫苞桑之固。臣無任瞻天仰聖、激切屛營之至，謹以三事五規隨表封進以聞。

策

陳乙
同考試官教諭林批：「古之帝王及我聖祖神宗，維持世道，以成太平無疆之休，惟有此學此道。我皇上會其全，闡其妙，亦惟在此。子能歷歷言之，不媿中州之士矣。」
同考試官教諭鄭批：「愉楊
translation_en:
…Your gracious favor. I humbly hope that Your Majesty will carry forward the fine example of stopping the imperial carriage to read, examining this work from time to time, and display the noble magnanimity that turns as readily as a wheel, putting its recommendations into effect one by one. May your radiance, like that of the sun, shine ever more brightly, distinguishing without confusion the loyal from the wicked; may your heavenly firmness exercise sole judgment, ensuring that punishments and rewards take effect. May benevolence, discernment, and martial prowess be refined through civil culture, and may the tasks of increasing the population, enriching it, and educating it be fully accomplished. May the main and collateral branches of the imperial house endure for a hundred generations, further nurturing the legacy of flourishing millet—the provision made for descendants; may your allotted reign endure for ten thousand years, secured forever as though bound to the firm roots of a mulberry clump. Your servant, looking up to Heaven and reverently regarding Your Sageliness, cannot contain his profound emotion and trembling awe. I respectfully submit under seal, together with this memorial, the Three Matters and Five Admonitions for Your Majesty’s consideration.
