title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖學之文貴於平正嚴肅是作不尚刻削不事詞華蓋庶幾有得於此者
同考試官學正梁　批〔初中二場已占子邃博之〕
〔學及得五策氣昌辭渾〕
聖製一策尤見問悉不獨對揚而已佳士佳士
考試官主事袁　批〔道統之傳〕
聖學之妙善於鋪張錄之
考試官主事蕭　批〔五策俱不凡是篇條陳當至道〕
〔統之傳以及我〕
祖宗開國啓後之意既已悉備其于
===
皇上躬行心得之妙亦能窺識豈亦沾漏之久者乎
道有大統至聖人而後會其全學有心法
得聖人而始闡其妙夫會其全則兼統條
貫治道由之而大成矣闡其妙則告詔箴
規聖德因之而日著矣以一心而契帝王
道統之傳以數言而盡古今授受之妙何
幸於我
皇上今日見之愚也不敏敢因明問而摹寫其
萬一以復夫斯道在天下三極賴之以立
punctuated:
聖學之文，貴於平正嚴肅。是作不尚刻削，不事詞華，蓋庶幾有得於此者。

同考試官學正梁批〔初中二場已占子邃博之〕〔學及得五策氣昌辭渾〕聖製一策，尤見問悉，不獨對揚而已。佳士！佳士！

考試官主事袁批〔道統之傳〕聖學之妙，善於鋪張，錄之。

考試官主事蕭批〔五策俱不凡是篇條陳當至道〕〔統之傳以及我〕祖宗開國啓後之意，既已悉備，其于皇上躬行心得之妙，亦能窺識，豈亦沾漏之久者乎？

道有大統，至聖人而後會其全；學有心法，得聖人而始闡其妙。夫會其全，則兼統條貫，治道由之而大成矣；闡其妙，則告詔箴規，聖德因之而日著矣。以一心而契帝王道統之傳，以數言而盡古今授受之妙，何幸於我皇上今日見之！愚也不敏，敢因明問而摹寫其萬一以復。夫斯道在天下，三極賴之以立
translation_en:
…writing on sagely learning is valued for its evenness, rectitude, gravity, and solemnity. This composition prizes neither laborious refinement nor ornate diction; it seems indeed to have attained something of this ideal.

Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor, comments: 〔In the first and second sessions I had already discerned your profound and extensive〕〔learning. On receiving your five policy essays, I found their spirit abundant and their language rounded and substantial.〕The essay answering the imperially composed question especially reveals thoroughness in addressing the question [?], going beyond merely responding to and extolling the imperial message. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!

Examiner Yuan, Secretary, comments: 〔The transmission of the succession of the Way〕and the subtleties of sagely learning are ably expounded. Accept him.

Examiner Xiao, Secretary, comments: 〔All five policy essays are extraordinary. This piece sets forth its points aptly [?], reaching the transmission of the succession of the Way〕〔and extending to our〕imperial ancestors’ purposes in founding the state and preparing the way for their successors, all of which it treats fully. It also discerns the subtleties of His Majesty’s personal practice and inward understanding. Could he, too, have long been steeped in these influences [?]?

The Way has a great succession: only with a sage is its entirety brought together. Learning has a method of the mind: only through a sage are its subtleties elucidated. When its entirety is brought together, its ramifications and connecting principles are comprehensively unified, and through this the way of governance reaches its fullest realization. When its subtleties are elucidated, instructions, declarations, admonitions, and counsels are given, and through these sagely virtue becomes daily more manifest. With a single mind, to accord with the transmission of the succession of the Way among emperors and kings; in a few words, to encompass the subtleties of its transmission and reception throughout past and present—how fortunate we are to witness this today in our Emperor! Foolish and slow of understanding though I am, I venture, in response to your discerning question, to portray one ten-thousandth of this as my reply. As for this Way within the world, the Three Ultimates—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—depend upon it for their establishment…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
者也心學在聖人道統因之以行者也有
其心斯有其學有其學斯有其道有其道
斯有其治自古聖君賢相以訓以謨以箴
以戒凡以明此而已也求諸五帝之世黃
帝嘗有輿几之箴矣一傳而執中再傳而
精一其統同其道同也求諸三王之世大
禹嘗有夏氏之箴矣商繼而建中周繼而
建極其道同其心同也降而漢唐大風有
歌栢梁有詠丹扆君位政刑諸箴非不蔚
===
乎成章也視吾聖敬之道何居降而趙宋
脩身有訓自戒有詞元良六藝內侍諸作
非不粲然成文也方諸誠一之道何預無
怪乎治功之不振統紀之不明也我
太祖創業垂統以心學作之於前
列聖繼體守文以心學傳之於後是故允執厥
中之旨晦蝕於天下也久矣至洪武五年
而始講明誠一弗二之學遺忘於後世也
久矣于觀心亭而始表章他如洪範
punctuated:
者也。心學在聖人，道統因之以行者也。有其心，斯有其學；有其學，斯有其道；有其道，斯有其治。自古聖君賢相，以訓以謨，以箴以戒，凡以明此而已也。求諸五帝之世，黃帝嘗有輿几之箴矣。一傳而執中，再傳而精一，其統同，其道同也。求諸三王之世，大禹嘗有夏氏之箴矣。商繼而建中，周繼而建極，其道同，其心同也。降而漢唐，《大風》有歌，《栢梁》有詠，丹扆、君位、政刑諸箴，非不蔚乎成章也，視吾聖敬之道何居？降而趙宋，脩身有訓，自戒有詞，元良、六藝、內侍諸作，非不粲然成文也，方諸誠一之道何預？無怪乎治功之不振、統紀之不明也。
我太祖創業垂統，以心學作之於前；列聖繼體守文，以心學傳之於後。是故允執厥中之旨，晦蝕於天下也久矣，至洪武五年而始講明；誠一弗二之學，遺忘於後世也久矣，于觀心亭而始表章。他如《洪範》
translation_en:
… to be established. In the sages, learning of the mind is what enables the succession of the Way to be carried forward. With such a mind comes such learning; with such learning comes such a Way; with such a Way comes such governance. Since antiquity, sage rulers and worthy ministers have offered instructions, counsels, admonitions, and warnings, all simply to make this clear. Looking to the age of the Five Emperors, the Yellow Emperor once had admonitions for his carriage and armrest. In the first transmission came holding fast to the mean; in the second, refinement and singleness of mind. Their succession was the same, and their Way was the same. Looking to the age of the Three Kings, Yu the Great once had the Admonitions of the Xia. The Shang succeeded them and established the mean; the Zhou succeeded them and established the supreme standard. Their Way was the same, and their mind was the same. Later, under the Han and Tang, there were the Song of the Great Wind and verses on the Cypress Beam Terrace, along with admonitions concerning the vermilion screen, the ruler’s position, and government and punishments. These were certainly splendid compositions, but where did they stand in relation to our Way of sagely reverence? Later still, under the Zhao house of Song, there were instructions on self-cultivation, verses of self-admonition, and works concerning the heir apparent, the Six Arts, and palace attendants. These were certainly brilliant writings, but what part did they have in the Way of sincerity and singleness? No wonder achievements in governance languished and the guiding principles of the succession remained obscure.
Our Taizu founded the dynasty and handed down its succession, initiating it through learning of the mind; the successive sage emperors inherited the throne and maintained its institutions, transmitting it through learning of the mind thereafter. Thus the meaning of “sincerely hold fast to the mean” had long been obscured in the world, and only in the fifth year of Hongwu was it expounded clearly. The learning of sincerity and singleness, without division, had long been forgotten by later generations, and only at the Pavilion for Contemplating the Mind was it brought to prominence. Other examples include the Great Plan …

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
御註大學則
親覽尚書直指春秋直指以次而成聖學心法
周易大義更世而作一二百年天清地寧
民康物阜遺吾人以太平之盛者豈偶然
哉至我
皇上
首出庶物卓冠羣倫以
聖人之資居大寳之位道已至矣而憂勤惕厲
之恒存心已存矣而告戒箴規之罔怠覽
===
范浚之心箴有得則註而釋之心身主使
之說何其明而悉也讀程頤之四箴有悟
則分而解之動與禮合之言何其約而盡
也若夫敬一一箴則又道統淵源所繫聖
學終始所關首曰人有此心萬理咸具蓋
烝民之秉彛也而吾心之大原以闡繼曰
匪一弗純匪敬弗聚文王之緝熙也而存
心之要領以明曰政曰仁曰誠曰德言雖
殊矣而理未嘗不一曰畏曰勤曰肅曰慎
punctuated: 御註，《大學》則親覽；《尚書直指》、《春秋直指》以次而成，《聖學心法》、《周易大義》更世而作。一二百年，天清地寧，民康物阜，遺吾人以太平之盛者，豈偶然哉！至我皇上，首出庶物，卓冠羣倫，以聖人之資居大寳之位，道已至矣，而憂勤惕厲之恒存；心已存矣，而告戒箴規之罔怠。覽范浚之《心箴》，有得則註而釋之，心身主使之說，何其明而悉也！讀程頤之《四箴》，有悟則分而解之，動與禮合之言，何其約而盡也！若夫《敬一》一箴，則又道統淵源所繫、聖學終始所關。首曰：「人有此心，萬理咸具。」蓋烝民之秉彛也，而吾心之大原以闡。繼曰：「匪一弗純，匪敬弗聚。」文王之緝熙也，而存心之要領以明。曰政，曰仁，曰誠，曰德，言雖殊矣，而理未嘗不一；曰畏，曰勤，曰肅，曰慎，
translation_en:
…was imperially annotated, while the Great Learning was personally perused. Direct Guide to the Book of Documents and Direct Guide to the Spring and Autumn Annals were completed in succession; Methods of the Mind in Sagely Learning and Essential Meaning of the Changes of Zhou were composed across successive reigns. For one or two hundred years, Heaven has been clear and Earth tranquil, the people prosperous and goods abundant. Could it be mere chance that we have been bequeathed such flourishing peace?

Now our reigning emperor stands foremost among all beings, far surpassing his peers. With the endowments of a sage, he occupies the throne. His attainment of the Way is already consummate, yet his anxious diligence and vigilant self-discipline remain constant; his mind is already preserved, yet he never relaxes his attention to admonitions and precepts. Reading Fan Jun’s Admonition on the Mind, he gained insights and annotated and elucidated it. How clear and comprehensive is its account of the mind as the body’s ruler! Reading Cheng Yi’s Four Admonitions, he gained understanding and explained each separately. How concise yet exhaustive are its words on bringing action into accord with ritual propriety!

As for the single Admonition on Reverent Unity, it bears upon the very source of the transmission of the Way and concerns sagely learning from beginning to end. It opens: “Human beings possess this mind; within it all principles are complete.” This refers to the constant moral nature held by the people, and thereby elucidates the great source of our minds. It continues: “Without unity, there is no purity; without reverence, there is no gathering together.” This is King Wen’s unceasing cultivation of luminous virtue, and thereby makes clear the essentials of preserving the mind. It speaks of government, benevolence, sincerity, and virtue: though the words differ, their principle has never been other than one. It speaks of awe, diligence, solemnity, and caution…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
旨雖異也而功未嘗不同言天則嚴其心
之所自出言民則謹其心之所由施靜虛
無欲心之寂也左右輔弼心之感也萬邦
則王心之感也聖賢之所受授
祖宗之所述作會其全而無遺闡其妙而殆盡
豈尋常章句者可得而擬議之哉嗚呼盛
矣雖然漢申公有言曰爲治不在多言顧
力行何如耳愚也竊嘗聞而知之我
皇上自
===
繼統以來宵衣旰食示天下以勤制禮作樂示
天下以孝求賢重道示天下以文柔遠能
邇示天下以武要皆敬一之所發也則夫
登斯世于夏商周之上陋漢唐宋而不居
又奚以他求乎哉書曰念終始典于學詩
曰日就月將示我顯德行執事倘與進焉
敢執是以爲
廟堂獻
第二問
punctuated:
旨雖異也，而功未嘗不同。言天，則嚴其心之所自出；言民，則謹其心之所由施。靜虛無欲，心之寂也；左右輔弼，心之感也；萬邦則王，心之感也。聖賢之所受授，祖宗之所述作，會其全而無遺，闡其妙而殆盡，豈尋常章句者可得而擬議之哉！嗚呼，盛矣！雖然，漢申公有言曰：「爲治不在多言，顧力行何如耳。」愚也竊嘗聞而知之。我皇上自繼統以來，宵衣旰食，示天下以勤；制禮作樂，示天下以孝；求賢重道，示天下以文；柔遠能邇，示天下以武。要皆敬一之所發也。則夫登斯世于夏商周之上，陋漢唐宋而不居，又奚以他求乎哉？書曰：「念終始典于學。」詩曰：「日就月將，示我顯德行。」執事倘與進焉，敢執是以爲廟堂獻。

第二問
translation_en:
…Though their purports differ, the work they require has never been different. In speaking of Heaven, it reveres that from which the heart originates; in speaking of the people, it exercises care over that through which the heart puts its intentions into practice. Stillness, emptiness, and freedom from desire are the heart in repose; assistance from counselors on either side is the heart responding to things; reigning over the myriad states is likewise the heart responding to things. What the sages and worthies received and transmitted, and what the imperial ancestors expounded and composed—all is gathered together in its entirety, with nothing omitted, and its subtleties are elucidated almost exhaustively. How could ordinary scholars of textual phrases and sentences presume to assess it? Ah, how magnificent!

Nevertheless, Shen Gong of the Han said: “Governing does not depend on many words; it depends only on how one strives to put them into practice.” I, in my ignorance, have privately heard and come to understand this. Since succeeding to the imperial line, our Emperor has dressed before dawn and eaten only late in the day, displaying diligence to all under Heaven; established rites and composed music, displaying filial devotion; sought worthy men and honored the Way, displaying civil virtue; and conciliated those afar and brought those nearby into harmony, displaying martial virtue. In essence, all these proceed from single-minded reverence. To raise this age above the Xia, Shang, and Zhou, and to regard the Han, Tang, and Song as inadequate and refuse to rest at their level—what other means need be sought?

The Book of Documents says: “From beginning to end, keep your thoughts constantly on learning.” The Book of Odes says: “Advance daily and progress monthly; show me resplendent virtuous conduct.” If you, honored officials, would join in advancing toward this, I venture to offer these words to the imperial court.

Second Question

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
陳大壯
同考試官教諭馬　批　詞意婉轉引證詳明譬之
大河有源有委支流脉絡秩秩可觀末復致意於
昭代何其忠愛懇切也他日事業吾於此卜焉
同考試官教諭張　批　五策俱善條答經義一問
尤見考據精覈且議論閎博主司得此可以自慶矣
考試官主事袁　批　學以明經致用爲貴所謂明經
者非訓詁之謂也謂其能博古通今也此作縱橫出入識
見不凡必有用之學也首薦何疑
===
考試官主事蕭　批　周禮春秋周孔心術盡在於此
本自明白正大疑之補之穿鑿附會者世儒之陋也此作
無所因襲獨能發揮大旨而辭亦瑩邃讀之足以破
羣疑矣
聖人之道不明不行於天下非道之過也
學之者之失其傳也夫道之在天下如菽
粟水火之不可無而其明且行也如日之
麗天而水之行地曷嘗有疑而不信抑而
不尊者哉其所以不明不行者則由於學
punctuated:
陳大壯

同考試官教諭馬批：詞意婉轉，引證詳明。譬之大河，有源有委，支流脉絡秩秩可觀。末復致意於昭代，何其忠愛懇切也！他日事業，吾於此卜焉。

同考試官教諭張批：五策俱善，條答經義一問，尤見考據精覈，且議論閎博。主司得此，可以自慶矣。

考試官主事袁批：學以明經致用爲貴。所謂明經者，非訓詁之謂也，謂其能博古通今也。此作縱橫出入，識見不凡，必有用之學也。首薦何疑？

考試官主事蕭批：《周禮》《春秋》，周孔心術盡在於此，本自明白正大。疑之、補之、穿鑿附會者，世儒之陋也。此作無所因襲，獨能發揮大旨，而辭亦瑩邃，讀之足以破羣疑矣。

聖人之道不明不行於天下，非道之過也，學之者之失其傳也。夫道之在天下，如菽粟水火之不可無；而其明且行也，如日之麗天而水之行地。曷嘗有疑而不信、抑而不尊者哉？其所以不明不行者，則由於學
translation_en:
Chen Dazhuang

Comment by Associate Examiner Ma, Instructor: The expression and thought are graceful and subtle, and the supporting citations detailed and clear. It resembles a great river, with its source and outlet, its tributaries and connecting channels impressively ordered. At the end he again expresses his concern for our illustrious dynasty: how earnest his loyalty and devotion! From this I can foretell his future achievements.

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: All five policy essays are good. His point-by-point response to the question on the meaning of the Classics especially reveals precise and thorough examination of evidence, together with wide-ranging argument. The presiding examiners may congratulate themselves on obtaining such a work.

Comment by Examiner Yuan, Secretary: Learning is valued for illuminating the Classics and putting them to practical use. What is meant by illuminating the Classics is not merely explaining words: it means being broadly versed in antiquity and thoroughly understanding the present. This work ranges freely through its subject and displays uncommon insight. Such learning must have practical value. What doubt can there be about recommending him first?

Comment by Examiner Xiao, Secretary: The Rites of Zhou and the Spring and Autumn Annals contain the entire workings of the minds of the Duke of Zhou and Confucius. They are inherently clear, upright, and correct. To doubt them, supplement them, or subject them to strained interpretations and forced associations is the failing of commonplace scholars. This work follows no borrowed pattern, but independently brings out their central purport; its language is also lucid and profound. Reading it is enough to dispel the many doubts.

That the Way of the sages is neither understood nor practiced throughout the world is no fault of the Way; it is because those who study it have lost its transmission. The Way is as indispensable to the world as beans and grain, water and fire. Its illumination and practice are like the sun shining in heaven and water flowing over the earth. How could there ever be reason to doubt and distrust it, or disparage it and withhold reverence? The reason it is neither understood nor practiced thus lies with those who study …

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
之者之失其傳耳夫惟失其傳也是以衆
言淆亂而聖人之微言大義或幾乎息矣
不是之求而惟道之咎甚矣吾見其滋惑
也執事發策諸生若有疑於周禮春秋二
書者愚固知執事之引而不發也請條其
說夫周禮之作於周公春秋之筆削於孔
子雖五尺童子亦無疑者吾不意漢武之
好文何休之多識而乃致詆於周禮也一
則曰瀆亂不經之書一則曰戰國陰謀之
===
書是何其謬歟然彼自謬耳於周禮乎何
損吾又不意夫王安石之博聞慕古而乃
深譏夫春秋也曰此斷爛朝報耳是何其
悖歟然彼自悖耳於春秋乎何尤考工一
記此河間獻王之所補也殊不知司空一
職固已散見於五官之中矣而乃以百工
技藝之事補之續貂之陋朱子譏之當矣
黜周王魯此何休之所疑也殊不知所書
之王即平王也所爲之歷即周正也所稱
punctuated: 之者之失其傳耳。夫惟失其傳也，是以衆言淆亂，而聖人之微言大義或幾乎息矣。不是之求，而惟道之咎，甚矣，吾見其滋惑也！執事發策諸生，若有疑於《周禮》《春秋》二書者。愚固知執事之引而不發也，請條其說。夫《周禮》之作於周公，《春秋》之筆削於孔子，雖五尺童子亦無疑者。吾不意漢武之好文、何休之多識，而乃致詆於《周禮》也。一則曰「瀆亂不經之書」，一則曰「戰國陰謀之書」，是何其謬歟！然彼自謬耳，於《周禮》乎何損？吾又不意夫王安石之博聞慕古，而乃深譏夫《春秋》也，曰「此斷爛朝報耳」，是何其悖歟！然彼自悖耳，於《春秋》乎何尤？《考工》一記，此河間獻王之所補也。殊不知司空一職，固已散見於五官之中矣，而乃以百工技藝之事補之。續貂之陋，朱子譏之當矣。黜周王魯，此何休之所疑也。殊不知所書之王，即平王也；所爲之歷，即周正也；所稱
translation_en:
…because those who study it have lost its transmission. Precisely because this transmission has been lost, conflicting pronouncements sow confusion, and the subtle words and profound meaning of the sage have nearly fallen silent. Instead of seeking the cause here, they blame only the Way. How extreme this is! I see their confusion only increasing.

In presenting a policy question to the students, you, sir, appear to entertain doubts about the Rites of Zhou and the Spring and Autumn Annals. Yet I know that you are drawing the bow without releasing the arrow, leaving us to pursue the implications. Allow me to address the points in order. That the Duke of Zhou composed the Rites of Zhou, and that Confucius edited the Spring and Autumn Annals, are matters about which even a small child has no doubts. I would not have expected Emperor Wu of Han, with his love of letters, or He Xiu, with his extensive learning, to disparage the Rites of Zhou. One called it “a disorderly and irreverent book that violates canonical norms”; the other, “a book of Warring States intrigues.” How mistaken they were! Yet the error was theirs alone: what harm could it do to the Rites of Zhou?

Nor would I have expected Wang Anshi, with his broad learning and admiration for antiquity, to deride the Spring and Autumn Annals so severely, saying, “It is merely a fragmentary, tattered court bulletin.” How perverse! Yet the perversity was his alone: what fault could it establish in the Spring and Autumn Annals?

The Record of Artificers was supplied as a supplement by Prince Xian of Hejian. He failed to recognize that the duties of the Minister of Works were already described in passages scattered among the five ministries, and instead supplied an account of the skills and crafts of the various artisans. Master Zhu was right to criticize this inferior addition as an unworthy tail appended to sable fur.

Deposing Zhou and making Lu king: this was the interpretation entertained by He Xiu. He failed to recognize that the king recorded in the text was King Ping, and that the calendar it employed was the Zhou calendar, with its prescribed first month; the one it styled…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
之公即魯隱也安在其黜周而王魯乎素
王之說杜預辨之詳矣治周禮者始於劉
德立於劉歆傳於鄭康成是三子者其用
心亦勤矣然德之失在於補亡歆之失在
於輔莽而康成之失在於私意臆决旁据
曲證就而論之則鄭氏其最失乎觀其惑
於緯書泥於司馬法亦略可見矣春秋之
傳則左氏艶而富穀梁清而婉公羊辨而
裁是三家者其於道亦幾矣然左氏之失
===
也誣穀梁之失也短公羊之失也俗要而
論之則左氏其稍優乎觀其依經以辯理
錯經以合異亦略可推矣執事又謂
國家明經取士而周禮不列於學官
列聖崇儒右文而春秋不以進講是則有說矣
夫周禮之不列於學官蓋自漢已然矣虎
觀之校讎石渠之同異五經博士之置惟
易詩書春秋大戴小戴禮耳我
朝之不列於學官者非襲漢氏之陋也蓋禮
punctuated:
之公即魯隱也，安在其黜周而王魯乎？素王之說，杜預辨之詳矣。治周禮者，始於劉德，立於劉歆，傳於鄭康成。是三子者，其用心亦勤矣。然德之失在於補亡，歆之失在於輔莽，而康成之失在於私意臆决，旁据曲證。就而論之，則鄭氏其最失乎？觀其惑於緯書，泥於司馬法，亦略可見矣。春秋之傳，則左氏艶而富，穀梁清而婉，公羊辨而裁。是三家者，其於道亦幾矣。然左氏之失也誣，穀梁之失也短，公羊之失也俗。要而論之，則左氏其稍優乎？觀其依經以辯理，錯經以合異，亦略可推矣。
執事又謂：「國家明經取士，而周禮不列於學官；列聖崇儒右文，而春秋不以進講。」是則有說矣。夫周禮之不列於學官，蓋自漢已然矣。虎觀之校讎，石渠之同異，五經博士之置，惟易、詩、書、春秋、大戴、小戴禮耳。我朝之不列於學官者，非襲漢氏之陋也。蓋禮
translation_en:
…the duke referred to is Duke Yin of Lu. Where, then, is there any dethroning of Zhou and making Lu king? Du Yu has thoroughly refuted the theory of the “uncrowned king.” The study of the Rites of Zhou began with Liu De, was established by Liu Xin, and was transmitted by Zheng Kangcheng. These three men certainly applied themselves diligently. Yet De erred in supplying what was missing, Xin in assisting Wang Mang, and Kangcheng in making conjectural judgments according to his own notions, drawing on extraneous sources and straining evidence. Judged on these grounds, was Zheng perhaps the most mistaken? His being misled by the apocryphal writings and constrained by the Methods of the Minister of War (Sima fa) gives some indication of this. Among the commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, Zuo’s is ornate and abundant, Guliang’s lucid and subtle, and Gongyang’s discriminating and judicious. These three schools all came close to the Way. Yet Zuo’s fault is misrepresentation, Guliang’s insufficiency, and Gongyang’s vulgarity. On balance, might Zuo’s be somewhat superior? His reliance on the classic to explain principles, and his interweaving of its passages to reconcile discrepancies, give some grounds for this inference.
You further state: “The state selects men through their understanding of the classics, yet the Rites of Zhou is not included in official instruction; successive sage emperors have honored Confucian learning and esteemed letters, yet the Spring and Autumn Annals is not presented in lectures before the throne.” There is an explanation for this. The exclusion of the Rites of Zhou from official instruction goes back to the Han. In the textual collation at the Tiger Pavilion, the discussions of agreements and differences at the Stone Canal Pavilion, and the establishment of Erudites of the Five Classics, there were only the Changes, Odes, Documents, Spring and Autumn Annals, and the ritual texts of the Elder Dai and Younger Dai. Our dynasty’s exclusion of it from official instruction does not perpetuate a shortcoming of the Han. For the Book of Rites…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
記之王制尚書之周官皆周禮也又何必
並列而後爲重乎春秋之不以進講蓋自
王安石始耳貢舉不以取士庠序不以設
官經筵不以進讀而國是無所折衷矣我
朝之不以進講者非踵王氏之失也蓋五經
之立配之五行而取士之科固治春秋也
又何待進講而後爲重乎雖然程子有言
有關雎麟趾之意而後可以行周官之法
度我
===
國家稽古建官一放乎周官之意而損益之
師其意不泥其迹此則善用周禮者也不
然雖列之學官無益也董子有言有國者
不可以不知春秋前有讒而不見後有賊
而不知爲人臣者不可以不知春秋守經
事而不知其宜遭變事而不知其權今
天子文武聖神垂情於治亂興衰之故若春秋
者雖以之進講可也夫周禮可以師其意
矣而儀禮乃禮經之經也獨無可采者歟
punctuated:
記之《王制》、尚書之《周官》，皆周禮也，又何必並列而後爲重乎？春秋之不以進講，蓋自王安石始耳。貢舉不以取士，庠序不以設官，經筵不以進讀，而國是無所折衷矣。我朝之不以進講者，非踵王氏之失也。蓋五經之立，配之五行，而取士之科固治春秋也，又何待進講而後爲重乎？雖然，程子有言：「有關雎、麟趾之意，而後可以行周官之法度。」
我國家稽古建官，一放乎周官之意而損益之，師其意，不泥其迹，此則善用周禮者也。不然，雖列之學官，無益也。董子有言：「有國者不可以不知春秋，前有讒而不見，後有賊而不知；爲人臣者不可以不知春秋，守經事而不知其宜，遭變事而不知其權。」今天子文武聖神，垂情於治亂興衰之故，若春秋者，雖以之進講可也。夫周禮可以師其意矣，而儀禮乃禮經之經也，獨無可采者歟？
translation_en:
…the “Royal Regulations” chapter of the Record of Rites and the “Offices of Zhou” chapter of the Book of Documents both embody the rites of Zhou. Why must the Rites of Zhou also be included alongside them before it can be accorded importance? The exclusion of the Spring and Autumn Annals from lectures before the emperor began with Wang Anshi. It was not used to select men through the examinations; no teaching posts were established for it in the schools; and it was not read at the Classics Colloquium. Thus, state policy had no standard by which to adjudicate right and wrong. Our dynasty’s exclusion of it from imperial lectures does not perpetuate Wang’s error. The establishment of the Five Classics corresponds to the Five Phases, and the examinations for selecting men certainly include specialization in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Why, then, must it await inclusion in imperial lectures before being accorded importance? Nevertheless, Master Cheng said: “Only when one possesses the spirit of ‘Guanju’ (‘The Ospreys’) and ‘Linzhi’ (‘The Qilin’s Hooves’) can one implement the laws and institutions of the Offices of Zhou.”
In establishing its offices through study of antiquity, our dynasty has wholly followed the intent of the Offices of Zhou, making appropriate additions and reductions. It takes that intent as its model without clinging rigidly to its outward forms: this is skillful use of the Rites of Zhou. Otherwise, even including it in the official curriculum would be of no benefit. Master Dong said: “Those who possess a state cannot afford to be ignorant of the Spring and Autumn Annals: [without such knowledge,] slander confronts them and they do not see it; traitors lurk behind them and they do not know it. Those who serve as ministers cannot afford to be ignorant of the Spring and Autumn Annals: [without such knowledge,] in handling ordinary affairs they do not know what is appropriate, and when confronted with exceptional circumstances they do not know how to adapt.” Our present Son of Heaven, accomplished in civil and military affairs, sagely and divinely perceptive, directs his attention to the causes of order and disorder, rise and decline. A work such as the Spring and Autumn Annals could therefore well be presented in lectures before him. Now, the intent of the Rites of Zhou may be taken as a model; yet the Ceremonies and Rites is the very canon of the ritual classics. Can it alone contain nothing worthy of adoption?

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
春秋可以進講矣而綱目亦春秋之翼也
獨無可取者歟書生之見如此不識執事
者以爲何如也
第三問
張爊
同考試官教諭林　批〔酌古準今鑿鑿可行此必有用世之志者〕
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔氣昌詞健如探囊取物隨取隨有非積蓄深厚者恐不能到〕
同考試官學正梁　批〔通變神明非可以輕議者此作語有剛韓鍊之取爾〕
===
考試官主事袁　批〔策士正欲觀其才識此作議論滂洽綜理周悉其才識可知矣〕
考試官主事蕭　批〔養用人才處籌度精密甚熟於世故者與〕
人才之在天下不患其不足用而患乎用
之不得其道養之豫而求之廣擇之精而
任之專有鼓舞之機焉有奔走之術焉有
punctuated:
春秋可以進講矣，而綱目亦春秋之翼也，獨無可取者歟？書生之見如此，不識執事者以爲何如也。

第三問
張爊
同考試官教諭林　批〔酌古準今，鑿鑿可行，此必有用世之志者。〕
同考試官教諭鄭　批〔氣昌詞健，如探囊取物，隨取隨有，非積蓄深厚者恐不能到。〕
同考試官學正梁　批〔通變神明，非可以輕議者。此作語有剛韓鍊之取爾。〕
考試官主事袁　批〔策士正欲觀其才識，此作議論滂洽，綜理周悉，其才識可知矣。〕
考試官主事蕭　批〔養用人才處，籌度精密，甚熟於世故者與？〕

人才之在天下，不患其不足用，而患乎用之不得其道。養之豫而求之廣，擇之精而任之專，有鼓舞之機焉，有奔走之術焉，有
translation_en:
The Spring and Autumn Annals may indeed be expounded before the emperor; but the Outline and Details (Gangmu), too, is a complement to the Spring and Autumn Annals. Does it alone contain nothing worth adopting? Such are this scholar’s views; I do not know what you, the officials presiding over this examination, will think of them.

Third policy question
Zhang Ao

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Instructor: 〔He weighs antiquity against present circumstances; his proposals are demonstrably practicable. This must be someone resolved to serve the world.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Zheng, Instructor: 〔His spirit is exuberant and his diction vigorous. Like someone reaching into a bag for an object, he finds whatever he reaches for. I fear that none without deep and substantial stores of learning could attain this level.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, School Director: 〔Adapting to change with inspired understanding is no matter for casual discussion. The language of this composition has a forceful, refined quality worthy of selection [?].〕

Comment by Examiner Yuan, Secretary: 〔The very purpose of examining scholars through policy questions is to observe their ability and discernment. This composition’s arguments are extensive and well informed, and its treatment comprehensive and thorough: the author’s ability and discernment are evident.〕

Comment by Examiner Xiao, Secretary: 〔In discussing the nurturing and employment of talent, his calculations are meticulous and precise. Is he not someone thoroughly versed in worldly affairs?〕

As for talented people in the world, the concern is not that there are too few to employ, but that they are employed improperly. Nurture them in advance and seek them widely; select them carefully and entrust them with undivided responsibility. There are means of inspiring them, methods of setting them energetically to work, and there are…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
綜覈之實焉如是而曰人才不足用如是
而曰今之人才不如古人吾不信也請以
是爲明問復夫今之人才豈惟有媿於唐
虞三代視漢唐宋亦有間矣且今之賢良
方正者誰歟明經詞賦者誰歟至於律曆
卜算農官水利非惟無其人而其學殆且
廢矣方其平居無事則羣聚而試於有司
其待次於都下者蓋不特數千人而已也
所謂一官而三人共之者豈虛語哉及遇
===
警急則倉皇畏縮一無可否求其發謀出
慮輸力效忠斷斷乎可以隨用隨効者蓋
鮮矣此秉鈞衡者之所以有乏人廢事之
嘆也說者乃歸咎於糊名易書之制不如
鄉舉里選之善夫以一日之長而欲觀其
終身之實誠若有可議者然今之所謂豪
傑者大抵出於科目耳謂糊名易書不足
以得人者非也乃若鄉舉里選之法惟成
周爲能行之至漢則不然矣蓋所謂鄉舉
punctuated: 綜覈之實焉。如是而曰人才不足用，如是而曰今之人才不如古人，吾不信也。請以是爲明問復。夫今之人才，豈惟有媿於唐虞三代？視漢唐宋亦有間矣。且今之賢良方正者誰歟？明經詞賦者誰歟？至於律曆卜算、農官水利，非惟無其人，而其學殆且廢矣。方其平居無事，則羣聚而試於有司；其待次於都下者，蓋不特數千人而已也。所謂一官而三人共之者，豈虛語哉？及遇警急，則倉皇畏縮，一無可否。求其發謀出慮、輸力效忠，斷斷乎可以隨用隨効者，蓋鮮矣。此秉鈞衡者之所以有乏人廢事之嘆也。說者乃歸咎於糊名易書之制，不如鄉舉里選之善。夫以一日之長而欲觀其終身之實，誠若有可議者。然今之所謂豪傑者，大抵出於科目耳。謂糊名易書不足以得人者，非也。乃若鄉舉里選之法，惟成周爲能行之，至漢則不然矣。蓋所謂鄉舉
translation_en:
…and there is substantive scrutiny of their performance. If, with all this, someone says that talented men are insufficient for service, or that today’s talented men do not measure up to those of antiquity, I do not believe it. Allow me to offer this in reply to your discerning question.

As for today’s talented men, do they fall short only of those of the ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties? Even compared with those of the Han, Tang, and Song, they stand at some distance. Who today are the worthy and upright? Who are those proficient in the Classics or in literary composition? As for pitch standards and calendrical calculation, divination and computation, agricultural administration and water conservancy, not only are there no qualified men: these branches of learning themselves are almost abandoned. In ordinary times, when nothing is amiss, men gather in crowds to be examined by the responsible authorities. Those awaiting their turn for appointment in the capital number more than merely several thousand. Can the saying that three men share a single office be empty talk? Yet when an emergency arises, they become flustered and shrink back, unable to decide anything. Few indeed can devise plans, offer considered counsel, exert themselves in loyal service, and be relied upon to produce results whenever employed. This is why those who hold the reins of government lament that duties go unfulfilled for want of men.

Some commentators blame the system of concealing candidates’ names and recopying their scripts, claiming that it is inferior to recommendation and selection through local communities. To seek to judge a man’s lifelong substance by the ability he displays on a single day does indeed seem open to criticism. Yet those now called outstanding men have, for the most part, emerged through the examinations. It is wrong to say that concealing names and recopying scripts cannot secure capable men. As for the method of local recommendation and selection, only the Zhou in its flourishing age could put it into practice; by the Han, this was no longer so. For what was called local recommendation…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
里選者無亦因人之毁譽而爲低昂耳彼
劉毅之所謂中正八損者庸可恃乎上下
相欺名實相眩非惟其勢有所不可而其
法亦難以相信矣謂鄉舉里選盡足以得
人者誠迂也夫糊名易書之制乃我
聖祖
神宗斟酌損益以立萬世不刊之典而可以輕
議也哉執事必欲變而通之使今之人才
卓如古昔無已則舉制科耳行辟薦耳重
===
師儒耳議資格耳夫以經義取士是矣然
習經義而不通時變無乃流而爲學究乎
請於科目之外略倣宋人制科之意或九
年一舉或六年一舉嚴立章程定爲規制
如宏詞博學如陰陽技藝如甲兵錢穀皆
得以專門應制或京朝官或有司或學士
弟子員或布衣韋帶之士皆得以所長自
售不惟其類惟其人吾見上以是求下以
是應如是而異才不出者吾不信也夫以
punctuated:
里選者，無亦因人之毁譽而爲低昂耳。彼劉毅之所謂中正八損者，庸可恃乎？上下相欺，名實相眩，非惟其勢有所不可，而其法亦難以相信矣。謂鄉舉里選盡足以得人者，誠迂也。夫糊名易書之制，乃我聖祖神宗斟酌損益，以立萬世不刊之典，而可以輕議也哉？執事必欲變而通之，使今之人才卓如古昔，無已，則舉制科耳，行辟薦耳，重師儒耳，議資格耳。

夫以經義取士，是矣。然習經義而不通時變，無乃流而爲學究乎？請於科目之外，略倣宋人制科之意，或九年一舉，或六年一舉，嚴立章程，定爲規制。如宏詞博學，如陰陽技藝，如甲兵錢穀，皆得以專門應制。或京朝官，或有司，或學士弟子員，或布衣韋帶之士，皆得以所長自售。不惟其類，惟其人。吾見上以是求，下以是應，如是而異才不出者，吾不信也。夫以
translation_en:
…selection within local communities amounts, perhaps, merely to raising or lowering candidates according to others’ praise and disparagement. Could the rectifiers, with the eight defects of which Liu Yi spoke, possibly be relied upon? Superiors and subordinates deceive one another; reputation and reality become confused. Not only do circumstances make such a system impracticable in some respects, but its procedures also make mutual trust difficult. To claim that recommendation by districts and selection within local communities are wholly adequate to obtain worthy men is truly unrealistic. The system of concealing candidates’ names and recopying their scripts was established by our Sagely Founder and Divine Ancestor [?], after weighing what to retain and what to amend, as an immutable institution for all ages. How could it be lightly criticized? If you, sir, insist on adapting it so that it works effectively, making the talented men of today as outstanding as those of antiquity, then, if changes must be made, hold special examinations by imperial decree, institute recruitment and recommendation, give greater weight to Confucian teachers, and reconsider eligibility requirements.

Selecting men through essays on the meaning of the Classics is indeed right. Yet if they practise such essays without understanding changing circumstances, will they not degenerate into mere pedants? I propose that, outside the regular examinations, we broadly follow the intent of the special examinations held under the Song, conducting them once every nine years or once every six years, establishing strict regulations and making these a settled system. Whether their specialties are elegant composition and broad learning, yin-yang studies and technical arts, or military affairs and fiscal administration, candidates should all be permitted to respond to the imperial summons in their particular fields. Whether officials at the capital and court, officials in administrative posts, scholars and registered students, or men in commoners’ cloth robes and plain belts, all should be allowed to present themselves on the strength of their particular abilities. Consider the individual, rather than merely his category. As I see it, if those above seek men in this way and those below respond accordingly, I cannot believe that exceptional talent would fail to emerge. Now, to use…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
科目待士足矣然取文藝而不采行義無
乃晉而爲浮靡乎請於制科之外議爲辟
薦之典撫臣責之監司監司責之守令訪
之嚴穴參之縉紳有道德隆重者有孝弟
力田者有行義潔脩者有問學淵深者則
稽其實蹟其名以
聞或一省一人焉或數省一人焉或通天下而
一人焉而又必以賢才之多寡爲司府之
殿最隱匿者有罰冒濫者有罰不惟其數
===
惟其人吾見上有好者下必有甚焉者矣
如是而人不競勸者吾亦不信也今之所
謂師儒者國學則大司成也鄉校則小學
正也而督學者則憲臣也司成尊官憲臣
要職其重也久矣惟司鄉校者官守既卑
禮待甚薄其間能自振拔者什之一二耳
彼方以上之人不加優異而亦甘心於自棄
也是以職業不脩絃誦不聞甚則黌校鞠
爲疏闊者有矣請自今以往銓除之必慎
punctuated:
科目待士足矣，然取文藝而不采行義，無乃晉而爲浮靡乎？請於制科之外，議爲辟薦之典。撫臣責之監司，監司責之守令，訪之嚴穴，參之縉紳。有道德隆重者，有孝弟力田者，有行義潔脩者，有問學淵深者，則稽其實，蹟其名以聞。或一省一人焉，或數省一人焉，或通天下而一人焉。而又必以賢才之多寡爲司府之殿最。隱匿者有罰，冒濫者有罰。不惟其數，惟其人。吾見上有好者，下必有甚焉者矣。如是而人不競勸者，吾亦不信也。
今之所謂師儒者，國學則大司成也，鄉校則小學正也，而督學者則憲臣也。司成尊官，憲臣要職，其重也久矣。惟司鄉校者，官守既卑，禮待甚薄，其間能自振拔者什之一二耳。彼方以上之人不加優異，而亦甘心於自棄也。是以職業不脩，絃誦不聞，甚則黌校鞠爲疏闊者有矣。請自今以往，銓除之必慎。
translation_en:
…The regular examinations suffice as a means of engaging scholars. Yet if literary accomplishment is selected while moral conduct is disregarded, will this not lead to frivolity and extravagance [?]? I propose that, alongside the special examinations, procedures for recruitment and recommendation be established. Provincial governors should charge the surveillance officials with this responsibility, and the surveillance officials should charge the prefects and magistrates. They should seek candidates among those dwelling in caves as recluses [?] and consult members of the official gentry. Where there are men of eminent moral virtue, men who show filial piety and fraternal respect and diligently cultivate the fields, men of pure and cultivated conduct, or men of profound learning, their actual merits should be investigated and their names recorded [?] for submission to the throne. There might be one such man in a province, one in several provinces, or just one throughout the empire. Moreover, the number of worthy and talented men found must serve as a basis for assessing the provincial commissions and prefectures as inferior or superior. Those who conceal worthy men should be punished, as should those who make fraudulent or indiscriminate recommendations. The concern should be the men themselves, rather than their number. I observe that when those above favor something, those below invariably pursue it still more ardently. I cannot believe that, under such arrangements, people would fail to compete in striving to improve.
Those now called teachers of classical learning are, in the National University, the Chancellor; in local schools, the minor school instructors; and those who supervise education are censorial officials. The Chancellor holds an honored office, and the censorial officials occupy important posts: their standing has long been high. Only those in charge of local schools hold lowly offices and receive very scant courtesy. Among them, merely one or two in ten can rouse themselves to rise above their circumstances. Because their superiors confer no special favor or distinction upon them, they too willingly abandon their own aspirations. Consequently, their duties go unattended, and the sounds of strings and recitation are unheard. In extreme cases, schools have even fallen into neglect and desolation [?]. I propose that henceforth particular care must be taken in selecting and appointing them…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
禮待之必優教授則以進士爲之學正教
諭則以舉人爲之訓導則以貢士爲之其
稱職者則稍加優異不次超遷如是則師
儒重而人才衆盛矣今之所謂資格者科
目也例貢也吏役也科目正途其重也久
矣惟例貢吏役局於流品限於資格其間
能自奮立者百之一二耳彼方以上之人
槩無甄別而絶意於進取也是以廉恥不
立簠簋不飾甚則奴隸而呵斥之者有矣
===
請自今以往不以流品爲高下而以賢否
爲低昂拔吏役之稱職者躋之例貢之上
拔例貢之稱職者列之科目之間如是則
資格定而官方得人矣夫此固非紛更變
法也四者之中惟制科非
祖宗之法耳然所謂制科者非廢科目也謂與
科目並行也乃若辟薦之典師儒之重資
格之議則
先朝有故事矣
punctuated:
禮待之必優。教授則以進士爲之，學正、教諭則以舉人爲之，訓導則以貢士爲之。其稱職者，則稍加優異，不次超遷。如是，則師儒重而人才衆盛矣。今之所謂資格者，科目也，例貢也，吏役也。科目正途，其重也久矣。惟例貢、吏役，局於流品，限於資格，其間能自奮立者，百之一二耳。彼方以上之人槩無甄別，而絶意於進取也。是以廉恥不立，簠簋不飾，甚則奴隸而呵斥之者有矣。
請自今以往，不以流品爲高下，而以賢否爲低昂。拔吏役之稱職者，躋之例貢之上；拔例貢之稱職者，列之科目之間。如是，則資格定而官方得人矣。夫此固非紛更變法也。四者之中，惟制科非祖宗之法耳。然所謂制科者，非廢科目也，謂與科目並行也。乃若辟薦之典、師儒之重、資格之議，則先朝有故事矣。
translation_en:
…and they must be accorded generous ceremonial treatment. Professors should be appointed from among metropolitan graduates (jinshi); School Directors and Instructors from among provincial graduates (juren); and Assistant Instructors from among tribute students. Those who discharge their duties well should receive progressively greater distinction and promotion beyond the normal sequence. In this way, scholarly teachers will be held in esteem, and talented men will flourish in abundance. What are now called categories of eligibility comprise those entering through the examinations, tribute students admitted under special regulations, and clerical personnel. The examinations constitute the regular path to office and have long enjoyed prestige. Tribute students admitted under special regulations and clerical personnel, however, are confined by their category of entry and restricted by their eligibility status. Among them, only one or two in a hundred can rouse themselves to achieve an independent standing. Believing that their superiors make no distinctions among them, they abandon all thought of advancement. Consequently, they fail to cultivate integrity and a sense of shame, and their conduct in office is corrupt. Some are even treated as slaves and subjected to angry rebukes.
I ask that henceforth men should not be ranked higher or lower according to their category of entry, but advanced or demoted according to their worth. Promote clerical personnel who discharge their duties well above tribute students admitted under special regulations; promote capable men among these tribute students into the ranks of those who entered through the examinations. Thus eligibility will be properly ordered, and suitable men will fill official posts. These proposals certainly do not amount to disruptive changes in established institutions. Of the four measures, only special examinations fall outside the institutions of the imperial ancestors. Yet by special examinations I do not mean abolishing the regular examinations; I mean conducting them alongside the regular examinations. As for the practice of recruitment by invitation and recommendation, the esteem accorded scholarly teachers, and the reconsideration of eligibility, there are precedents from earlier reigns.

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
國初如宋濂如劉基非辟召之尤者乎如宋
訥如胡儼非師儒之箸者乎乃若以吏役
至卿佐者如楊時習況鍾之徒不可悉數
孰謂其不足以得人乎夫重師儒則養之
豫矣開制科則求之廣矣舉辟薦則擇之
精矣議資格則任之專矣率是以鼓舞申
才奔走豪傑而又加之以綜核之實吾見
今日之人才雖躋之三代可也而何漢唐
宋之云哉夫所謂綜核者非督責之謂也
===
循名以求其實稽事以考其成旌別以興
其耻黜陟以作其懦敦本實而抑浮華奬
直節而察顯譽凡所謂疑心而任耳目者
一切不行而必以至公至明臨之務使上
下相安莫有因循苟且之意如是則雖不
舉制科可也不行辟薦可也不重師儒可
也不議資格可也而人才自興矣不此之
務而徒紛更於法制之間是不琢玉而求
文采也亦何益之有哉吾固曰不患其不
punctuated:
國初，如宋濂、如劉基，非辟召之尤者乎？如宋訥、如胡儼，非師儒之箸者乎？乃若以吏役至卿佐者，如楊時習、況鍾之徒，不可悉數，孰謂其不足以得人乎？夫重師儒，則養之豫矣；開制科，則求之廣矣；舉辟薦，則擇之精矣；議資格，則任之專矣。率是以鼓舞申才，奔走豪傑，而又加之以綜核之實，吾見今日之人才，雖躋之三代可也，而何漢、唐、宋之云哉！

夫所謂綜核者，非督責之謂也。循名以求其實，稽事以考其成，旌別以興其耻，黜陟以作其懦，敦本實而抑浮華，奬直節而察顯譽。凡所謂疑心而任耳目者，一切不行，而必以至公至明臨之，務使上下相安，莫有因循苟且之意。如是，則雖不舉制科可也，不行辟薦可也，不重師儒可也，不議資格可也，而人才自興矣。不此之務，而徒紛更於法制之間，是不琢玉而求文采也，亦何益之有哉！吾固曰：不患其不
translation_en:
At the beginning of the dynasty, were men such as Song Lian and Liu Ji not outstanding examples of recruitment by summons? Were men such as Song Ne and Hu Yan not distinguished scholar-teachers? As for those who rose from clerical service to become ministers and assistant ministers, men such as Yang Shixi and Kuang Zhong are too numerous to enumerate. Who could say that these methods are insufficient to secure worthy men? Honoring scholar-teachers prepares men of talent in advance; instituting special examinations broadens the search for them; employing summons and recommendation makes their selection more discerning; reconsidering qualifications for office makes their appointment more focused. By these means, we may encourage and advance talent [?] and bring outstanding men into service. If we also add genuine, comprehensive scrutiny of performance, I believe that the talented men of today could rank alongside those of the Three Dynasties. Why speak merely of the Han, Tang, or Song?

What I call comprehensive scrutiny does not mean exacting compliance through harsh demands. It means seeking actual performance corresponding to nominal duties, examining affairs to assess accomplishments, distinguishing merit to awaken a sense of shame, and using dismissal and promotion to rouse the timid. It means strengthening substance and suppressing superficial display, rewarding upright integrity and scrutinizing conspicuous reputations. All practices of harboring suspicions and relying on informants must be rejected; officials must instead be overseen with the utmost impartiality and discernment. Every effort should be made to ensure that superiors and subordinates are at ease with one another, with none inclined to drift along or muddle through. If this is done, it will be acceptable even without holding special examinations, employing summons and recommendation, giving particular weight to scholar-teachers, or reconsidering qualifications for office: talented men will arise of themselves. To neglect this task and merely keep altering laws and institutions is to seek beautiful patterns in jade without carving it. What benefit could there be in that? Thus I have maintained: the concern is not that they are not…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
足用而患乎用之不得其道也
第四問
胡經
同考試官教諭李　批〔弭災致變要在脩德而已〕
吾子惓惓致重於此其亦知要者耶
考試官主事袁　批〔說天心仁愛之意甚懇切〕
考試官主事蕭　批〔意婉而文亦順敘可謂善言〕
天矣
災異之來可憂也亦可喜也何也乖氣致
戾和氣致祥災異之來固未有無因而至
者如之何其勿憂也然天之所以告戒乎
我者容詎知其非仁愛乎我也哉知此則
可憂者未必不可喜而所以反災爲祥者
固有在人而不在天者矣彼以災異爲不
足憂者固不足責而惑於氣數拘於事應
者亦豈足以知天人相與之際哉執事有
感於今日之災異而以消弭之術下詢予
學愚也何足以知之姑舉其所知者以對
punctuated:
足用，而患乎用之不得其道也。

第四問
胡經

同考試官教諭李　批〔弭災致變，要在脩德而已〕吾子惓惓致重於此，其亦知要者耶！
考試官主事袁　批〔說天心仁愛之意甚懇切〕
考試官主事蕭　批〔意婉而文亦順敘，可謂善言〕天矣。

災異之來，可憂也，亦可喜也。何也？乖氣致戾，和氣致祥。災異之來，固未有無因而至者，如之何其勿憂也？然天之所以告戒乎我者，容詎知其非仁愛乎我也哉？知此，則可憂者未必不可喜，而所以反災爲祥者，固有在人而不在天者矣。彼以災異爲不足憂者，固不足責；而惑於氣數、拘於事應者，亦豈足以知天人相與之際哉？執事有感於今日之災異，而以消弭之術下詢予，學愚也，何足以知之？姑舉其所知者以對。
translation_en:
…that they are sufficient for service, but that they are not employed in the proper way.

Fourth Policy Question
Hu Jing

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “The essential means of averting disasters and bringing about change [?] lies solely in cultivating virtue.” You repeatedly place great emphasis on this; surely you understand what is essential!

Comment by Examiner Yuan, Secretary: “His explanation of Heaven’s benevolent and loving intentions is deeply earnest.”

Comment by Examiner Xiao, Secretary: “The meaning is gently expressed, and the writing proceeds smoothly; he may be said to speak well of Heaven.”

The arrival of disasters and anomalies is cause for concern, but also cause for joy. Why? Discordant vital forces bring calamity; harmonious vital forces bring auspicious signs. Disasters and anomalies never arrive without a cause: how could we fail to be concerned? Yet when Heaven thereby admonishes us, how can we know that this is not an expression of its benevolent love for us? Once we understand this, what causes concern need not be incapable of bringing joy. The means of turning disaster into auspiciousness indeed lie with human beings rather than with Heaven. Those who regard disasters and anomalies as no cause for concern are scarcely worth reproaching. But those who are misled by the cycles of cosmic forces and fate, or bound by correspondences between events and portents, can hardly understand the interaction of Heaven and humanity either. Moved by the disasters and anomalies of the present day, you have condescended to ask me how they may be dispelled. Ignorant as I am in my learning [?], how could I understand this adequately? I shall nevertheless offer what I know in reply.

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
昔者楚莊王以國無災異禱於山川曰此
天忘我而孔子之作春秋也如日食不雨
星隕大水之類皆存而弗削至祥瑞則削
而弗錄此其意可想也是以有天下者不
取必於或然之數而求盡夫當然之道不
求之天而求之人憂勤惕厲恐懼脩省曷
嘗敢一毫放肆也哉夫脩玄德而祥桑枯
死此殷大戊之可稱者也發善言而熒惑
退舍此宋景公之可錄者也豈惟二君爲
===
然堯嘗有九年之水矣而拳拳於四岳之
咨則堯之所以事天者何如也湯嘗有七
年之旱矣而懇懇於六事之責則湯之所
以事天者何如也吾獨惜夫董仲舒之善
言天人而猶惑於氣數也觀其火災之對
述春秋兩觀亳社桓僖二宮之災以証高
園便殿之失其用意非不深且切也但拘
於某事應某事則其義迂矣其後淮南衡
山之獄株連蔓引得非仲舒啓之歟乃若
punctuated: 昔者，楚莊王以國無災異，禱於山川曰：「此天忘我！」而孔子之作《春秋》也，如日食、不雨、星隕、大水之類，皆存而弗削；至祥瑞，則削而弗錄。此其意可想也。是以有天下者，不取必於或然之數，而求盡夫當然之道；不求之天，而求之人。憂勤惕厲，恐懼脩省，曷嘗敢一毫放肆也哉！夫脩玄德而祥桑枯死，此殷大戊之可稱者也；發善言而熒惑退舍，此宋景公之可錄者也。豈惟二君爲然？堯嘗有九年之水矣，而拳拳於四岳之咨，則堯之所以事天者何如也？湯嘗有七年之旱矣，而懇懇於六事之責，則湯之所以事天者何如也？吾獨惜夫董仲舒之善言天人，而猶惑於氣數也。觀其火災之對，述《春秋》兩觀、亳社、桓僖二宮之災，以証高園便殿之失，其用意非不深且切也。但拘於某事應某事，則其義迂矣。其後淮南、衡山之獄，株連蔓引，得非仲舒啓之歟？乃若
translation_en:
In former times, King Zhuang of Chu, because his state had suffered no calamities or anomalies, prayed to the mountains and rivers, saying, “Heaven has forgotten me!” When Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, he retained without deletion such occurrences as solar eclipses, failures of rain, falling stars, and great floods; auspicious portents, however, he removed and did not record. His intention in this can readily be understood. Thus, those who possess All-under-Heaven do not seek certainty in contingent workings of fate, but strive to fulfill the Way of what ought to be done. They seek the remedy not in Heaven but in human affairs. Anxious and diligent, vigilant and circumspect, fearful and devoted to self-cultivation and self-examination—when would they ever dare indulge themselves in the slightest?

By cultivating profound virtue, Taiwu of Yin caused the portentous mulberry tree to wither and die: this is what merits praise in him. By uttering good words, Duke Jing of Song caused Mars to retreat from its celestial station: this is what merits recording in him. Yet were these two rulers alone in acting thus? Yao once endured nine years of flooding, and earnestly sought counsel from the Four Marchmounts. What does this tell us about how Yao served Heaven? Tang once endured seven years of drought, and sincerely reproached himself on six matters. What does this tell us about how Tang served Heaven?

I regret only that Dong Zhongshu, though skilled in discussing Heaven and humanity, remained confused by theories of cosmic forces and allotted fate. Consider his response concerning the fire: he recounted the calamities recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals at the two gate towers, the Bo Altar of the Soil, and the two ancestral temples of Dukes Huan and Xi, using them to demonstrate the fault associated with the auxiliary hall at Gao’s mausoleum park. His intention was indeed profound and directly pertinent. Yet by insisting that a particular event corresponded to another particular event, he made his interpretation strained. Later, the cases against Huainan and Hengshan implicated ever-widening circles of people. Could it not have been Zhongshu who opened the way to this? As for…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
宣帝之厲精圖治而史臣之紀災異獨爲
最詳者盖深有取夫宣帝之綜核名實克
謹天戒以爲災異雖多固無害其中興之
治也然而申韓雜用刑名繩下卒之啓三
大釁者得非宣帝之過歟今
聖天子敬
天法祖親賢遠奸固宜其休徵滋至而災異滅
息矣夫何邇年以來旱潦則不時矣風霾
則屢作矣日食地震星殞火災亦旣相仍
===
矣是豈乖氣之相感歟盖天之仁愛我
君其意固有攸在而執事必欲求夫弭災救變
之術則竊有說焉夫徧走羣望此禜禳之
末節耳戒飭百工此粉飾之虛文耳反災
爲祥之術果在是乎昔宋儒真德秀有言
祥多而自恃者未必不危異衆而知懼者
未必不安顧人主所以應之者何如耳然
則洪範庶徵之說月令五行之應其今日
之所當致意者乎乃若開言路以來諫諍
punctuated: 宣帝之厲精圖治，而史臣之紀災異獨爲最詳者，盖深有取夫宣帝之綜核名實，克謹天戒，以爲災異雖多，固無害其中興之治也。然而申韓雜用，刑名繩下，卒之啓三大釁者，得非宣帝之過歟？今聖天子敬天法祖，親賢遠奸，固宜其休徵滋至而災異滅息矣。夫何邇年以來，旱潦則不時矣，風霾則屢作矣，日食、地震、星殞、火災亦旣相仍矣！是豈乖氣之相感歟？盖天之仁愛我君，其意固有攸在，而執事必欲求夫弭災救變之術，則竊有說焉。夫徧走羣望，此禜禳之末節耳；戒飭百工，此粉飾之虛文耳。反災爲祥之術，果在是乎？昔宋儒真德秀有言：「祥多而自恃者，未必不危；異衆而知懼者，未必不安。顧人主所以應之者何如耳。」然則《洪範》庶徵之說，《月令》五行之應，其今日之所當致意者乎？乃若開言路以來諫諍
translation_en:
…Emperor Xuan devoted himself strenuously to good government, yet the court historians recorded the calamities and anomalies of his reign in exceptional detail. This was surely because they greatly valued his thorough scrutiny of names and actual performance and his conscientious heed to Heaven’s warnings. They considered that, numerous though the calamities and anomalies were, these did not detract from the good government of his dynastic restoration. Yet he also employed the teachings of Shen Buhai and Han Fei, using penal methods and the matching of performance to official claims to constrain his subordinates, ultimately opening the way to three great troubles. Was this not Emperor Xuan’s fault?

Now our sagely Son of Heaven reveres Heaven and follows the example of his ancestors, draws close to the worthy and keeps the wicked at a distance. Surely auspicious signs ought therefore to arrive in growing numbers, and calamities and anomalies to cease. Why, then, in recent years have droughts and floods occurred out of season, violent winds and dust storms repeatedly arisen, and solar eclipses, earthquakes, falling stars, and fires followed one another? Could these be the effects of mutually resonating discordant forces? Surely Heaven has a purpose in its benevolent concern for our ruler. If you gentlemen insist on seeking a means to avert calamities and remedy abnormal occurrences, I venture to offer an explanation.

Rushing everywhere to sacrifice at the various sacred sites is merely a minor detail of rites for warding off harm; admonishing the officials is merely an empty form that gives an appearance of improvement. Does the means of turning calamity into good fortune really lie in these things? The Song Confucian scholar Zhen Dexiu once said: “Those who grow complacent because auspicious signs are plentiful are not necessarily free from danger; those who learn fear because anomalies are numerous are not necessarily denied security. It depends only on how the ruler responds.” Should we not, then, give our attention today to the account of the various signs in the “Great Plan” and the correspondences of the Five Phases in the “Monthly Ordinances”? As for opening channels of speech to encourage remonstrance…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
端士風以抑僥倖清吏源以去冗濫慎民
牧以求循良干政者黜之失律者誅之幽
滯者揚之放逐者錄之則又當今之所不
可闕者執是以求弭災救變之術思過半
矣杞人之憂不自知其踈謬故敢爲執事
者陳之乃若
聖君賢相之所以格天者則自有道固非狂瞽
之所能窺測其萬一也
第五問
王朝良
===
同考試官訓導嚴　批〔說時事甚整切末復歸重於得人此誠不易之論也〕
同考試官訓導陳　批〔文有頓挫而處置甚詳必非迂儒可到〕
考試官主事袁　批〔憂深言切子其識時務者歟〕
考試官主事蕭　批〔時務條悉無遺可與論天下事矣〕
天下之事在於審勢達變而已矣因勢以
punctuated:
端士風以抑僥倖，清吏源以去冗濫，慎民牧以求循良，干政者黜之，失律者誅之，幽滯者揚之，放逐者錄之，則又當今之所不可闕者。執是以求弭災救變之術，思過半矣。杞人之憂，不自知其踈謬，故敢爲執事者陳之。乃若聖君賢相之所以格天者，則自有道，固非狂瞽之所能窺測其萬一也。

第五問
王朝良

同考試官訓導嚴批〔說時事甚整切，末復歸重於得人，此誠不易之論也。〕
同考試官訓導陳批〔文有頓挫，而處置甚詳，必非迂儒可到。〕
考試官主事袁批〔憂深言切，子其識時務者歟？〕
考試官主事蕭批〔時務條悉無遺，可與論天下事矣。〕

天下之事在於審勢達變而已矣。因勢以
translation_en:
…rectify the ethos of scholars to curb the pursuit of unmerited advancement; purify the sources of official recruitment to eliminate superfluous and unqualified appointees; and choose those who shepherd the people carefully, seeking conscientious and worthy officials. Dismiss those who interfere in government; execute those who violate military discipline; promote those left obscure and stalled in office; and restore to consideration those dismissed and banished. These, too, are measures indispensable today. By pursuing ways to avert disasters and remedy calamities through these measures, one will already have grasped more than half the matter. My anxieties are those of the man of Qi who feared the sky would fall; unaware of my own shallowness and errors, I nevertheless venture to lay them before you. As for the means by which our sagely ruler and worthy ministers move Heaven, they have their own Way, of which a rash and ignorant man such as myself cannot fathom even the smallest part.

Fifth Policy Question
Wang Chaoliang

Associate Examiner Yan, an Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion of current affairs is very orderly and pertinent. At the end, it again places the emphasis on securing the right men. This is truly an incontrovertible argument.〕
Associate Examiner Chen, an Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The writing has rhythmic variation, and the proposed measures are very detailed—certainly beyond the reach of a pedantic scholar.〕
Examiner Yuan, a Secretary, comments: 〔Your concern is deep and your words urgent. Are you not one who understands the affairs of the times?〕
Examiner Xiao, a Secretary, comments: 〔Current affairs are treated systematically and exhaustively, with nothing omitted. Here is someone with whom one can discuss the affairs of the realm.〕

Managing the affairs of the realm depends simply on assessing circumstances and understanding change. By following the prevailing circumstances in order to…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
通變隨變以從宜則天下之事殆無不可
爲者矣書曰有備無患此言防之於未然
也易曰繻有衣袽終日戒此言救之於已
然也今河南之事其未然者無復可圖矣
其已然者寧可坐視其弊而不爲之所乎
黃河爲害遷徙不常漕渠淤塞矣頃者動
三省之民以疏之而塞者如故意者未究
乎治水之道歟水之性分之則衰順之則
安爲今日之計莫若疏金龍口以通北鎮
===
之門户疏丁家道口以通徐呂之咽喉孫
家渡可疏也則朱仙鎮之故道通而河勢
漸分矣趙皮寨可疏也則黃陵岡之下流
通而水怒少殺矣又必濬渦河以通宿遷
濬白河以通中牟導其下流決其壅滯隄
築之必固蓄洩之以時而得人則如夏忠
靖之理江淮陳恭襄之開通濟任之專而
不惑於浮議行之漸而不急夫遊功如是
則漕渠其可通矣否則勞民傷財如之何
punctuated: 通變，隨變以從宜，則天下之事殆無不可爲者矣。《書》曰：「有備無患。」此言防之於未然也。《易》曰：「繻有衣袽，終日戒。」此言救之於已然也。今河南之事，其未然者無復可圖矣；其已然者，寧可坐視其弊而不爲之所乎？黃河爲害，遷徙不常，漕渠淤塞矣。頃者動三省之民以疏之，而塞者如故，意者未究乎治水之道歟？水之性，分之則衰，順之則安。爲今日之計，莫若疏金龍口以通北鎮之門户，疏丁家道口以通徐呂之咽喉。孫家渡可疏也，則朱仙鎮之故道通，而河勢漸分矣；趙皮寨可疏也，則黃陵岡之下流通，而水怒少殺矣。又必濬渦河以通宿遷，濬白河以通中牟，導其下流，決其壅滯。隄築之必固，蓄洩之以時。而得人，則如夏忠靖之理江淮、陳恭襄之開通濟，任之專而不惑於浮議，行之漸而不急夫遊功。如是，則漕渠其可通矣；否則，勞民傷財，如之何
translation_en:
…adapt to change, and respond to changing circumstances with appropriate measures; then scarcely any affair in the realm will be beyond accomplishment. The Book of Documents says, “With preparation there will be no calamity.” This means preventing trouble before it arises. The Book of Changes says, “Have rags ready against leaks [?]; remain vigilant all day.” This means remedying trouble after it has arisen. As for Henan’s affairs today, planning against troubles before they arise is no longer possible. But once they have arisen, can we simply sit and watch their harmful effects without taking measures?

The Yellow River causes havoc, shifting its course unpredictably, and the grain-transport canal has silted up. Recently, the people of three provinces were mobilized to dredge it, yet the blockage remains as before. Might this be because the principles of water management have not been fully investigated? Water’s nature is such that dividing its flow diminishes its force, while following its natural course makes it stable. For present purposes, nothing would be better than dredging Jinlongkou to open the gateway to Beizhen, and dredging Dingjia Daokou to open the vital passage through Xu and Lü. If Sunjiadu can be dredged, the old channel at Zhuxianzhen will open, and the river’s force will gradually be divided. If Zhaopizhai can be dredged, the lower course at Huanglinggang will open, and the fury of the waters will abate somewhat. We must also dredge the Guo River to open passage to Suqian, and dredge the Bai River to open passage to Zhongmou, guiding their downstream flow and clearing their obstructions. Embankments must be built firmly, and water stored and released at the proper times.

If suitable men are obtained—as when Xia Zhongjing managed the rivers of the Jiang–Huai region and Chen Gongxiang opened the Tongji Canal—they should be given undivided responsibility, without being swayed by ill-informed criticism. The work should proceed gradually, without pressing for quick results [?]. In this way, the grain-transport canal can be opened. Otherwise, exhausting the people and wasting resources, how could one…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
其有成功邪滁賊恃險干逆天紀勢甚猖
獗矣茲者連二省之兵以剿之而叛者亦
寧意者未盡夫用兵之道與用兵之道動
靜相時翕張視勢爲今之計莫若塞壺關
之口以遏其奔衝據林邑之險以防其出
沒禁旅可用也分畨迭肄則彼之精鋭羈
矣土兵可用也堅壁清野則彼之樵采絶
矣又必用鄉導以察其險易懸重賞以疑
其腹心脅從者不問投降者不誅攻其所
===
不救掩其所不備而選將則如充國之坐
制先零李愬之雪夜破蔡假以節鉞而無
中制之憂錄其功賞而嚴失律之罰如是
則小醜其可殄矣否則覆軍殺將如之何
其不肝食邪亢旱爲虐麥禾不收民之憔
悴甚矣又加之蝗蝻兩河南北赤地千里
茲欲處之亦惟爲守令者布寛恤之恩罷
督責之令踏勘必實先期
奏聞或蠲夏税之太半或蠲秋粮之什七又
punctuated:
其有成功邪？滁賊恃險，干逆天紀，勢甚猖獗矣。茲者連二省之兵以剿之，而叛者亦寧，意者未盡夫用兵之道與？用兵之道，動靜相時，翕張視勢。爲今之計，莫若塞壺關之口，以遏其奔衝；據林邑之險，以防其出沒。禁旅可用也，分畨迭肄，則彼之精鋭羈矣；土兵可用也，堅壁清野，則彼之樵采絶矣。又必用鄉導以察其險易，懸重賞以疑其腹心，脅從者不問，投降者不誅，攻其所不救，掩其所不備。而選將則如充國之坐制先零、李愬之雪夜破蔡，假以節鉞，而無中制之憂；錄其功賞，而嚴失律之罰。如是，則小醜其可殄矣。否則覆軍殺將，如之何其不肝食邪？
亢旱爲虐，麥禾不收，民之憔悴甚矣。又加之蝗蝻，兩河南北，赤地千里。茲欲處之，亦惟爲守令者布寛恤之恩，罷督責之令，踏勘必實，先期奏聞，或蠲夏税之太半，或蠲秋粮之什七，又
translation_en:
…how could it succeed? The bandits of Chu rely on difficult terrain and defy Heaven’s order; their power has grown utterly rampant. Recently, troops from two provinces have been combined to suppress them, yet the rebels remain at ease [?]. Perhaps the principles of warfare have not been fully applied? In warfare, movement and stillness must accord with the proper moment, and contraction and expansion must follow the circumstances. For the present, the best plan is to block the entrance to Huguan, checking their headlong assaults, and occupy the defensible terrain of Linyi, preventing their movements in and out. The imperial guard troops can be employed: divide them into rotating contingents for successive training, and the enemy’s elite forces will be held in check. Local troops can be employed: strengthen the fortifications and clear the countryside, and the enemy’s supplies of firewood and provisions will be cut off. Local guides must also be employed to investigate difficult and accessible terrain, and substantial rewards offered to sow suspicion among their trusted followers. Those compelled to join them should not be prosecuted, and those who surrender should not be executed. Attack where they cannot bring relief, and strike where they are unprepared. In selecting commanders, seek men like Chongguo, who subdued the Xianling without advancing, or Li Su, who captured Cai on a snowy night. Grant them the credential staff and battle-axe of command, freeing them from concern over interference from the court. Record and reward their achievements, while strictly punishing breaches of military discipline. In this way, these petty villains can be exterminated. Otherwise, armies will be destroyed and commanders killed—how could their livers escape being devoured [?]?
Prolonged drought wreaks havoc; wheat and other grain yield no harvest, and the people are terribly worn down. On top of this come locusts and their nymphs: north and south of the Yellow River, the land lies barren for a thousand li. To deal with this now, prefects and county magistrates must extend benevolent relief and revoke orders demanding payment. Their inspections on the ground must ascertain the actual conditions, and they must memorialize the throne in advance. They might remit the greater part of the summer tax, or seven-tenths of the autumn grain levy, and furthermore…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
必發倉以賑之移粟以撫之凡可以恤民
隱者力爲之圖如富弼之在青州趙閱道
之在浙西則民沾實惠而雲漢之什可無
作矣徭役太煩勞者下息民之疲敝久矣
又加之以征調十室九空朝夕不保茲欲
救之亦惟爲守令者禁額外之誅求罷不
急之營繕撙節有方稍加存恤開河之役
暫停勦賊之兵不出又必視戶之上下均
其賦稅量丁之多寡節其庸調凡可以拯
===
民窮者曲爲之處如陽城之撫字如黄霸
之愛養則民獲安息而鴻鴈之苦庶有瘳
矣雖然治河有說矣而轉般之法亦不可
不預講也弭盜有方矣而安輯之計亦不
可不先圖也旱蝗可憂而長平義倉之設
其亦有可采歟徭役可閔而差役免役之
法其亦有可做歟凡此四者皆目前之急
務謂如拯溺救焚之不暇者而審勢達變
愚則四存乎其人也若曰坐而論天下之
punctuated:
必發倉以賑之，移粟以撫之。凡可以恤民隱者，力爲之圖。如富弼之在青州、趙閱道之在浙西，則民沾實惠，而《雲漢》之什可無作矣。
徭役太煩，勞者下息，民之疲敝久矣。又加之以征調，十室九空，朝夕不保。茲欲救之，亦惟爲守令者禁額外之誅求，罷不急之營繕，撙節有方，稍加存恤。開河之役暫停，勦賊之兵不出。又必視戶之上下，均其賦稅；量丁之多寡，節其庸調。凡可以拯民窮者，曲爲之處。如陽城之撫字，如黄霸之愛養，則民獲安息，而《鴻鴈》之苦庶有瘳矣。
雖然，治河有說矣，而轉般之法亦不可不預講也；弭盜有方矣，而安輯之計亦不可不先圖也。旱蝗可憂，而長平義倉之設，其亦有可采歟？徭役可閔，而差役免役之法，其亦有可做歟？凡此四者，皆目前之急務，謂如拯溺救焚之不暇者。而審勢達變，愚則四存乎其人也。若曰坐而論天下之
translation_en:
…It is also essential to open the granaries to provide relief and transport grain to sustain the people. Every means of alleviating their suffering must be pursued with vigor. If officials act as Fu Bi did in Qingzhou and Zhao Yuedao in western Zhejiang, the people will receive tangible benefits, and there will be no occasion to compose a poem like “The Milky Way” (Yunhan).
Corvée obligations are excessively burdensome, and those who toil have no respite [?]; the people have long been exhausted and impoverished. Military levies and requisitions compound their distress: nine households in ten stand empty, and people cannot be sure of surviving from morning to evening. To rescue them now, prefects and county magistrates must prohibit exactions beyond the prescribed quotas, halt nonessential construction and repairs, practice economy systematically, and afford them some care and relief. River-dredging labor should be temporarily suspended, and troops should not be dispatched to suppress bandits. Officials must also assess households according to their means and distribute taxation equitably, and regulate labor-service payments and levies according to the number of adult males. Every possible means of rescuing the people from destitution must be considered with care. If officials nurture them as Yang Cheng did and care for them as Huang Ba did, the people will obtain peace and rest, and the suffering described in “The Wild Geese” (Hongyan) may at last be relieved.
Nevertheless, although proposals for managing the river have been offered, methods of transshipment must also be discussed beforehand; although measures for suppressing banditry have been identified, plans for restoring peace and bringing people back into settled life must also be devised in advance. Drought and locusts are cause for concern: might there be something worth adopting in the establishment of “Changping” [?] and charitable granaries? Corvée burdens deserve compassion: might there be something practicable in the systems of assigned service and exemption from service? These four matters are all urgent tasks of the present moment, allowing no more delay than rescuing someone from drowning or fire. As for assessing circumstances and responding to change, in my humble view all four depend upon the right people [?]. If one says that to sit and discuss the affairs of the world…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
事也易進而處天下之事也難則執事可
以無問而愚也可以無對矣
punctuated: 事也易，進而處天下之事也難，則執事可以無問，而愚也可以無對矣。
translation_en: …affairs is easy, whereas stepping forward to manage the affairs of the realm is difficult, then you, sir, need not have asked, and I, in my ignorance, need not have replied.

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄後序
衮奉
命校文河南道出燕趙涉衛趨大
梁降觀于郊野其土風往往
啬而愿約而愉憂勤而寛舒
及試士其言亦多毅而不隘
直而不夸孫而不迫辨而中
===
其義核其慮詳雍容和平蓋
猶有先王之遺焉夫河洛故
都會而天地之中其書圖則
羲禹之所則也禮樂則周公
之所制作也周之盛也其在
成康之際乎成王營雒以正
四方於時風俗和平賢才衆
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄後序

衮奉命校文河南，道出燕趙，涉衛，趨大梁，降觀于郊野，其土風往往啬而愿，約而愉，憂勤而寛舒。及試士，其言亦多毅而不隘，直而不夸，孫而不迫，辨而中，其義核，其慮詳，雍容和平，蓋猶有先王之遺焉。

夫河洛，故都會而天地之中，其書圖則羲禹之所則也，禮樂則周公之所制作也。周之盛也，其在成康之際乎？成王營雒，以正四方，於時風俗和平，賢才衆
translation_en:
Afterword to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

I, Gun, received the command to evaluate examination essays in Henan. My route passed through Yan and Zhao, crossed Wei, and led toward Daliang. Going out among the fields to observe, I found the local customs generally frugal and sincere, restrained yet cheerful, diligent in their concerns yet relaxed and at ease. When I examined the candidates, their writings likewise were often resolute without narrowness, forthright without exaggeration, modest without constraint, and discriminating yet apt. Their meanings were sound, their deliberations thorough, and their manner composed and harmonious. Surely something of the legacy of the former kings still survives here.

The region of the Yellow and Luo Rivers was an ancient metropolitan center and lies at the center of Heaven and Earth. Its Writing and Chart were what Fuxi and Yu took as their models; its rites and music were what the Duke of Zhou fashioned. Was not Zhou at its height in the age of Kings Cheng and Kang? King Cheng built Luo to set the four quarters aright. At that time, customs were harmonious and peaceful, and worthy and talented men in great numbers…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
興故詩人美之曰藹藹王多
吉人曁乎漢室梁孝王嘉禮
儒術招致賓徒時則有鄒枚
司馬之流相與作爲賦頌以
褒贊功德其制度宏麗文辭
瑰瑋蓋亦雅頌之亞也嗣是
無聞焉豈世道升降使然哉
===
我
明興設科取士其始賢良文學太
半出於荊楊吳粵之間河洛
之士蓋鮮焉乃
孝廟時則彬彬矣今
天子脩弘
祖構海內興起禮文偹隅下邑亦
punctuated:
興，故詩人美之曰：「藹藹王多吉人。」曁乎漢室，梁孝王嘉禮儒術，招致賓徒，時則有鄒、枚、司馬之流，相與作爲賦頌，以褒贊功德。其制度宏麗，文辭瑰瑋，蓋亦雅頌之亞也。嗣是無聞焉，豈世道升降使然哉？
我明興，設科取士，其始賢良文學太半出於荊楊吳粵之間，河洛之士蓋鮮焉。乃孝廟時，則彬彬矣。今天子脩弘祖構，海內興起，禮文偹，隅下邑亦
translation_en:
…arose. Thus the poet praised them, saying: “In abundant numbers, the king has many worthy men.” By the Han dynasty, Prince Xiao of Liang honored Confucian learning and recruited guests and followers. Among them were men such as Zou, Mei, and Sima, who together composed rhapsodies and encomia to celebrate achievements and virtue. Their compositions were grand and splendid in form, their language magnificent and extraordinary—surely second only to the Elegantiae and Hymns of the Book of Odes. Thereafter, nothing comparable was heard of. Could this have resulted from the rise and decline of the moral order of the age?
When our Ming dynasty arose, it instituted examinations to recruit men for office. At first, more than half the worthy and learned men came from the regions of Jing, Yang, Wu, and Yue; men from the He–Luo region were few. By the reign of Xiaozong, however, cultured men were flourishing there. Now the Son of Heaven cultivates and expands the foundations laid by his ancestors. Throughout the realm, men are stirred to endeavor, ritual and cultural forms are fully established, and even remote, small towns [?] also…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
蔚乎多士在河洛固宜有異
材茂等如周之所謂藹藹吉
人者奮出其間區區詞賦之
徒直薄不爲耳昔者先王之
制治也以質文相救後世則
文敝而質日衰識治者蓋深
憂焉夫文勝則變而趨質質
===
勝則變而趨道是故與其文
也寧質河洛之文不勝其質
吾是之取爾吾是之取爾〔奏〕
也不斂惴惴焉惟不得人以
塞
明詔是懼故敢盡布其說以爲諸
生告若夫低昻之衷闓衞之
punctuated:
蔚乎多士。在河洛，固宜有異材茂等，如周之所謂藹藹吉人者，奮出其間，區區詞賦之徒，直薄不爲耳。昔者先王之制治也，以質文相救；後世則文敝而質日衰，識治者蓋深憂焉。夫文勝則變而趨質，質勝則變而趨道。是故與其文也，寧質。河洛之文不勝其質，吾是之取爾，吾是之取爾。
〔奏〕也不斂，惴惴焉，惟不得人以塞明詔是懼，故敢盡布其說，以爲諸生告。若夫低昻之衷、闓衞之
translation_en:
…abounds in men of learning. In the He–Luo region, it is surely fitting that men of exceptional talent and outstanding ability should rise from among them, like those described in the Zhou phrase, “a multitude of worthy men.” They simply disdain to engage in the petty pursuits of mere composers of verse and rhapsodies. In former times, when the ancient kings established their government, they used substance and refinement to remedy each other’s deficiencies. In later ages, refinement became corrupted, while substance declined day by day. Those who understand governance have been deeply troubled by this. When refinement predominates, change tends toward substance; when substance predominates, change tends toward the Way. Thus, rather than refinement, one should prefer substance. In He–Luo, refinement does not outweigh substance. This is what I value; this is what I value.
I, 〔Zou〕, am unrestrained [?] and apprehensive, fearing only that I may fail to find suitable men to fulfill the illustrious imperial edict. I therefore venture to set forth my views in full, to make them known to you students. As for the impartiality of assigning higher and lower rankings, and the examination precinct’s security [?] …

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
命下祇懼靡夙靡夜迺如期至則
百務周悉實維巡按監察御
史譚〔纘〕經畫精密鎮守則太
監呂〔憲〕巡撫則副都御史潘
〔塤〕雅重文事總河政者右都
御史盛〔應期〕也迺若學正梁
〔舉〕教諭李〔一清〕鄧〔公度〕張〔賀〕
===
林〔大道〕馬〔驎〕訓導梁〔文重〕陳
〔汝〕嚴〔玉振〕先是以御史〔纘〕屬
左布政使董〔銳〕右布政使蔡
〔潮〕禮聘亦如期至事事而提
調則參政許〔復禮〕伍〔全〕監試
則按察使張〔翰〕僉事王〔洙〕贊
翼惟慎其參政丁〔致祥〕陶〔諧〕
punctuated: 命下，祇懼，靡夙靡夜，迺如期至。則百務周悉，實維巡按監察御史譚〔纘〕經畫精密。鎮守則太監呂〔憲〕，巡撫則副都御史潘〔塤〕，雅重文事。總河政者，右都御史盛〔應期〕也。迺若學正梁〔舉〕，教諭李〔一清〕、鄧〔公度〕、張〔賀〕、林〔大道〕、馬〔驎〕，訓導梁〔文重〕、陳〔汝〕、嚴〔玉振〕，先是以御史〔纘〕屬左布政使董〔銳〕、右布政使蔡〔潮〕禮聘，亦如期至，事事。而提調則參政許〔復禮〕、伍〔全〕，監試則按察使張〔翰〕、僉事王〔洙〕，贊翼惟慎。其參政丁〔致祥〕、陶〔諧〕，
translation_en:
… When the command came down, we received it with reverent apprehension, working morning and night, and duly arrived at the appointed time. Every arrangement was thoroughly attended to, thanks to the meticulous planning of Regional Inspector Tan Zan. The eunuch stationed as defender was Grand Eunuch Lü Xian, and the Grand Coordinator was Vice Censor-in-Chief Pan Xun; they held literary affairs in high esteem. The official overseeing river administration was Right Censor-in-Chief Sheng Yingqi.

As for Departmental School Instructor Liang Ju; County School Instructors Li Yiqing, Deng Gongdu, Zhang He, Lin Dadao, and Ma Lin; and Assistant Instructors Liang Wenzhong, Chen Ru, and Yan Yuzhen, Censor Zan had previously entrusted Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Dong Rui and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Cai Chao with formally inviting them. They too arrived at the appointed time and attended to their duties. The Proctors were Administration Vice Commissioners Xu Fuli and Wu Quan; supervising the examination were Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Han and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wang Zhu. They exercised the utmost care in their assistance. As for Administration Vice Commissioners Ding Zhixiang and Tao Xie …

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
參議鄭〔雲翔〕王〔本善〕副使翟
〔瓚〕樊〔繼祖〕周〔忠〕顧〔燁〕僉事祁
〔鵠〕初〔杲〕温〔濡〕張〔庠〕張〔紳〕都指
揮僉事霍〔汝愚〕李〔郁〕則皆于
試事與有勞焉者廼合提學
副使楊〔維聰〕所簡士二千人
三試之得士八十惟
===
制錄其文之如式者以
獻亦惟
制〔璆〕不肖維諸執事之相與共是
役也罔有不盡廼心廼力者
冀惟得人爲
天子使耳嗟爾諸士遂以言進其
亦思
punctuated:
參議鄭〔雲翔〕、王〔本善〕，副使翟〔瓚〕、樊〔繼祖〕、周〔忠〕、顧〔燁〕，僉事祁〔鵠〕、初〔杲〕、温〔濡〕、張〔庠〕、張〔紳〕，都指揮僉事霍〔汝愚〕、李〔郁〕，則皆于試事與有勞焉者。廼合提學副使楊〔維聰〕所簡士二千人，三試之，得士八十。惟制，錄其文之如式者以獻，亦惟制。
〔璆〕不肖，維諸執事之相與共是役也，罔有不盡廼心廼力者，冀惟得人爲天子使耳。嗟爾諸士，遂以言進，其亦思
translation_en:
…Administration Assistant Commissioners Zheng Yunxiang and Wang Benshan; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhai Zan, Fan Jizu, Zhou Zhong, and Gu Ye; Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Qi Hu, Chu Gao, Wen Ru, Zhang Xiang, and Zhang Shen; and Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Huo Ruyu and Li Yu all contributed their labors to the examination. We then assembled the two thousand candidates selected by Yang Weicong, Surveillance Vice Commissioner in charge of education, and examined them in three sessions, selecting eighty. This followed the imperial regulations; recording those examination essays that conformed to the prescribed forms and submitting them to the throne likewise followed the imperial regulations.
Unworthy though I, Qiu, am, all the officials who shared in this undertaking devoted their hearts and strength to it without exception, hoping only to obtain worthy men for the Son of Heaven to employ. Ah, you gentlemen, having thus advanced through your written words, should also reflect…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹塲
四書
參乎吾道一以貫之曾子曰唯
君子之所不可及者其唯人之所不見乎
大人者言不必信行不必果惟義所在
易
先王以作樂崇德殷薦之上帝以配祖考
艮其止止其所也
通乎晝夜之道而知
天下之動貞夫一者也
===
書
帝德廣運乃聖乃神乃武乃文
欽予時命其惟有終說復于王曰惟木從
繩則正后從諫則聖后克聖臣不命
其承疇敢不祗若王之休命
天惟純佑命則商實
穆穆在上明明在下灼于四方罔不惟德
之勤
punctuated:
第壹塲

四書
「參乎！吾道一以貫之。」曾子曰：「唯。」
君子之所不可及者，其唯人之所不見乎！
大人者，言不必信，行不必果，惟義所在。

易
先王以作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝，以配祖考。
艮其止，止其所也。
通乎晝夜之道而知。
天下之動，貞夫一者也。

書
帝德廣運，乃聖乃神，乃武乃文。
「欽予時命，其惟有終。」說復于王曰：「惟木從繩則正，后從諫則聖。后克聖，臣不命其承，疇敢不祗若王之休命？」
天惟純佑命，則商實。
穆穆在上，明明在下，灼于四方，罔不惟德之勤。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
“Shen! My Way is threaded together by a single principle.” Master Zeng replied, “Yes.”
What others cannot match in the gentleman is surely what they do not see!
The great man need not invariably keep his word or carry his actions through to completion; he follows only what is right.

Book of Changes (Yijing)
The former kings accordingly created music to exalt virtue, offering it in abundance to the Lord on High and associating their ancestors with Him in the sacrifice.
To rest where one should rest means to rest in one's proper place.
To comprehend the Way of day and night and thereby possess wisdom.
The movements of all under Heaven find their constancy in the One.

Book of Documents (Shujing)
The emperor's virtue extends far and wide: sagely and spirit-like, martial and cultured.
“Reverently heed this command of mine, and carry it through to the end.” Yue replied to the king: “Wood that follows the marking line becomes straight; a ruler who follows remonstrance becomes sagely. If the ruler can be sagely, his servants will carry out his wishes without being commanded. Who would dare not reverently obey the king's excellent commands?”
Heaven greatly supports our mandate; thus Shang is made secure [?].
Reverent and dignified above, discerning and enlightened below, their brilliance shone throughout the four quarters; none failed to apply themselves diligently to virtue.

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
詩
南有樛木葛藟纍之樂只君子福履綏之
南有樛木葛藟荒之樂只君子福履
將之南有樛木葛藟縈之樂只君子
福履成之
神之聽之終和且平
維此文王小心翼翼昭事上帝聿懷多福
厥德不回以受方國
思無邪思馬斯徂
===
春秋
王姬歸于齊〔莊公十一年〕公及齊侯宋公陳
侯衛侯鄭伯許男曹伯會王世子于
首止〔僖公五年〕
楚人伐黃〔僖公十一年〕狄侵衛〔僖公十三年〕
晉侯使韓穿來言汶陽之田歸之于齊〔成
公八年〕公會晉侯齊侯宋公衛侯鄭伯
曹伯莒子杞伯同盟于蒲〔成公九年〕叔
弓如晉〔昭公八年〕公會劉子晉侯齊侯
punctuated:
詩
南有樛木，葛藟纍之。樂只君子，福履綏之。南有樛木，葛藟荒之。樂只君子，福履將之。南有樛木，葛藟縈之。樂只君子，福履成之。
神之聽之，終和且平。
維此文王，小心翼翼。昭事上帝，聿懷多福。厥德不回，以受方國。
思無邪，思馬斯徂。

春秋
王姬歸于齊〔莊公十一年〕。公及齊侯、宋公、陳侯、衛侯、鄭伯、許男、曹伯會王世子于首止〔僖公五年〕。
楚人伐黃〔僖公十一年〕。狄侵衛〔僖公十三年〕。
晉侯使韓穿來言汶陽之田歸之于齊〔成公八年〕。公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、杞伯，同盟于蒲〔成公九年〕。叔弓如晉〔昭公八年〕。公會劉子、晉侯、齊侯
translation_en:
Book of Odes
In the south are trees with drooping branches; kudzu and creeping vines entwine them. Joyful is the noble lord; may blessings bring him repose. In the south are trees with drooping branches; kudzu and creeping vines cover them. Joyful is the noble lord; may blessings sustain him. In the south are trees with drooping branches; kudzu and creeping vines wind around them. Joyful is the noble lord; may blessings bring him fulfillment.
When the spirits hear this, all will end in harmony and peace.
This King Wen was careful and reverent. He served the Lord on High with manifest devotion, thereby receiving many blessings. His virtue did not deviate, and so he received the states of the regions.
Let thoughts be without waywardness; the horses move onward.

Spring and Autumn Annals
The king’s daughter married into Qi. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Zhuang〕 The duke, together with the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Chen, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Baron of Xu, and the Earl of Cao, met the king’s heir apparent at Shouzhi. 〔Fifth year of Duke Xi〕
The men of Chu attacked Huang. 〔Eleventh year of Duke Xi〕 The Di invaded Wei. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Xi〕
The Marquis of Jin sent Han Chuan to convey the instruction that the lands of Wenyang be returned to Qi. 〔Eighth year of Duke Cheng〕 The duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, and the Earl of Qi, and they jointly entered into a covenant at Pu. 〔Ninth year of Duke Cheng〕 Shu Gong went to Jin. 〔Eighth year of Duke Zhao〕 The duke met the Viscount of Liu, the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi …

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
宋公衛侯鄭伯曹伯莒子邾子滕子
薛伯杞伯小邾子于平丘〔昭公十三年〕
楚公子貞帥師伐鄭〔襄公八年〕
禮記
毋不敬儼若思安定辭安民哉
四者君以正用之故君者立於無過之地
也
人生而靜天之性也感於物而動性之欲
也
===
夫孝置之而塞乎天地溥之而横乎四海
施諸後世而無朝夕推而放諸東海
而準推而放諸西海而準推而放諸
南海而準推而放諸北海而準
第貳場
論
古之學者爲己
詔誥表內科一道
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔〔建元〕
punctuated:
宋公、衛侯、鄭伯、曹伯、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子于平丘〔昭公十三年〕。
楚公子貞帥師伐鄭〔襄公八年〕。

禮記
毋不敬，儼若思，安定辭。安民哉！
四者，君以正用之，故君者立於無過之地也。
人生而靜，天之性也；感於物而動，性之欲也。
夫孝，置之而塞乎天地，溥之而横乎四海，施諸後世而無朝夕。推而放諸東海而準，推而放諸西海而準，推而放諸南海而準，推而放諸北海而準。

第貳場
論
古之學者爲己。

詔誥表內科一道
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔〔建元〕
translation_en:
…the Duke of Song, the Duke of Wei, the Earl of Zheng, the Earl of Cao, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Xiaozhu at Pingqiu. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhao〕
Prince Zhen of Chu led an army to attack Zheng. 〔Eighth year of Duke Xiang〕

Record of Rites (Liji)
Never fail in reverence; be solemn as though absorbed in thought, and composed and measured in speech. This will bring peace to the people!
The ruler employs these four correctly; hence the ruler stands in a position free from error.
At birth, human beings are still: this is their Heaven-given nature. When affected by things, they become active: these are the desires of that nature.
As for filial piety, set it in place and it fills Heaven and Earth; spread it abroad and it extends across the Four Seas; apply it to later generations and it admits no distinction between morning and evening. Extend and apply it to the Eastern Sea, and it holds true; extend and apply it to the Western Sea, and it holds true; extend and apply it to the Southern Sea, and it holds true; extend and apply it to the Northern Sea, and it holds true.

Second Session
Discourse
The learners of antiquity studied for their own sake.

One composition from among edicts, proclamations, and memorials [?]
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty calling for the recommendation of men of worth and goodness, upright and correct, who would speak frankly and remonstrate without reserve. 〔Jianyuan era…〕

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
〔元年〕
擬唐以孫伏伽爲治書侍御史誥〔武德元年〕
擬宋司馬光進三事五規表〔嘉祐六年〕
判語〔五條〕
制書有違
收支留難
奏對失序
驛使稽程
斷罪不當
===
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問昔者堯舜禹之相授受也曰人心惟危
道心惟微惟精惟一允執厥中此帝王
道統之源也禹之傳湯湯之傳於文武
皆不外此固可得而言矣漢唐而下無
聞焉其故何耶我
太祖無所授而得之天性其見於典故君臣問
答之間微詞大旨固亦有可言者與
punctuated:
〔元年〕
擬唐以孫伏伽爲治書侍御史誥〔武德元年〕。
擬宋司馬光進三事五規表〔嘉祐六年〕。
判語〔五條〕
制書有違。
收支留難。
奏對失序。
驛使稽程。
斷罪不當。

第叁場
策〔五道〕
問：昔者堯舜禹之相授受也，曰：「人心惟危，道心惟微，惟精惟一，允執厥中。」此帝王道統之源也。禹之傳湯，湯之傳於文武，皆不外此，固可得而言矣。漢唐而下無聞焉，其故何耶？我太祖無所授而得之天性，其見於典故、君臣問答之間，微詞大旨，固亦有可言者與？
translation_en:
…〔first year〕
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang appointing Sun Fujia as Vice Censor-in-chief.〔First year of Wude〕
Compose a memorial in the manner of Sima Guang of the Song presenting the Three Matters and Five Admonitions.〔Sixth year of Jiayou〕
Legal judgments〔five topics〕
Violation of an imperial decree.
Obstruction of receipts and disbursements.
Failure to observe proper order when submitting reports and answering the emperor.
A postal-relay messenger’s delay beyond the prescribed travel time.
Improper sentencing.

Third Session
Policy essays〔five questions〕
Question: When Yao, Shun, and Yu transmitted the succession to one another in antiquity, they said: “The human mind is precarious; the mind of the Way is subtle. Be discerning and single-minded; sincerely hold fast to the mean.” This is the source of the emperors’ and kings’ transmission of the Way. Yu’s transmission to Tang, and Tang’s transmission to Wen and Wu, all remained within this teaching; these can certainly be discussed. From the Han and Tang onward, however, nothing was heard of it. Why was this?
Our Taizu received it through no transmission, but attained it through his Heaven-endowed nature. As manifested in historical precedents and exchanges between ruler and ministers, surely its subtle expressions and great purport also offer something that can be discussed?

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
列聖相承同底於道有由然矣方今
皇上望道拳拳真有紹堯舜禹湯文武以及我
祖宗之所傳者故敬一有箴五箴有註明白淵
微誠有非世儒牽合文義所能及者
御製御翰布之天下諸生誦法久矣抑有能仰
窺
聖製之奧妙者乎其於帝王
祖宗相傳之道亦有相發明乎其敬陳之毋忽
問周禮爲周公致治之跡而春秋則孔子
所筆削此固無疑者或者乃詆周禮爲
瀆亂陰謀之書而謂春秋爲斷爛朝報
其僭謬固不待辨乃若我
===
國家明經取士而周禮獨不列於學官
列聖崇儒右文而春秋獨不以進講此其故何
歟將二書者果有可疑如何休葦所云
乎不然何其抑而不見尊信也且考工
一記或者以爲漢儒所補而緜周王曾
雖儒者不能無疑焉其然豈其然乎且
punctuated:
列聖相承，同底於道，有由然矣。方今皇上望道拳拳，真有紹堯舜禹湯文武以及我祖宗之所傳者。故敬一有箴，五箴有註，明白淵微，誠有非世儒牽合文義所能及者。御製御翰，布之天下，諸生誦法久矣。抑有能仰窺聖製之奧妙者乎？其於帝王祖宗相傳之道，亦有相發明乎？其敬陳之，毋忽。

問：周禮爲周公致治之跡，而春秋則孔子所筆削，此固無疑者。或者乃詆周禮爲瀆亂陰謀之書，而謂春秋爲斷爛朝報，其僭謬固不待辨。乃若我國家明經取士，而周禮獨不列於學官；列聖崇儒右文，而春秋獨不以進講，此其故何歟？將二書者果有可疑，如何休葦所云乎？不然，何其抑而不見尊信也？且考工一記，或者以爲漢儒所補，而緜周王曾，雖儒者不能無疑焉。其然？豈其然乎？且
translation_en:
…The successive sage emperors have inherited from one another and alike attained the Way; there are reasons why this is so. Today His Majesty earnestly aspires to the Way, truly carrying forward what Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, as well as our imperial ancestors, transmitted. Thus he has composed an Admonition on Reverent Unity and annotations to the Five Admonitions. Clear and lucid, profound and subtle, these contain insights truly beyond the reach of commonplace scholars who strain to reconcile textual meanings. His imperial compositions, in his own calligraphy, have been disseminated throughout the realm, and you students have long recited them and taken them as your model. Yet can any of you reverently glimpse the mysteries of these imperial writings? Do they also illuminate the Way transmitted among the ancient emperors and kings and our imperial ancestors? Set this forth respectfully, without negligence.

Question: The Rites of Zhou records how the Duke of Zhou brought about good government, while the Spring and Autumn Annals was edited by Confucius. These facts are beyond doubt. Yet some have disparaged the Rites of Zhou as a book of disorder and covert plotting, and called the Spring and Autumn Annals fragmentary court bulletins. The presumptuous errors of such claims need no refutation. Nevertheless, our dynasty selects officials through mastery of the classics, yet the Rites of Zhou alone is not included in the official curriculum. The successive sage emperors have honored Confucian learning and esteemed literary culture, yet the Spring and Autumn Annals alone is not presented in lectures before the throne. Why is this? Can these two books really contain grounds for doubt, as He Xiu and others [?] have claimed? If not, why are they slighted rather than honored and trusted? Furthermore, some consider the Record of Artificers to have been supplied by Han Confucian scholars; as for the passage transcribed as ‘緜周王曾’ [?], even Confucian scholars cannot remain free of doubt. Is this so? Can it really be so? Furthermore…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
有定理神而明之者其惟大人矣乎是故二三
敗德言之貴信也尚矣然或不擇可否規規於
言之可踐是諒而已矣大人則圓神不滯可以
信可以無信雖曰擬之後言而實未嘗預期其
信也豈若是之諒也哉果斷團觀行之貴果也
審矣然或不顧是非硜硜於行之必決是固而
已矣大人則旁行不流可以果可以無果雖曰
議之後動而實未嘗預期其果也豈若是之固
也哉然則如之何而後可亦曰有義存焉耳時
===
以出之而淺深詳略一以義爲權衡義可信則
信如其非義雖不信無傷也是義之所在即言
之所在聲固可爲律矣孰能如其信也哉孫以
行之而操縱闔闢一以義爲準的義當果則果
如其非義雖不果無害也是義之所在即行之
所在身固可爲度矣孰能如其果也哉是則信
可也必於信則不可果可也必於果則不可無
意無必而義之與比非大人其孰能之抑此大
人者其惟孔子當之耳觀其一言一動從心所
punctuated:
有定理，神而明之者，其惟大人矣乎？是故二三敗德，言之貴信也尚矣。然或不擇可否，規規於言之可踐，是諒而已矣。大人則圓神不滯，可以信，可以無信；雖曰擬之後言，而實未嘗預期其信也。豈若是之諒也哉？果斷團觀，行之貴果也審矣。然或不顧是非，硜硜於行之必決，是固而已矣。大人則旁行不流，可以果，可以無果；雖曰議之後動，而實未嘗預期其果也。豈若是之固也哉？
然則如之何而後可？亦曰有義存焉耳。時以出之，而淺深詳略，一以義爲權衡。義可信則信，如其非義，雖不信無傷也。是義之所在，即言之所在，聲固可爲律矣，孰能如其信也哉？孫以行之，而操縱闔闢，一以義爲準的。義當果則果，如其非義，雖不果無害也。是義之所在，即行之所在，身固可爲度矣，孰能如其果也哉？
是則信可也，必於信則不可；果可也，必於果則不可。無意無必，而義之與比，非大人其孰能之？抑此大人者，其惟孔子當之耳。觀其一言一動，從心所
translation_en:
