…The examination system suffices to provide opportunities for scholars. Yet if we select them for literary accomplishment without considering their conduct and sense of duty, will they not all lapse into superficial extravagance? I ask that, beyond the established examinations, regulations be devised for recruitment through invitation and recommendation. Provincial governors should charge the surveillance commissioners with this responsibility, and the surveillance commissioners should charge the prefects and magistrates. They should seek men living in seclusion among cliffs and caves and consult members of the gentry. If there are men of eminent moral virtue, men who are filial, respectful toward their elder brothers, and diligent in farming, men whose conduct is upright and pure, or men of profound learning, their actual conduct should be investigated and their names traced out [?] and reported to the throne. There might be one such man in a province, one in several provinces, or one in the entire empire. Moreover, the number of worthy and talented men must be made a criterion for ranking the performance of the provincial commissions and prefectures. Those who conceal worthy men should be punished, as should those who put forward false or indiscriminate recommendations. It is the men themselves, not merely their number, that matter. I observe that when those above favor something, those below invariably pursue it still more zealously. I cannot believe that, under such arrangements, people would fail to vie with one another in striving to improve.
Those now called Confucian teachers are, in the Directorate of Education, the Chancellor, and in local schools, the lesser school instructors; those who supervise education are censorial officials. The Chancellor holds an exalted office, and the censorial officials occupy important posts: their standing has long been high. Only those in charge of local schools hold lowly offices and receive scant ceremonial respect. Among them, scarcely one or two in ten can rouse themselves to rise above their circumstances. Because their superiors accord them no special consideration, they too become inclined to give up on themselves. Consequently, their duties go unfulfilled, and the sounds of strings and recitation are unheard. In extreme cases, school grounds have even become vegetable gardens [the concluding wording here is garbled: 有參]. I ask that henceforth the selection and appointment of these men invariably be undertaken with care…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
禮待之必優教授則以進士爲之學正教
諭則以舉人爲之訓導則以貢士爲之其
稱職者則稍加優異不次超遷如是則師
儒重而人才衆盛矣今之所謂資格者科
目也例貢也吏役也科目正途其重也久
矣惟例貢吏役局於流品限於資格其間
能自奮立者百之一二耳彼方以上之人
槩無甄別而絕意於進取也是以廉耻不
立簠簋不飾甚則奴隸而呵斥之者有矣
===
請自今以往不以流品爲高下而以賢否
爲低昻拔吏役之稱職者躋之例貢之上
拔例貢之稱職者列之科目之間如是則
資格定而官方得人矣夫此固非紛更變
法也四者之中惟制科非
祖宗之法耳然所謂制科者非廢科目也謂與
科目並行也乃若辟薦之典師儒之重資
格之議則
先朝有故事矣
punctuated: 禮待之必優。教授則以進士爲之，學正、教諭則以舉人爲之，訓導則以貢士爲之。其稱職者則稍加優異，不次超遷。如是則師儒重而人才衆盛矣。今之所謂資格者，科目也，例貢也，吏役也。科目正途，其重也久矣。惟例貢、吏役局於流品，限於資格，其間能自奮立者百之一二耳。彼方以上之人槩無甄別，而絕意於進取也是以廉耻不立，簠簋不飾，甚則奴隸而呵斥之者有矣。請自今以往，不以流品爲高下，而以賢否爲低昻。拔吏役之稱職者，躋之例貢之上；拔例貢之稱職者，列之科目之間。如是則資格定而官方得人矣。夫此固非紛更變法也。四者之中，惟制科非祖宗之法耳。然所謂制科者，非廢科目也，謂與科目並行也。乃若辟薦之典、師儒之重、資格之議，則先朝有故事矣。
translation_en:
…and they must be accorded generous ceremonial treatment. Prefectural school instructors should be metropolitan graduates (jinshi); department and county school instructors should be provincial graduates (juren); and assistant instructors should be tribute students. Those who discharge their duties well should receive additional marks of favor and promotion beyond the normal order. In this way, teachers will be held in esteem, and talented men will flourish in abundance.

What are now called qualifications for office derive from the examination route, tribute admission under prescribed regulations, and service as clerks or runners. The examinations are the regular path, and their importance has long been recognized. Those entering through regulated tribute admission or clerical service, however, are confined by their category of entry and restricted by qualification requirements. Among them, only one or two in a hundred can rouse themselves to establish their worth. Seeing that their superiors make no distinctions among them, they abandon all thought of advancement. Consequently, they fail to cultivate integrity and shame and are guilty of official impropriety—literally, of leaving the sacrificial vessels unadorned. Matters even reach the point where they are treated as slaves and shouted at.

I ask that henceforth rank be determined by worthiness rather than category of entry. Elevate those clerks and runners who discharge their duties well above men admitted through regulated tribute admission; elevate deserving men from the latter group to stand among those who entered through the examinations. In this way, qualifications for office will be properly settled, and government offices will obtain suitable men.

These proposals certainly do not amount to indiscriminate alteration of established institutions. Of the four measures, only special examinations fall outside the institutions of our imperial ancestors. Yet by special examinations I do not mean abolishing the regular examinations; I mean conducting them alongside the regular examinations. As for the practice of recruitment by invitation and recommendation, the esteem accorded teachers, and the reconsideration of qualifications for office, there are precedents from earlier reigns.

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
國初如宋濂如劉基非辟召之尤者乎如宋
訥如胡儼非師儒之著者乎乃若以吏役
至卿佐者如楊時習況鍾之徒不可悉數
孰謂其不足以得人乎夫重師儒則養之
豫矣開制科則求之廣矣舉辟薦則擇之
精矣議資格則任之專矣率是以鼓舞中
才奔走豪傑而又加之以綜核之實吾見
今日之人才雖躋之三代可也而何漢唐
宋之云哉夫所謂綜核者非督責之謂也
===
循名以求其實稽事以考其成旌別以興
其恥黜陟以作其懦敦本實而抑浮華獎
直節而察顯譽凡所謂疑心而任耳目者
一切不行而必以至公至明臨之務使上
下相安莫有因循苟且之意如是則雖不
舉制科可也不行辟薦可也不重師儒可
也不議資格可也而人才自異矣不此之
務而徒紛更於法制之間是不琢玉而求
文采也亦何益之有哉吾固曰不患其不
punctuated: 國初，如宋濂，如劉基，非辟召之尤者乎？如宋訥，如胡儼，非師儒之著者乎？乃若以吏役至卿佐者，如楊時習、況鍾之徒，不可悉數，孰謂其不足以得人乎？夫重師儒則養之豫矣，開制科則求之廣矣，舉辟薦則擇之精矣，議資格則任之專矣。率是以鼓舞中才，奔走豪傑，而又加之以綜核之實，吾見今日之人才，雖躋之三代可也，而何漢唐宋之云哉！夫所謂綜核者，非督責之謂也。循名以求其實，稽事以考其成，旌別以興其恥，黜陟以作其懦，敦本實而抑浮華，獎直節而察顯譽。凡所謂疑心而任耳目者，一切不行，而必以至公至明臨之，務使上下相安，莫有因循苟且之意。如是，則雖不舉制科可也，不行辟薦可也，不重師儒可也，不議資格可也，而人才自異矣。不此之務，而徒紛更於法制之間，是不琢玉而求文采也，亦何益之有哉！吾固曰：不患其不
translation_en:
At the founding of the dynasty, were not men such as Song Lian and Liu Ji outstanding examples of recruitment by summons? Were not men such as Song Ne and Hu Yan distinguished scholarly teachers? As for those who rose from clerical service to high ministerial office, men such as Yang Shixi and Kuang Zhong are too numerous to enumerate. Who could say that these methods were inadequate for obtaining capable men? Honoring scholarly teachers ensures that talent is nurtured in advance; instituting special examinations broadens the search; promoting recruitment by invitation and recommendation makes selection more discerning; and reconsidering qualifications for appointment ensures dedicated service. By these means, men of middling ability can be encouraged and outstanding men brought into active service. If substantive, comprehensive scrutiny is added, I believe that the talented men of today could rank alongside those of the Three Dynasties. Why speak merely of the Han, Tang, and Song? What I call comprehensive scrutiny does not mean coercive supervision and demands.

It means seeking actual performance corresponding to nominal responsibilities, examining undertakings to assess their accomplishment, distinguishing the worthy to awaken a sense of shame, and using demotion and promotion to rouse the timid. It means fostering substance and suppressing superficial display, rewarding upright integrity and scrutinizing conspicuous reputations. All practices of harboring suspicions and relying on the reports of one's eyes and ears must be abandoned. Officials must instead be overseen with the utmost impartiality and discernment, so that superiors and subordinates are at ease with one another and none entertains an inclination toward habitual neglect or expedient half-measures. If this is done, it would be possible even to dispense with special examinations, recruitment by invitation and recommendation, particular emphasis on scholarly teachers, and deliberation over qualifications for appointment: the quality of talented men would improve of itself. To neglect this task and merely keep altering laws and institutions is to seek the patterned beauty of jade without carving it. What benefit could that bring? Thus I have maintained: one should not worry that they are not…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
足用而患乎用之不得其道也
第四問
胡經
同考試官教諭李　批〔弭災致變要在脩德而已吾子惓惓致重於此其亦知要者耶〕
考試官主事袁　批〔說天心仁愛之意甚懇切〕
考試官主事蕭　批〔意婉而文亦順叙可謂善言天矣〕
災異之來可憂也亦可喜也何也乖氣致
===
戾和氣致祥災異之來固未有無因而至
者如之何其勿憂也然天之所以告戒乎
我者容詎知其非仁愛乎我也哉知此則
可憂者未必不可喜而所以反災爲祥者
固有在人而不在天者矣彼以災異爲不
足憂者固不足責而惑於氣數拘於事應
者亦豈足以知天人相與之際哉執事有
感於今日之災異而以消弭之術下詢承
學愚也何足以知之姑舉其所知者以對
punctuated:
足用，而患乎用之不得其道也。

第四問
胡經
同考試官教諭李，批〔弭災致變，要在脩德而已。吾子惓惓致重於此，其亦知要者耶？〕
考試官主事袁，批〔說天心仁愛之意甚懇切。〕
考試官主事蕭，批〔意婉而文亦順叙，可謂善言天矣。〕

災異之來，可憂也，亦可喜也。何也？乖氣致戾，和氣致祥。災異之來，固未有無因而至者，如之何其勿憂也？然天之所以告戒乎我者，容詎知其非仁愛乎我也哉？知此，則可憂者未必不可喜，而所以反災爲祥者，固有在人而不在天者矣。彼以災異爲不足憂者，固不足責，而惑於氣數、拘於事應者，亦豈足以知天人相與之際哉？執事有感於今日之災異，而以消弭之術下詢承學，愚也何足以知之？姑舉其所知者以對。
translation_en:
…adequate for service; rather, the concern is that they are not employed in the proper way.

Fourth Question
Hu Jing 胡經

Associate Examiner Li 李, Instructor, comments: 〔The essential means of averting disasters and bringing about change [?] lies solely in cultivating virtue. You repeatedly place great emphasis on this: surely you understand what is essential?〕
Examiner Yuan 袁, Secretary, comments: 〔His explanation of Heaven’s benevolent and loving intent is deeply earnest.〕
Examiner Xiao 蕭, Secretary, comments: 〔The thought is tactfully expressed, and the writing proceeds smoothly and coherently. He may be said to speak well of Heaven.〕

The coming of disasters and anomalies is cause for concern, but also cause for joy. Why? Discordant vital energies bring calamity; harmonious vital energies bring auspicious signs. Disasters and anomalies never arrive without a cause. How, then, could we remain unconcerned? Yet how can we know that Heaven’s warnings to us are not expressions of its benevolence and love toward us? Once we understand this, what causes concern need not be incapable of bringing joy. The means of turning disaster into good fortune assuredly lies with human beings, rather than with Heaven. Those who consider disasters and anomalies unworthy of concern are hardly worth reproaching. But those who are misled by the cycles of vital energy and fate, or constrained by correspondences between events and portents, likewise cannot understand the workings of the relationship between Heaven and humanity.

Moved by the disasters and anomalies of the present day, you have graciously asked us students about the means of dispelling them. How could someone as ignorant as I be qualified to understand this? Nevertheless, I shall offer what I know in reply.

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
昔者楚莊王以國無災異禱於山川曰此
天忘我而孔子之作春秋也如日食不雨
星隕大水之類皆存而弗削至祥瑞則削
而弗錄此其意可想也是以有天下者不
取必於或然之數而求盡夫當然之道不
求之天而求之人憂勤惕厲恐懼脩省曷
嘗敢一毫放肆也哉夫脩玄德而祥桑枯
死此殷大戊之可稱者也發善言而熒惑
退舍此宋景公之可錄者也豈惟二君爲
===
然堯嘗有九年之水矣而拳拳於四岳之
咨則堯之所以事天者何如也湯嘗有七
年之旱矣而懇懇於六事之責則湯之所
以事天者何如也吾獨惜夫董仲舒之善
言天人而猶惑於氣數也觀其火災之對
述春秋兩觀亳社桓僖二宮之災以証高
園便殿之失其用意非不深且切也但拘
於某事應某事則其義迂矣其後淮南衡
山之獄株連蔓引得非仲舒啓之歟乃若
punctuated: 昔者楚莊王以國無災異，禱於山川曰：「此天忘我。」而孔子之作《春秋》也，如日食、不雨、星隕、大水之類，皆存而弗削；至祥瑞，則削而弗錄。此其意可想也。是以有天下者，不取必於或然之數，而求盡夫當然之道；不求之天，而求之人，憂勤惕厲，恐懼脩省，曷嘗敢一毫放肆也哉？夫脩玄德而祥桑枯死，此殷大戊之可稱者也；發善言而熒惑退舍，此宋景公之可錄者也。豈惟二君爲然？堯嘗有九年之水矣，而拳拳於四岳之咨，則堯之所以事天者何如也？湯嘗有七年之旱矣，而懇懇於六事之責，則湯之所以事天者何如也？吾獨惜夫董仲舒之善言天人，而猶惑於氣數也。觀其火災之對，述《春秋》兩觀、亳社、桓僖二宮之災，以証高園便殿之失，其用意非不深且切也。但拘於某事應某事，則其義迂矣。其後淮南、衡山之獄，株連蔓引，得非仲舒啓之歟？乃若
translation_en:
Formerly, King Zhuang of Chu, because his state had suffered no calamities or anomalies, prayed to the mountains and rivers, saying, “This means that Heaven has forgotten me.” When Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals, he retained without deletion such events as solar eclipses, failures of rain, falling stars, and great floods; auspicious portents, however, he deleted and did not record. His intention in this can be understood. Thus, those who rule All under Heaven do not seek certainty in contingent workings of fate, but strive to fulfill the Way that ought to be followed. They seek the remedy not in Heaven but in human affairs. Anxious and diligent, vigilant and wary, fearful and engaged in self-cultivation and examination, how could they ever dare indulge themselves in the slightest?

By cultivating hidden virtue, Tai Wu of Yin caused the portentous mulberry tree to wither and die: this is what deserves praise in him. By uttering good words, Duke Jing of Song caused Mars to retreat from its celestial lodge: this is what deserves recording in him. But were these two rulers alone in acting thus? Yao experienced nine years of flooding, yet earnestly sought counsel from the Four Chiefs. What does this show about how Yao served Heaven? Tang experienced seven years of drought, yet sincerely reproached himself over six possible failings. What does this show about how Tang served Heaven?

I regret only that Dong Zhongshu, though skilled in discussing Heaven and humanity, was still misled by notions of cosmic forces and fate. Consider his response concerning the fire: he recounted the fires recorded in the Spring and Autumn Annals at the two gate towers, the altar of Bo, and the two ancestral temples of Dukes Huan and Xi, using them to demonstrate the faults associated with the subsidiary hall in Emperor Gao’s mausoleum park. His purpose was certainly profound and pertinent. But by insisting that a particular event corresponded to another particular event, he made his interpretation strained. In the subsequent criminal cases involving Huainan and Hengshan, implication spread from one person to another in ever-widening circles. Could it not have been Zhongshu who opened the way to this? As for…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
宣帝之厲精圖治而史臣之紀災異獨爲
最詳者盖深有取夫宣帝之綜核名實克
謹天戒以爲災異雖多固無害其中興之
治也然而中韓雜用刑名繩下卒之啓三
大釁者得非宣帝之過歟今
聖天子敬
天法祖親賢遠奸固宜其休徵滋至而災異滅
息矣夫何邇年以來旱澇則不時矣風霾
則屢作矣日食地震星殞火災亦既相仍
===
矣是豈乖氣之相感歟盖天之仁愛我
君其意固有攸在而執事必欲求夫弭災救變
之術則竊有説焉夫徧走羣望此礫穰之
末節耳戒飭百工此粉飾之虛文耳反災
爲祥之術果在是乎昔宋儒真德秀有言
祥多而自恃者未必不危異衆而知懼者
未必不安顧人主所以應之者何如耳然
則洪範庶徵之説月令五行之應其今日
之所當致意者乎乃若開言路以來諫諍
punctuated:
宣帝之厲精圖治，而史臣之紀災異獨爲最詳者，盖深有取夫宣帝之綜核名實、克謹天戒，以爲災異雖多，固無害其中興之治也。然而中韓雜用，刑名繩下，卒之啓三大釁者，得非宣帝之過歟？
今聖天子敬天法祖，親賢遠奸，固宜其休徵滋至，而災異滅息矣。夫何邇年以來，旱澇則不時矣，風霾則屢作矣，日食、地震、星殞、火災亦既相仍矣？是豈乖氣之相感歟？盖天之仁愛我君，其意固有攸在。而執事必欲求夫弭災救變之術，則竊有説焉。夫徧走羣望，此礫穰之末節耳；戒飭百工，此粉飾之虛文耳。反災爲祥之術，果在是乎？昔宋儒真德秀有言：「祥多而自恃者，未必不危；異衆而知懼者，未必不安。顧人主所以應之者何如耳。」然則《洪範》庶徵之説、《月令》五行之應，其今日之所當致意者乎？乃若開言路以來諫諍，
translation_en:
…As for Emperor Xuan’s strenuous efforts to govern well, the court historians recorded disasters and anomalies during his reign in exceptional detail because they deeply valued his thorough scrutiny of names and actual performance and his conscientious heed to Heaven’s warnings. They considered that, numerous though the disasters and anomalies were, these did not detract from the restorative achievements of his government. Yet he employed the teachings of Zhong and Han [?; probably Shen Buhai and Han Fei] together and held his subordinates to the strictures of penal and administrative methods. This ultimately opened the way to three great calamities: was this not Emperor Xuan’s fault?
Our sage Son of Heaven now reveres Heaven and follows his ancestors’ example, draws close to worthy men and keeps the wicked at a distance. Auspicious signs should surely arrive in increasing abundance, and disasters and anomalies should cease. Why, then, in recent years have droughts and floods occurred out of season, violent winds and dust haze arisen repeatedly, and solar eclipses, earthquakes, falling stars, and fires followed one another? Could this be a mutual response among discordant vital forces? Heaven surely has a purpose in its benevolent love for our sovereign. Since you, sir, insist on seeking methods to avert disasters and remedy abnormal occurrences, I venture to offer an explanation.
Rushing everywhere to the various sites of sacrifice is merely a minor detail of rites for averting misfortune [?]; issuing admonitions to the officials is merely empty ceremony that embellishes appearances. Do the methods for turning disaster into good fortune really lie in these things? The Song Confucian scholar Zhen Dexiu once said: “Those who become complacent because auspicious signs are plentiful are not necessarily free from danger; those who know fear because anomalies are numerous are not necessarily denied security. It depends solely on how the ruler responds to them.” Should we not, then, attend today to the account of the various signs in the “Great Plan” and the correspondences of the Five Phases in the “Monthly Ordinances”? As for opening channels of speech to invite remonstrance…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
端士風以抑僥倖清吏源以去冗濫慎民
牧以求循良干政者黜之失律者誅之幽
滯者揚之放逐者錄之則又當今之所不
可闕者執是以求弭災救變之術思過半
矣杞人之憂不自知其蹤謬故敢為執事
者陳之乃若
聖君賢相之所以格天者則自有道固非狂瞽
之所能窺測其萬一也
第五問
===
王朝良
同考試官訓導嚴　批　說時事甚整切末復歸重於得人此誠不易之論也
同考試官訓導陳　批　文有頓挫而處置甚詳必非迂儒可到
考試官主事袁　批　憂深言切子其識時務者歟
考試官主事蕭　批　時務條悉無遺可與論天下事矣
天下之事在於審勢達變而已矣因勢以
punctuated:
端士風以抑僥倖，清吏源以去冗濫，慎民牧以求循良。干政者黜之，失律者誅之，幽滯者揚之，放逐者錄之，則又當今之所不可闕者。執是以求弭災救變之術，思過半矣。杞人之憂，不自知其蹤謬，故敢為執事者陳之。乃若聖君賢相之所以格天者，則自有道，固非狂瞽之所能窺測其萬一也。

第五問

王朝良

同考試官訓導嚴批：說時事甚整切，末復歸重於得人，此誠不易之論也。

同考試官訓導陳批：文有頓挫，而處置甚詳，必非迂儒可到。

考試官主事袁批：憂深言切，子其識時務者歟？

考試官主事蕭批：時務條悉無遺，可與論天下事矣。

天下之事，在於審勢達變而已矣。因勢以
translation_en:
…rectify the conduct of scholars to curb opportunistic advancement; purify the sources of official recruitment to eliminate superfluous and unqualified appointees; and select those who shepherd the people carefully, seeking conscientious and capable officials. Dismiss those who interfere in government; execute those who violate military discipline; promote those left languishing in obscurity; and restore to consideration those dismissed or banished. These, too, are indispensable measures at present. By pursuing these measures in seeking ways to quell disasters and remedy calamities, one will already have grasped more than half the matter. Like the man of Qi who feared that the sky would fall, I am unaware of the absurdity of my own apprehensions [?]; nevertheless, I venture to set them before you. As for the means by which our sagely ruler and worthy ministers move Heaven, they have their own Way, of which a rash and benighted person such as myself cannot discern even the smallest fraction.

Fifth Question

Wang Chaoliang

Comment by Associate Examiner Yan, Assistant Instructor: His discussion of current affairs is very orderly and pertinent. At the end he returns to the importance of obtaining the right men. This is indeed an argument that cannot be gainsaid.

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Assistant Instructor: The writing has rhythmic pauses and turns, and the proposed measures are very detailed. This is certainly beyond the reach of a pedantic scholar.

Comment by Examiner Yuan, Secretary: Your concern is deep and your words urgent. Are you not one who understands the affairs of the times?

Comment by Examiner Xiao, Secretary: His treatment of current affairs is systematic and thorough, omitting nothing. He is someone with whom one can discuss the affairs of the realm.

The affairs of the realm depend simply upon assessing circumstances and understanding change. By following the prevailing circumstances in order to…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
通變隨變以從宜則天下之事殆無不可
爲者矣書曰有備無患此言防之於未然
也易曰繻有衣袽終日戒此言救之於已
然也今河南之事其未然者無復可圖矣
其已然者寧可坐視其弊而不爲之所乎
黃河爲害遷徙不常漕渠淤塞矣頃者動
三省之民以疏之而塞者如故意者未究
乎治水之道歟水之性分之則衰順之則
安爲今日之計莫若疏金龍口以通北鎮
===
之門户疏丁家道口以通徐吕之咽喉孫
家渡可疏也則朱仙鎮之故道通而河勢
漸分矣趙皮寨可疏也則黃陵岡之下流
通而水怒少殺矣又必濬渦河以通宿遷
濬白河以通中牟導其下流決其壅滯隄
築之必固蓄洩之以時而得人則如夏忠
靖之理江淮陳恭襄之閘通濟任之專而
不惑於浮議行之漸而不急夫近功如是
則漕渠其可通矣否則勞民傷財如之何
punctuated:
通變，隨變以從宜，則天下之事殆無不可爲者矣。《書》曰：「有備無患。」此言防之於未然也。《易》曰：「繻有衣袽，終日戒。」此言救之於已然也。今河南之事，其未然者無復可圖矣；其已然者，寧可坐視其弊而不爲之所乎？
黃河爲害，遷徙不常，漕渠淤塞矣。頃者動三省之民以疏之，而塞者如故，意者未究乎治水之道歟？水之性，分之則衰，順之則安。爲今日之計，莫若疏金龍口以通北鎮之門户，疏丁家道口以通徐吕之咽喉。孫家渡可疏也，則朱仙鎮之故道通，而河勢漸分矣；趙皮寨可疏也，則黃陵岡之下流通，而水怒少殺矣。又必濬渦河以通宿遷，濬白河以通中牟，導其下流，決其壅滯，隄築之必固，蓄洩之以時。而得人，則如夏忠靖之理江淮、陳恭襄之閘通濟，任之專而不惑於浮議，行之漸而不急夫近功。如是，則漕渠其可通矣；否則，勞民傷財，如之何
translation_en:
…to adapt to change, and respond to changing circumstances with appropriate measures: then scarcely any affair in the realm would be impossible to accomplish. The Book of Documents says, “With preparation, there is no calamity.” This speaks of prevention before trouble arises. The Book of Changes says, “For a leaking boat, have rags ready; remain watchful all day.” [?] This speaks of remedying trouble after it has arisen. In Henan’s present affairs, there is no longer any opportunity to plan before trouble arises. Now that it has arisen, can we simply sit by and watch its harmful effects without devising a remedy?
The Yellow River causes harm, shifting its course unpredictably, and the grain-transport canals have silted up. Recently, people from three provinces were mobilized to dredge them, yet the obstructions remain as before. Perhaps the principles of controlling water have not been fully investigated? Water’s nature is such that dividing its flow diminishes its force, while following its natural course makes it peaceful. For present purposes, nothing would be better than dredging Jinlongkou to open the gateway to Beizhen, and dredging Dingjia Daokou to open the vital passage through Xu and Lü. If Sunjiadu can be dredged, the old channel at Zhuxianzhen will be opened, and the river’s force will gradually be divided. If Zhaopizhai can be dredged, the downstream channel at Huanglinggang will be opened, and the water’s fury will be somewhat diminished. We must also dredge the Guo River to open passage to Suqian, and dredge the Bai River to open passage to Zhongmou, guiding their downstream flow and clearing their blockages. Embankments must be solidly built, and water retained or released at the proper times. As for securing the right men, there are the examples of Xia Zhongjing’s management of the Jiang and Huai waterways and Chen Gongxiang’s construction of sluices at Tongji. Give such men undivided responsibility, without being swayed by idle criticism; carry out the work gradually, without pressing for immediate results. In this way, the grain-transport canals can be opened. Otherwise, exhausting the people and wasting resources, how could …

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
其有成功邪潞賊恃險干逆天紀勢甚猖
獗矣茲者連二省之兵以剿之而叛者亦
寧意者未盡夫用兵之道歟用兵之道動
靜相時翕張視勢爲今之計莫若塞壺關
之口以遏其奔衝據林邑之險以防其出
沒禁旅可用也分番迭肆則彼之精鋭羈
矣土兵可用也堅壁清野則彼之樵采絶
矣又必用鄉導以察其險易懸重賞以疑
其腹心脅從者不問投降者不誅攻其所
===
不救掩其所不備而選將則如充國之坐
制先零李愬之雪夜破蔡假以節鉞而無
中制之憂錄其功賞而嚴失律之罰如是
則小醜其可殄矣否則覆軍殺將如之何
其不旰食邪亢旱爲虐麥禾不收民之憔
悴甚矣又加之蝗蝻兩河南北赤地千里
茲欲處之亦惟爲守令者布寬恤之恩罷
督責之令踏勘必實先期
奏聞或蠲夏稅之太半或蠲秋糧之什七又
punctuated:
其有成功邪？潞賊恃險，干逆天紀，勢甚猖獗矣。茲者連二省之兵以剿之，而叛者亦寧，意者未盡夫用兵之道歟？用兵之道，動靜相時，翕張視勢。爲今之計，莫若塞壺關之口以遏其奔衝，據林邑之險以防其出沒。禁旅可用也，分番迭肆，則彼之精鋭羈矣；土兵可用也，堅壁清野，則彼之樵采絶矣。又必用鄉導以察其險易，懸重賞以疑其腹心，脅從者不問，投降者不誅，攻其所不救，掩其所不備。而選將則如充國之坐制先零、李愬之雪夜破蔡，假以節鉞而無中制之憂，錄其功賞而嚴失律之罰。如是，則小醜其可殄矣；否則覆軍殺將，如之何其不旰食邪？
亢旱爲虐，麥禾不收，民之憔悴甚矣。又加之蝗蝻，兩河南北，赤地千里。茲欲處之，亦惟爲守令者布寬恤之恩，罷督責之令，踏勘必實，先期奏聞，或蠲夏稅之太半，或蠲秋糧之什七，又
translation_en:
…how could it succeed? The rebels of Lu rely on difficult terrain and defy Heaven’s order; their power has grown rampant. Recently, troops from two provinces have been combined to suppress them, yet the rebels remain at ease [?]. Might this be because the principles of warfare have not been fully applied? In warfare, movement and stillness must accord with the moment, and contraction and expansion with the situation. The best plan now is to block the entrance to Huguan to check their rushes, and occupy the strategic terrain of Linyi to prevent their movements in and out. The imperial guard troops can be employed: let them attack in successive rotations, and the rebels’ elite forces will be tied down. Local troops can be employed: let them strengthen their defenses and clear the countryside of supplies, and the rebels’ access to firewood and provisions will be cut off. Local guides must also be employed to ascertain which terrain is difficult and which accessible; substantial rewards must be offered to sow suspicion among their trusted followers. Those coerced into joining them should not be called to account, and those who surrender should not be executed. Attack where they cannot bring relief, and strike where they are unprepared. In choosing commanders, seek men like Chongguo, who subdued the Xianling through holding his position, or Li Su, who captured Cai on a snowy night. Grant them the tally and battle-axe of command, freeing them from concern about interference from the court; record their achievements and reward them, while strictly punishing breaches of military discipline. In this way, these petty villains can be exterminated. Otherwise, armies will be destroyed and commanders killed: how could Your Majesty avoid delaying your meals in anxiety?
Severe drought has wrought havoc; wheat and other grain crops have failed, and the people are utterly worn down. On top of this have come locusts and their nymphs: north and south of the Yellow River [?], the land lies bare for a thousand li. To deal with this now, prefects and county magistrates must extend benevolent leniency and relief, and rescind orders pressing for payment. Their inspections in the field must establish the facts, and they must memorialize the throne in advance, seeking perhaps remission of more than half the summer tax or seven-tenths of the autumn grain levy; furthermore…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
必發倉以賑之移粟以撫之凡可以恤民
隱者力爲之圖如富弼之在青州趙閱道
之在浙西則民沾實惠而雲漢之什可無
作矣徭役太煩勞者不息民之疲敝久矣
又加之以征調十室九空朝夕不保茲欲
救之亦惟爲守令者禁額外之誅求罷不
急之營繕撙節有方稍加存恤開河之役
暫停勦賊之兵不出又必視户之上下均
其賦稅量丁之多寡節其庸調凡可以拯
===
民窮者曲爲之處如陽城之撫字如黄霸
之愛養則民獲安息而鴻鴈之苦庶有瘳
矣雖然治河有説矣而轉般之法亦不可
不預講也弭盜有方矣而安輯之計亦不
可不先圖也旱蝗可憂而長平義倉之設
其亦有可采歟徭役可閔而差役免役之
法其亦有可做歟凡此四者皆目前之急
務謂如拯溺救焚之不暇者而審勢達變
愚則西存乎其人也若曰坐而論天下之
punctuated:
必發倉以賑之，移粟以撫之。凡可以恤民隱者，力爲之圖。如富弼之在青州、趙閱道之在浙西，則民沾實惠，而《雲漢》之什可無作矣。徭役太煩，勞者不息，民之疲敝久矣。又加之以征調，十室九空，朝夕不保。茲欲救之，亦惟爲守令者禁額外之誅求，罷不急之營繕，撙節有方，稍加存恤。開河之役暫停，勦賊之兵不出。又必視户之上下，均其賦稅；量丁之多寡，節其庸調。凡可以拯民窮者，曲爲之處。如陽城之撫字，如黄霸之愛養，則民獲安息，而《鴻鴈》之苦庶有瘳矣。
雖然，治河有説矣，而轉般之法亦不可不預講也；弭盜有方矣，而安輯之計亦不可不先圖也。旱蝗可憂，而長平義倉之設，其亦有可采歟？徭役可閔，而差役免役之法，其亦有可做歟？凡此四者，皆目前之急務，謂如拯溺救焚之不暇者。而審勢達變，愚則西存乎其人也。若曰坐而論天下之
translation_en:
…it is also essential to open the granaries to provide relief and transport grain to sustain the people. Every means of alleviating their suffering must be pursued with all one's strength. If officials act as Fu Bi did in Qingzhou and Zhao Yuedao did in western Zhejiang, the people will receive tangible benefits, and there will be no occasion to compose a poem like “The Milky Way” (Yunhan).
Labor service is excessively burdensome, and those who toil have no respite: the people have long been exhausted. Military levies have compounded this burden, leaving nine households out of ten empty and the people's survival uncertain from morning to evening. To rescue them now, prefects and magistrates must prohibit exactions beyond the prescribed quotas, suspend nonessential construction and repairs, practice economy methodically, and give them some care and relief. Canal excavation should be temporarily halted, and troops should not be sent out to suppress bandits. Moreover, taxes must be apportioned equitably according to households' relative means, and labor-service and commodity levies adjusted according to the number of adult males. Every possible means of rescuing the people from destitution must be carefully worked out. With nurturing care like that of Yang Cheng and loving support like that of Huang Ba, the people will obtain peace and rest, and the suffering described in “The Wild Geese” (Hongyan) may at last be relieved.
Nevertheless, although proposals for managing the river have been offered, methods of grain transshipment must also be discussed in advance; although ways to quell banditry have been identified, plans for pacification and resettlement must also be devised beforehand. Drought and locusts are cause for anxiety: might there be something worth adopting in the establishment of “changping” [?; probably “ever-normal”] and charitable granaries? Labor-service burdens merit compassion: might there be something practicable in the systems of assigned service and exemption from service? These four matters are all urgent tasks of the present, as pressing as rescuing the drowning or saving people from a fire, with no time to spare. Yet assessing circumstances and responding to change depend, in my humble view, on the right person [?]. If one says that to sit and discuss the affairs of the world…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
事也易進而處天下之事也難則執事可
以無問而愚也可以無對矣
punctuated: 事也易，進而處天下之事也難，則執事可以無問，而愚也可以無對矣。
translation_en: …the affairs of the realm are easy to discuss, but difficult to step forward and manage, then you, sir, need not have asked, and I, in my ignorance, need not have answered.

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄後序
袁奉
命校文河南道出燕趙涉衛趨大
梁降觀于郊野其土風往往
嗇而愿約而愉憂勤而寬舒
及試士其言亦多毅而不隘
直而不夸孫而不迫辨而中
===
其義核其慮詳雍容和平蓋
猶有先王之遺焉夫河洛故
都會而天地之中其書圖則
義禹之所則也禮樂則周公
之所制作也周之盛也其在
成康之際乎成王營雒以正
四方於時風俗和平賢才衆
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄後序

袁奉命校文河南，道出燕趙，涉衛，趨大梁，降觀于郊野。其土風往往嗇而愿，約而愉，憂勤而寬舒。及試士，其言亦多毅而不隘，直而不夸，孫而不迫，辨而中。其義核，其慮詳，雍容和平，蓋猶有先王之遺焉。夫河洛，故都會而天地之中，其書圖則義禹之所則也，禮樂則周公之所制作也。周之盛也，其在成康之際乎？成王營雒以正四方，於時風俗和平，賢才衆
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

I, Yuan, received orders to assess examination compositions in Henan. My route passed through Yan and Zhao, crossed Wei, and proceeded toward Daliang. I went down into the countryside to observe its conditions. Local customs were generally frugal yet sincere, restrained yet cheerful, industrious and mindful of hardship yet easygoing. When I examined the candidates, their writings, too, were often resolute without being narrow, straightforward without being boastful, modest without being constrained, and discriminating yet well judged. Their reasoning was sound and their deliberations thorough; their manner was composed and harmonious. Surely something of the legacy of the former kings still remained there.

The region of the Yellow and Luo rivers was an ancient metropolitan center and the center of Heaven and Earth. Its writings and diagrams were what Yi [?] and Yu took as their models; its rites and music were what the Duke of Zhou fashioned and established. Was not the flourishing age of Zhou the time of Kings Cheng and Kang? King Cheng built Luo to bring order to the four quarters. At that time, customs were harmonious and peaceful, and worthy, talented men were numerous…

title: 嘉靖七年河南鄉試錄
text:
密則璆也序之詳矣袠故略
馬
刑部福建清吏司主事袁袠
序
punctuated:
密則璆也序之詳矣，袠故略馬。

刑部福建清吏司主事袁袠序。
translation_en:
…As for the details [?], Qiu has set them out fully in his preface, so I, Zhi, keep this brief [?].

Preface by Yuan Zhi, Secretary in the Fujian Bureau of the Ministry of Justice.
